Call to Order 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of settler 
colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply connected 
to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their cultural ways of 
life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these Indigenous Nations 
maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and work as humble 
and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to learn about and 
educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous Nations whose land 
we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty in all the ways that 
we can.

Items Pulled from the Consent Calendar 

Constitutional Amendments 

Legislation on First Reading 
 
Bill #78-045 Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, Enock Nturubika 
 This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a 
 new Affiliated Project between SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law 
 advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-law 
 students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning 
 about the law, with the resources available from the SGA, Pre-law 
 advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
 governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 (Assigned to Judiciary, Finance, Internal Affairs, Student Life, 
 09.23.2026) (Passed Student Life, 09.24.2026) (Passed Internal 
 Affairs, 09.28.2026) (Passed Judiciary, Finance, 09.29.2026) (Referred to Finance, 09.30.2026) (Tabled in Finance, 10.06.2026, 
 10.13.2026, 10.20.2026) 

Bill #78-051 Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis, Tanner Bigenho 
 This bill will restructure vacant Senate seats to be placed on the 
 ballot when candidacy opens in an election, even if it is not the 
 correct semester for the seat to be placed on the ballot. This gives 
 the Student Body the ability to vote on more of their representation in 
 the Student Senate. (Assigned to Rules, Judiciary, 10.21.2026) 

Bill #78-052 Sponsored by James Tizon 
 A budget transfer in the amount of $30,485 from Activity And Service 
 (A And S) Fee Management And Reserve account to The Division of 
 Student Affairs Finance & Administration. This transfer will pay for the 
 Student Government Association’s use of the systems Municode and 
 CivicPlus. (Assigned to Finance, 10.21.2026) 

Bill #78-053 Sponsored by James Tizon 
 Amending Chapter 710.6, “Violations and Penalties,” of the Student 
 Body Statutes to specify the removal of only physical campaign 
 materials, allowing digital campaign materials to remain. (Assigned 
 to Judiciary, 10.21.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Hannah Finman 
#78-048 This resolution authorizes the use of the $2,000 allocated during the 
 spring semester to support FSU Cooperative Collections and its 
 ongoing efforts to improve student access to shared educational, 
 wellness, and recreational resources. It also encourages appropriate 
 recognition of the Student Government Association's financial 
 support and accountability for the use of the allocated 
 funds. (Assigned to Student Life, 10.21.2026) 

Bill #78-054 Sponsored by Hannah Finman 
 This bill authorizes a transfer of $1,476.85 through Senate Projects to 
 supplement the $2,000 previously allocated to FSU Cooperative 
 Collections, bringing the total available funding to $3,476.85. The 
 funds will support the proposed replenishment of the Wellness & 
 Recovery Library, expansion of the 3-Day Calculator Program, and 
 addition of recreational equipment to the Leisure Library. The 
 legislation also encourages appropriate SGA branding, recognition, 
 and accountability for the use of student-funded 
 resources. (Assigned to Student Life, Internal Affairs, Finance, 
 10.21.2026) 

Bill #78-055 Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, Dylan Gaynor 
 This legislation would provide $1,610 to the Transportation and 
 Parking Services to create and install 14 signs at areas around 
 campus, demarcating Legacy Walk and the sidewalks up “Mt. 
 Diffenbaugh” as dismount zones for e-bikes and e-scooters. The locations of the signs and design of the signs are in the attachments 
 sections. (Assigned to Student Life, Internal Affairs, Finance, 
 10.21.2026) 

Legislation on Second Reading 
 
Allocation Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, James Tizon 
Resolution This resolution proposes the allocation of $14,206.35 to seven RSOs 
#78-016 who requested funding from the RSOAC. (Placed on Second

 FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY STUDENT GOVERNMENT ASSOCIATION

 Location: Senate Chambers 
Call to Order

Pledge of Allegiance 
 
 Senator Dawkins reads the Pledge of Allegiance. 

Moment of Silent Reflection 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of settler 
colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply connected 
to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their cultural ways of 
life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these Indigenous Nations 
maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and work as humble 
and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to learn about and 
educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous Nations whose land 
we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty in all the ways that 
we can.

 This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a 
 new Affiliated Project between SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law 
 advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-law 
 students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning 
 about the law, with the resources available from the SGA, Pre-law 
 advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
 governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals.

 CivicPlus. (Assigned to Finance, 10.21.2026)

Resolution Sponsored by Hannah Finman 
#78-048 This resolution authorizes the use of the $2,000 allocated during the 
 spring semester to support FSU Cooperative Collections and its 
 ongoing efforts to improve student access to shared educational, 
 wellness, and recreational resources. It also encourages appropriate recognition of the Student Government Association's financial 
 support and accountability for the use of the allocated 
 funds. (Assigned to Student Life, 10.21.2026)

Bill #78-054 Sponsored by Hannah Finman 
 This bill authorizes a transfer of $1,476.85 through Senate Projects to 
 supplement the $2,000 previously allocated to FSU Cooperative 
 Collections, bringing the total available funding to $3,476.85. The 
 funds will support the proposed replenishment of the Wellness & 
 Recovery Library, expansion of the 3-Day Calculator Program, and

 legislation also encourages appropriate SGA branding, recognition, 
 and accountability for the use of student-funded 
 resources. (Assigned to Student Life, Internal Affairs, Finance, 
 10.21.2026) 
 
 ■ 
Bill #78-055 Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, Dylan Gaynor

 Parking Services to create and install 14 signs at areas around 
 campus, demarcating Legacy Walk and the sidewalks up “Mt. 
 Diffenbaugh” as dismount zones for e-bikes and e-scooters. The 
 locations of the signs and design of the signs are in the attachments 
 sections. (Assigned to Student Life, Internal Affairs, Finance, 
 10.21.2026)

sections.text:
THE SEVENTY-EIGHTH STUDENT SENATE 
 Calendar: October 7, 2026 
 Location: Senate Chambers 
 Time: 7:30 PM 
 Submit Public Comment Here 

 Call to Order 

 Pledge of Allegiance 

 Moment of Silent Reflection 
Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 

 Presentations and Awards 
 • Google Presentation 

 Public Comments from Students, RSOs, and Members of the Campus Community 

 Messages from SGA Entities 

 Report of Senate Officers 

 Report of Senate Liaisons

 • Candidates Forwarded from the SGA Executive Branch • Brayden Gable - Student Senate - Engineering Seat 3 (Assigned to 
 Rules, 10.07.2026) 

 • Benjamin Bernsteen - Student Senate - Engineering Seat 5 (Assigned to 
 Rules, 10.07.2026) 

 • Dana Olson - Student Senate - Business Seat 3 (Assigned to Rules, 
 10.07.2026) 

 • Steven Becker - Student Senate - Business Seat 9 (Assigned to Rules, 
 10.07.2026) 

 • Joshua Tulchinsky - Mental Health Council - Director of Finance 
 (Assigned to Finance, 10.07.2026) 

 Consent Calendar 
 • Corrections and Approval of Senate and Committee Minutes 

 • Remaining Balances (Attached) 

 Items Pulled from the Consent Calendar 

 Constitutional Amendments 

 Legislation on First Reading 
Bill #78-044 Sponsored by Collin Mungall, Riley Perantoni 
 This bill would amend Chapter 309 of the Student Body Statutes to 
 establish a structure for Student Government grant programs. It 
 would create the Textbook Grant Program and the Internship 
 Housing Grant Program to provide financial support for qualifying 
 student expenses. (Assigned to Judiciary, Finance, Student Life, 
 09.23.2026) (Passed Student Life 09.24.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 
 Finance, 09.29.2026) (Referred to Finance, 09.30.2026) (Tabled in 
 Finance, 10.06.2026) 

Bill #78-045 Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, Enock Nturubika 
 This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a 
 new Affiliated Project between SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law 
 advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-law 
 students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning 
 about the law, with the resources available from the SGA, Pre-law 
 advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
 governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 (Assigned to Judiciary, Finance, Internal Affairs, Student Life, 
 09.23.2026) (Passed Student Life, 09.24.2026) (Passed Internal 
 Affairs, 09.28.2026) (Passed Judiciary, Finance, 09.29.2026) 
 (Referred to Finance, 09.30.2026) (Tabled in Finance, 
 10.06.2026) Bill #78-048 Sponsored by Jayden Hidalgo, Riley Perantoni 
 This bill would amend Chapter 409, Student Body Statutes (“Senate 
 In The Sunshine”), to require the Student Body Treasurer to provide 
 the Student Senate with a monthly report of the remaining fund 
 balances in five accounts: the RSO Allocation Committee, the RSO 
 Development Fund, Senate Projects, the Campus Advancement and 
 Development Fund, and Executive Projects. It replaces the more 
 detailed reporting requirements of Senate Bill 034 with the 
 streamlined approach recommended by Andy Johnson, Program 
 Director of FSU Student Governance & Advocacy. (Assigned to 
 Judiciary, Finance, 09.30.2026) (Tabled in Judiciary, Finance, 
 10.06.2026) 

Bill #78-049 Sponsored by Liya Dereje, Riley Perantoni 
 This bill would amend Chapter 801 of the Student Body Statutes to 
 require entities receiving A&S funding to submit attendance 
 information for each event funded in whole or in part with A&S fees 
 within ten days of the event. The bill establishes multiple methods for 
 collecting attendance data, including FSU Card swipe data, QR code 
 check-ins, and paper sign-ins when technology failures 
 occur. (Assigned to Student Life, Judiciary, Finance, 09.30.2026) 
 (Tabled in Student Life, 10.01.2026) (Tabled in Judiciary, 
 Finance, 10.06.2026) 

Proclamation Sponsored by Sophia Kelbert 
#78-022 This proclamation recognizes and commends the Florida State 
 University Victim Advocate Program, Title IX Office, Counseling & 
 Psychological Services, University Health Services, Student Support 
 & Transitions, and other campus and community partners for their 
 continued work supporting students affected by sexual violence and 
 assault. The proclamation further encourages the Florida State 
 University community to promote a culture grounded in safety, 
 respect, consent, compassion, accountability, and meaningful 
 support for survivors. (Assigned to Student Life, 10.07.2026) 

Bill #78-050 Sponsored by Matthias Dominguez 
 This Legislation allocates $4,000 from the Senate Projects Account 
 to FSU Transportation & Parking Services (TAPS) for the fabrication 
 and installation of permanent sustainable commute signage at 
 campus parking garages. The signage will feature highly visible and 
 research-backed slogans to encourage students to utilize alternative 
 transit options such as walking, biking, riding, or Nole 
 Transit. (Assigned to Student Life, Internal Affairs, Finance, 
 10.07.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Matthias Dominguez 
#78-047 This Legislation allocates $4,000 from the Senate Projects Account 
 to FSU Transportation & Parking Services (TAPS) for the fabrication 
 and installation of permanent sustainable commute signage at campus parking garages. The signage will feature highly visible and 
 research-backed slogans to encourage students to utilize alternative 
 transit options such as walking, biking, riding, or Nole Transit. 
 (Assigned to Student Life, 10.07.2026) 

Proclamation Sponsored by Hannah Finman, Kayra Serpenguzel 
#78-023 This proclamation recognizes Florida State University’s 175th 
 anniversary and celebrates the historical contributions of the Student 
 Government Association to the university community. It honors the 
 generations of student leaders who have advocated for the student 
 body, strengthened student representation, and contributed to the 
 university’s growth and development. (Assigned to Student Life, 
 10.07.2026) 

 Legislation on Second Reading 
Allocation Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, James Tizon 
Resolution This resolution proposes the allocation of $3,418.50 to two RSOs 
#78-014 who requested funding from the RSOAC. (Placed on Second 
 Reading by Senate President pursuant to SBS § 812.5(d), 
 10.07.2026) 

Bill #78-047 Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis 
 Amends Section 405 of Student Body Statutes relating to 
 impeachment procedure to implement safeguards to our current 
 process, and clarify the Judiciary Committee’s role in the process. In 
 addition, clarifies the appeal process and how suspension of an 
 official works while they are undergoing the impeachment process. 
 (Assigned to Judiciary, 09.30.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 
 10.06.2026) 

Proclamation Sponsored by Calleigh Bellmany, Kayra Serpenguzel 
#78-021 This proclamation formally recognizes the month of October as 
 National Breast Cancer Awareness Month, with the intention of 
 bringing awareness to all those impacted in our Florida State 
 University community by breast cancer. It presents facts and history 
 on this topic, reiterates the importance of early detection, and 
 recognizes the work of those who are conducting research to combat 
 breast cancer. (Assigned to Student Life, 09.30.2026) (Passed 
 Student Life, 10.01.2026) 

 New Business 

 Closing Announcements 

 Advisor Announcements 

 Final Roll Call and Adjournment

Short Title: Reforming Executive Misconduct Oversight Values and Ethics (REMOVE) Act 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
Amends Section 405 of Student Body Statutes relating to impeachment procedure to 
implement safeguards to our current process, and clarify the Judiciary Committee’s role in the 
process. In addition, clarifies the appeal process and how suspension of an official works while 
they are undergoing the impeachment process. 
 
Background Information: 
 While looking through Section 405, it was noticed that under the current process, students could 
file impeachment charges that were falsified with little to no evidence, and the Committee would still 
have to hear them as though they were true and call the accused officer into a hearing. It was then 
decided that additional safeguards, such as a preliminary hearing with the accuser arguing their case 
that the accused doesn’t have to attend, could positively benefit our current system. 
 In addition, upon looking at SGA Statutes from other public Florida universities, our Statutes 
lacked a clear procedure that would be uniformly used for all hearings, so it was also decided that 
adding in a clear process could also streamline the hearing process. Along with this, the hearing 
process that we use didn’t reflect what other universities use and find success with, so it was decided 
that by making the appeal process optional it could potentially mitigate unnecessary cases for the 
Student Supreme Court if there is a clear preponderance of evidence. 

Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
This legislation was originally brainstormed and drafted with current and former Senator input, before 
being looked over by Senate leadership to assure that the language was clear and the process was 
acceptable. After this, it was reviewed by Student Governance & Advocacy, who provided input about 
the length of how long opening and closing statements should be, as well as some advice relating to 
the appeal process and the preliminary hearing. Finally, a final draft was sent to both the Student 
Supreme Court Chief Justice and Attorney General for review, to ensure that all branches of SGA were 
aware of potential changes and to receive any relevant feedback. Both of these branches found no 
issue with the proposed legislation, with the Chief Justice choosing to defer to the Attorney General’s 
opinion, and the Attorney General approving the bill without proposed change. 

 Page 7 of 25Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
 If this bill were to be enrolled, it would create a clear process for impeachment: after articles are 
filed against an officer, the individual who filed the articles must appear in front of the Judiciary 
Committee with their evidence to argue the validity of their claim. If the Judiciary Committee proves the 
validity of the claim, the accused officer then must appear in front of the Judiciary Committee to defend 
themselves, and then the Committee votes on whether the case should be forwarded to the Student 
Senate as a whole, and if the Senate votes to impeach the officer, that individual then has the option to 
appeal to the Student Supreme Court, the VPSA, or accept the vote and vacate their office. 
 If the preliminary charges are accepted, the accused officer is suspended until the case is 
finished being considered by the Senate; if they continue the appeal process their suspension will also 
continue. Suspension includes the restriction of making official actions within that position, as well as 
suspension of OPS wages.

Short Title: An Act Amending Chapter 409, Student Body Statutes, to Require the Student 
Body Treasurer to Provide Monthly Fund Balance Reports to the Student Senate. 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 409, Student Body Statutes (“Senate In The Sunshine”), to require the 
Student Body Treasurer to provide the Student Senate with a monthly report of the remaining fund 
balances in five accounts: the RSO Allocation Committee, the RSO Development Fund, Senate 
Projects, the Campus Advancement and Development Fund, and Executive Projects. It replaces the 
more detailed reporting requirements of Senate Bill 034 with the streamlined approach recommended 
by Andy Johnson, Program Director of FSU Student Governance & Advocacy. 
 
Background Information: 
Senate Bill 034 sought to establish monthly financial reporting requirements for Senate-controlled 
accounts under Chapter 409. The bill passed the Student Senate but was subsequently vetoed. 
Because Senate Bill 034 already exists as an enrolled bill, Andy Johnson, Program Director of FSU 
Student Governance & Advocacy, advised that a new bill be introduced rather than a motion to 
reconsider. He recommended that the new bill simply make the Treasurer responsible for reporting 
remaining fund balances to the Senate each month and list the five funds the report should cover, 
rather than prescribing detailed report contents and transaction ledgers. The SG&A Accounting Office 
already prepares a fund balance report, including the CAD Fund, which can be used to satisfy this 
requirement. Regular access to current fund balances allows Senators to make informed allocation 
decisions and advances the transparency purpose of the Senate In The Sunshine chapter. 
Stakeholders include the Student Body Treasurer, the SG&A Accounting Office, the Student Senate, 
and the RSOs and departments funded through these accounts. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Andy Johnson, Program Director, FSU Student Governance & Advocacy, who reviewed Senate Bill 034 
following its veto and recommended the streamlined approach reflected in this bill, including use of the 
existing fund balance report prepared by the SG&A Accounting Office. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, the Student Body Treasurer would be responsible for providing the Student Senate a report 
of the remaining fund balances in the RSO Allocation Committee, RSO Development Fund, Senate 

 Page 14 of 25Projects, Campus Advancement and Development Fund, and Executive Projects accounts on a 
monthly basis while the Senate is in session. The existing fund balance report prepared by the SG&A 
Accounting Office may be used for this purpose, so no new reporting format is created. No other 
provisions of Chapter 409 are changed apart from renumbering the existing “Engagement with the 
Student Body” subsection.

Short Title: To Collect Attendance Data for SGA Sponsored Events 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 801 of the Student Body Statutes to require entities receiving A&S 
funding to submit attendance information for each event funded in whole or in part with A&S fees within 
ten days of the event. The bill establishes multiple methods for collecting attendance data, including 
FSU Card swipe data, QR code check-ins, and paper sign-ins when technology failures occur. 
 
Background Information: 
SGA provides A&S funding to organizations and entities that offer programming and events to FSU 
students. Currently, consistent attendance data across A&S-funded programming can provide valuable 
information about student participation and engagement. Requiring attendance data to be collected and 
submitted will allow SGA to identify participation trends and better understand the reach and 
effectiveness of programs supported by A&S fees. 
 
Attendance tracking is already used for certain large-scale campus events, demonstrating that 
attendance collection can be incorporated into event programming. The proposed legislation provides 
organizations with multiple methods of collecting attendance information, including card swipes and QR 
codes, while allowing paper collection in the event of technology failures 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 

During the development of this legislation, feedback was sought from individuals involved with SGA-
funded organizations regarding the feasibility and implementation of attendance tracking. The 
Treasurer of the Pride Student Union provided feedback based on his organization's experience using 
paper sign-in methods and recommended QR-code check-ins as a potentially efficient method for 
tracking attendance. The IRHC has already adopted card swipe systems and QR code scanning to 
track attendance, and has prepared a graph example of their signature events and attendance in the 
attachments. 

Office of the Treasurer was included in consultation and supports the tracking of attendance data, and 
the SGA Business Manager confirmed its ability to implement. 

 Page 24 of 25Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would require all entities receiving A&S funding to submit attendance 
information for each event funded at least in part with A&S fees within ten days of the event's 
conclusion. Organizations may collect attendance through FSU Card swipe data or QR-code check-ins 
using FSU IDs, with paper attendance available when technology failures occur. Attendance data would 
be submitted to the SGA Business Manager and the Office of the Treasurer. 
 
The collected information would provide SGA with consistent data on student participation in A&S-
funded programming, which can be used to identify attendance trends and evaluate the reach and 
effectiveness of funded events.

Short Title: Creating Student Government Grant Programs 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 309 of the Student Body Statutes to establish a structure for Student 
Government grant programs. It would create the Textbook Grant Program and the Internship Housing 
Grant Program to provide financial support for qualifying student expenses. 
 
Background Information: 
This legislation is being presented to create a formal process for Student Government to provide grant 
funding directly toward student expenses. The proposed programs would initially focus on two areas: 
textbook costs and housing costs associated with qualifying summer internships. 
 
Under the proposed structure, the Student Senate would determine funding for each grant through the 
annual budget process. The Office of the Treasurer, in coordination with the SGA Business Manager, 
would then oversee the administration and distribution of those funds. This structure allows Student 
Government to support student success while maintaining Senate oversight of the amount allocated to 
each program. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, Deputy Student Body Treasurer 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would create two Student Government grant programs. The Textbook Grant 
Program would allow FSU students to receive up to $200 per fiscal year toward textbook purchases 
through Bill's Bookstore. The Internship Housing Grant Program would provide eligible students 
participating in qualifying summer internships with $1,000 toward housing costs. The programs would 
be administered by the Office of the Treasurer, with funding determined annually by the Student 
Senate.

Short Title: To Establish the Legal Preparation Council 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would create the Legal Preparation Council, a new Affiliated Project between SGA, 
FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-law 
students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning about the law, with the resources 
available from the SGA, Pre-law advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 
Background Information: 
FSU ranks within the top 10 of undergraduate feeder institutions for Law School, producing a large pool 
of applicants to Law Schools across the United States. Despite this, overall support for pre-law 
programming and development across the University is low. The FSU Law School and Pre-Law team 
recognized this, attempting to launch more programming for these groups in the Fall semester. To 
compliment this programming, this legislation aims to work with these campus partners to support the 
success of pre-law students across the University. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Legislative consultation included the former Law School Council (funding board) Chair, SGA Advising, 
Pre-Law advising, the Pre-Law President’s council, Phi Alpha Delta, Prep and Conquer, Lex et Lux 
Society, Black Future Attorneys, Hispanic Future Attorneys, Chair of Judiciary, and the FSU Law 
School. The sponsors additionally held a Townhall on this legislation, inviting the opinions of pre-law 
students, and heavily advertised this to the student body, receiving large amounts of support across the 
pre-law sphere. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would create a new Affiliated Project to support the pre-law sphere at FSU, focusing on 
uplifting and aiding RSOs, Pre-Law and Law School admin, and supporting success of students 
entering law school.

Student Governance & Advocacy, advised that a new bill be introduced rather than a motion to 
reconsider. He recommended that the new bill simply make the Treasurer responsible for reporting 
remaining fund balances to the Senate each month and list the five funds the report should cover, 
rather than prescribing detailed report contents and transaction ledgers. The SG&A Accounting Office 
already prepares a fund balance report, including the CAD Fund, which can be used to satisfy this 
requirement. Regular access to current fund balances allows Senators to make informed allocation 
decisions and advances the transparency purpose of the Senate In The Sunshine chapter. 
Stakeholders include the Student Body Treasurer, the SG&A Accounting Office, the Student Senate, 
and the RSOs and departments funded through these accounts. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:

following its veto and recommended the streamlined approach reflected in this bill, including use of the 
existing fund balance report prepared by the SG&A Accounting Office.

of the remaining fund balances in the RSO Allocation Committee, RSO Development Fund, Senate

provisions of Chapter 409 are changed apart from renumbering the existing “Engagement with the 
Student Body” subsection.

 78th STUDENT SENATE 
 Legislation Cover Sheet 

 Senate Bill #: 049 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Dereje, Perantoni 
 Co-sponsor(s): Dewey 

Short Title: To Collect Attendance Data for SGA Sponsored Events 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 801 of the Student Body Statutes to require entities receiving A&S 
funding to submit attendance information for each event funded in whole or in part with A&S fees within 
ten days of the event. The bill establishes multiple methods for collecting attendance data, including 
FSU Card swipe data, QR code check-ins, and paper sign-ins when technology failures occur. 
 
Background Information: 
SGA provides A&S funding to organizations and entities that offer programming and events to FSU 
students. Currently, consistent attendance data across A&S-funded programming can provide valuable 
information about student participation and engagement. Requiring attendance data to be collected and 
submitted will allow SGA to identify participation trends and better understand the reach and 
effectiveness of programs supported by A&S fees. 
 
Attendance tracking is already used for certain large-scale campus events, demonstrating that 
attendance collection can be incorporated into event programming. The proposed legislation provides 
organizations with multiple methods of collecting attendance information, including card swipes and QR 
codes, while allowing paper collection in the event of technology failures 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 

During the development of this legislation, feedback was sought from individuals involved with SGA-
funded organizations regarding the feasibility and implementation of attendance tracking. The 
Treasurer of the Pride Student Union provided feedback based on his organization's experience using 
paper sign-in methods and recommended QR-code check-ins as a potentially efficient method for 
tracking attendance. The IRHC has already adopted card swipe systems and QR code scanning to 
track attendance, and has prepared a graph example of their signature events and attendance in the 
attachments. 

Office of the Treasurer was included in consultation and supports the tracking of attendance data, and 
the SGA Business Manager confirmed its ability to implement. 

 Page 28 of 29Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would require all entities receiving A&S funding to submit attendance 
information for each event funded at least in part with A&S fees within ten days of the event's 
conclusion. Organizations may collect attendance through FSU Card swipe data or QR-code check-ins 
using FSU IDs, with paper attendance available when technology failures occur. Attendance data would 
be submitted to the SGA Business Manager and the Office of the Treasurer. 
 
The collected information would provide SGA with consistent data on student participation in A&S-
funded programming, which can be used to identify attendance trends and evaluate the reach and 
effectiveness of funded events.

10-5-2026 COGS Meeting Minutes 
 
Absences: Terrence (unexcused), Fahad (excused), Sima (excused), Madison (excused) 
 
Steven: We can go into reading and approval of the meeting minutes. They’re posted in today’s 
agenda and on the QR code up here. 
 
Devan: Motion to approve 
 
Sadio: Seconded 
 
Steven: Any objections? Seeing none. Meeting minutes are approved. Now we’ll go into special 
introductions, and we have Lexi Holliday here representing the Student Senate. 
 
Lexi: Would love to do some collaborations between Senate and COGS, I’d like to foster the 
connection more, so let me know if you have any ideas or suggestions. I’m running for the 
student senate graduate studies seat this year since I’m pursuing a master’s next year and have 
been taking graduate-level coursework. If there are any ideas or policies that you guys have in 
mind, please let me know. There are lots of graduate student specific issues that I didn’t know 
about before. 
 
Steven: Any other student comments or reports in the audience? Seeing none. We’ll go directly 
into the report of the officers. Joey is running late so I’ll quickly go over the current budget 
report for him and he can cover his items more extensively later. But I wanted to quickly bring it 
up now before he gets here since one of the bills we have today is to transfer more money into 
this cycle’s presentation grant line item since we are almost out of funding and he still has about 
40 applications pending in his inbox. 
 
Steven: Annual budget report coming soon, we should be having this wrapped up sometime later 
this week. We also have the graduate lounge coming up with the globe on October 23rd. Should 
be a great time with live music, coffee, and tea. 
 
Steven: Main difference in the current budget report is the presentation grant number, and one of 
the bills today will specifically be referencing the line item for our current cycle. Next, we’ll go 
into updates from the Deputy Speakers. 
 
DaSean: I’ve been in contact with the food pantry, and I’ll be putting together a bill soon to 
coordinate a donation sponsored by the advocacy committee. Also looking into a retreat for us, I 
was thinking either bowling, rez, or paint a pot, if you have any preferences, feel free to send me 
an email. We’re thinking November-ish when it’s not so hot. That’s all I have from me. 
 
Claire: Janai and I were coordinating with Emily Woo, who is the photographer and 
videographer for SGA because Janai had this wonderful idea of doing headshots for every 
representative and we’ll get some group photos of all three committees and the executive board 
as well. I wanted to gauge with you guys if you would prefer to do pictures on a Monday after 
our usual meeting or if maybe we could find a weekend when we could do it. I’m personally thinking maybe a weekend would be better that way we can get some pretty pictures in the 
sunlight outside instead of having to take them inside because it’ll be dark out by the time our 
usual meetings are over. We could potentially schedule more than one, I would just have to 
coordinate with her and I’d like to keep it limited to maybe two sessions at most. I’m excited for 
this, I think it’ll be nice to have those. We’re still working on the budget report but that should be 
done pretty soon. 
 
Steven: What kind of attire were you thinking for the headshots? Should we wear the COGS 
polos or more formal attire with the name tags? 
 
Claire: I don’t think polos are the vibe, I would say business casual at least and then we can have 
some photos with the name tags on and some without that way we’re all free to reuse the pictures 
for other things if we’d like. 
 
Nicholette: Sadly, Mark, who we ended up switching over into the Veterans Advocate Seat last 
meeting so we could accommodation both petitioners, his schedule has now changed and he is 
unable to petition in formally tonight. And Arezoo is sadly not able to attend anymore as well. 
That’s my main two updates for tonight. 
 
DaSean: So is Mark not coming in at all now? 
 
Nicholette: No, but he said he is going to look into repetitioning either next semester and next 
year into the Veteran’s Advocate Seat if it’s still open, but right now, some circumstances came 
up and it won’t work with his schedule anymore. 
 
Steven: Next, we’ll go into Advisor announcements. 
 
Tanner: The deadline to register to vote or update your address so you can vote in Leon County 
for the midterm elections, outside of FSU, is tonight at 11:59pm. So if you have not done that 
yet, you have about three and a half hours left to do so. Joey is not here yet, but he worked really 
hard on moving the COGS grant applications into FSUHQ. Him and I think the e-board and 
some of you guys all had a hand in testing it, which I’m really appreciative of. It is 99% 
amazing, but there is just 1% that him and I are still trying to figure out. Basically, these grant 
emails are going to his student email in addition to his deputy speaker email. And a little 
elections update, so last week, our supervisor of elections resigned, and that was really fun. We 
have found a new acting supervisor of elections that Senate confirmed Wednesday night, thank 
you, Lexi, for that. He is a law student, and I think that it is actually a really cool idea to have a 
law student be our supervisor of elections, especially with the elections being under the judicial 
branch of SGA. I’m sure you all received an email from me last week that we had to cancel the 
candidate seminar last Friday. The previous supervisor of elections resigned at 4:30pm on 
Thursday and we had the candidate seminar scheduled the next business day at 8am. So I 
decided to postpone and reschedule the candidate seminar, and now it will be October 7th at 
4:30pm, and as a reminder, these are mandatory. Lastly, the SGA election days are October 11th 
and October 12th. There will also be an election night results announcement on October 12th at 
9pm at Proof in the Student Union. For inauguration, you will all be sworn in on Tuesday, 
December 1st. If you do not take the oath of office during inauguration, Nicholette will swear you in during the next COGS meeting. But I really encourage you all to attend. Steven will be giving 
his outgoing address as speaker, our new COGS speaker will be giving his or her incoming 
address, and DaSean will be signing the national anthem. And of course there will be free food 
too. You all will receive a Save-the-Datte email on Monday, October 19th and then you’ll receive 
your formal invitation on Monday November 2nd, to attend inauguration. There will be an RSVP, 
and whether you want to attend or not, please RSVP that way we know how many people are 
attending. Last thing, the state of the student body address hosted by the executive branch will be 
on Thursday, November 5th and hosted in the student union ballrooms. That’s all from me, thank 
you, Steven. 
 
Steven: Alright, that’s it for exec board updates, now we just have committee updates. 
 
Rasleen: We are working on troubleshooting FSUHQ to see if members are able to access it or 
not as well as updating the COGS website. Next meeting Internal Affairs committee meeting is 
on October 12th 7pm. 
 
Janai: No Outreach meeting last week because I was sick and had no voice, we will be catching 
up next week and should have more to report during the next meeting. 
 
Devan: The advocacy committee is working in tandem with GAU to have town halls or 
roundtable sessions with different colleges based on data they have collected. One of their 
officers, Ronnie, will be coming to our next meeting to speak with you all. We’re also seeing 
what we could do to get a Panama City Campus representative. 
 
Tanner: Does anyone remember Kyana? Kyana is now a student at the graduate school in 
Panama City, we could make her the next COGS representative. 
 
Steven: Thank you all, now we can get into our bills for the night. Joey, the floor is yours, 
you’ve got three minutes. This is bill number 25. 
 
Joey: I’ll keep this quick, this is a transfer for presentation grants. For those who are now, we 
have three cycles of presentation grants per year, and we have run out for the July to October 
cycle and about 38 applications still pending. I think $5,000 will cover what’s remaining and is a 
fair amount to move in for a cycle. It won’t cover everybody, but it’ll cover enough people that 
it’s worth it. And that’s kind of all there is to it. 
 
Steven: Thank you, sponsor. Questions? 
 
Rasleen: How much do we have in the reserves in total? 
 
Joey: I don’t think I’ve transferred in the $15,000 extra we have from cancelling the graduate 
assistant funding, so I think we’re at about $50,000. 
 
Rasleen: So we have two options, to either take from the reserves or to take from future grant 
cycles? 
 Joey: We can’t take from future grant cycles, those are set in stone. Those were allocated through 
the budget so they’re stuck the way they are. 
 
Rasleen: And the amount you’re taking out of reserves is just for presentation grants or 
attendance grants or both? 
 
Joey: Just for presentation grants. The attendance grants have no applications pending last time I 
checked. 
 
Claire: How many presentation grants do you have pending? I think it’s like 40 something 
maybe. 
 
Joey: I think we’re at 38, but I haven’t gone through and combed for the ones that are basically 
for the wrong cycle, because that tends to happen a lot towards the end. 
 
Steven: So about as high as $20,000 just in pending currently. And then the cycle cuts off when? 
 
Joey: October 16th. 
 
Steven: More questions for the sponsor? Do we want to transfer more money? 
 
Daniel G: What would be the negative of transferring more money? What instead would we be 
spending the reserves on? 
 
Joey: There are a few organizations that didn’t come on the budget this year, so they’ll probably 
be coming to request from us. 
 
Steven: Every bill that comes up in a meeting is allocated through our reserves. Last year our 
reserves were almost $100,000 and we almost all of it. This year it’s down to $35,000, not 
including the graduate assistant stipend, just for reference. If we have 40 applications pending 
that amount up to $20,000, then $5,000 isn’t enough. But if we transfer too much, we might need 
it for other cycles as well. 
 
Joey: If we intended to cover every single presentation grant that came in for each cycle, it would 
probably eat up the rest of our reserves. 
 
Daniel: I guess is it inevitable that if we have reserves left over that somebody will come ask for 
it? Or is there a chance that if we have reserves left over that they could come back and we could 
maybe pay for part of it? 
 
Steven: Yes but to retrospectively go back and give them the money wouldn’t be until the end of 
the fiscal year, which is June 2027. Unless you go out of town and want to wait eight months to 
be refunded for your conference travel. Is there a motion to extend the discussion by 5 minutes? 
 
Sadio: Motion to extend discussion time by 5 minutes 
 Islamiyat: Seconded 
 
Steven: We’ll try to wrap up this questions here, Devan. 
 
Devan: How many more applications can we expect over the next two and a half weeks? And it 
has to be in attendance within these next 2 weeks. So how many people will actually be applying 
right now to go somewhere? 
 
Joey: In my experience, nobody. Most of the time, at this point, if I’m getting an application, it’s 
for the November cycle. 
 
Devan: So hopefully $5,000 should be adequate enough, depending on how many of them there 
are actually within this cycle. 
 
Steven: Any further questions for the sponsor? Any final questions? Seeing none, we can go into 
a period of pro. Any pros for this bill? 
 
DaSean: This is great, I remember we discussed this happening in Sunset Committee, it was 
something we saw something. Glad we have enough reserves to make up at least a little bit of 
what is left. 
 
Steven: I can quickly add too. We’ve done this many times before, I think this is a great idea. If 
need be, we can come back during the next meeting to cover the rest. Any further pros for the 
sponsor? Seeing none, we’ll go into a period of con. Any cons or questions? Seeing none. Is 
there a motion to call the question? 
 
DaSean: Motion to call the question 
 
Islamiyat: Seconded 
 
Steven: Any objections? Seeing none. 
 
Vote on Bill 25: 17-0-1, bill passes. 
 
Bill 26, sponsored by Nicholette 
 
Nicholette: The Clinical Psychology Graduate Student Association speaker series event is on 
October 16th, 9am-1:30pm, this bill will cover food for that event. Approximately 30 people will 
be in attendance. Bagels and coffee in the morning and some lunch; it amounts to less than $10 a 
student for both breakfast and lunch with the quote being $280 total. President is also here as 
well if there are any questions for her. 
 
Steven: Thank you, sponsor. We’ll go into a period of questions. 
 
DaSean: Do you have the quote from Panera? 
 Nicholette: Yes 
 
Steven: It should be in the agenda 
 
Claire: I don’t think you sent it, Nicholette 
 
DaSean: Yeah I don’t see it in the agenda 
 
Claire: I think you only sent the cover sheet and the bill itself 
 
Steven: Could you just go over it quickly? 
 
Nicholette: There are 2 bagel packs for $38, a tote of coffee for $22, and three sets of assorted 
sandwiches for $200. 
 
DaSean: And this is without tax, right? 
 
Nicholette: Yes 
 
Islamiyat: When is it? 
 
Nicholette: It is on October 16th from 9am to 1:30pm 
 
Islamiyat: Who are the speakers? Are they from outside the area or are they from FSU? 
 
CPGSA President: She’s from FSU she works for the College of Medicine 
 
Islamiyat: Just one person? And the food covers everyone who attends? 
 
CPGSA President: Correct 
 
Steven: Any further questions for the sponsor of the bill? Seeing none. We can go into a period 
of pro. Anything in pro? 
 
DaSean: Sounds like a great event 
 
Steven: I can add quickly too that this organization comes to COGS about this time every single 
year for this event, and it’s always a great event. Any other pros? Seeing none, we can go into a 
final period of con and questions. Anything to say? 
 
DaSean: It’s not in con, I just have a question. Have you all thought about coming to the budget 
committee to request funding for this event? Just in case we don’t have bountiful reserves in the 
future? I think we meet in February. 
 Steven: We can send you the dates later on and then the funding is guaranteed, it’s great for 
organizations like you who have annual events planned that they repeat every year. Any final 
cons or questions? Seeing none. Is there a motion to call the question? 
 
Islamiyat: Motion to call the question 
 
DaSean: Seconded 
 
Steven: Any objections? Seeing none. 
 
Vote on Bill 26: 18-0-0 
 
Roundtable prompt: How are you feeling about this semester so far? 
 
Steven: Thank you everyone, meeting adjourned at 7:37pm.

 8 own experience with a 1974 breast cancer diagnosis and subsequent mastectomy; and 
 9 
10 WHEREAS, An average woman in the United States has about a 13%, or a 1 in 8, lifetime 
11 chance of developing invasive breast cancer. In 2026, the American Cancer Society estimates 
12 about 321,910 new cases of invasive breast cancer ; and 
13 
14 WHEREAS, Overall breast cancer rates have been rising by about 1% per year, with slightly 
15 faster increases (1.4% per year) in women under 50. The American Cancer Society estimates 
16 that 2,670 men in the United States will be diagnosed with invasive breast cancer, and about 
17 530 will die from the disease; and 
18

22 specifically demand more funding for stage 4 research rather than generic awareness; and 
23

27 treatment decisions; and

Short Title: To Collect Attendance Data for SGA Sponsored Events 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 801 of the Student Body Statutes to require entities receiving A&S 
funding to submit attendance information for each event funded in whole or in part with A&S fees within 
ten days of the event. The bill establishes multiple methods for collecting attendance data, including 
FSU Card swipe data, QR code check-ins, and paper sign-ins when technology failures occur. 
 
Background Information: 
SGA provides A&S funding to organizations and entities that offer programming and events to FSU 
students. Currently, consistent attendance data across A&S-funded programming can provide valuable 
information about student participation and engagement. Requiring attendance data to be collected and 
submitted will allow SGA to identify participation trends and better understand the reach and 
effectiveness of programs supported by A&S fees. 
 
Attendance tracking is already used for certain large-scale campus events, demonstrating that 
attendance collection can be incorporated into event programming. The proposed legislation provides 
organizations with multiple methods of collecting attendance information, including card swipes and QR 
codes, while allowing paper collection in the event of technology failures 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 

During the development of this legislation, feedback was sought from individuals involved with SGA-
funded organizations regarding the feasibility and implementation of attendance tracking. The 
Treasurer of the Pride Student Union provided feedback based on his organization's experience using 
paper sign-in methods and recommended QR-code check-ins as a potentially efficient method for 
tracking attendance. The IRHC has already adopted card swipe systems and QR code scanning to 
track attendance, and has prepared a graph example of their signature events and attendance in the 
attachments. 

Office of the Treasurer was included in consultation and supports the tracking of attendance data, and 
the SGA Business Manager confirmed its ability to implement. 

 Page 15 of 16
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would require all entities receiving A&S funding to submit attendance 
information for each event funded at least in part with A&S fees within ten days of the event's 
conclusion. Organizations may collect attendance through FSU Card swipe data or QR-code check-ins 
using FSU IDs, with paper attendance available when technology failures occur. Attendance data would 
be submitted to the SGA Business Manager and the Office of the Treasurer. 
 
The collected information would provide SGA with consistent data on student participation in A&S-
funded programming, which can be used to identify attendance trends and evaluate the reach and 
effectiveness of funded events.

Short Title: Creating Student Government Grant Programs 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 309 of the Student Body Statutes to establish a structure for Student 
Government grant programs. It would create the John Thrasher Textbook Grant and the Warren Mazek 
Internship Housing Grant to provide financial support for qualifying student expenses. 
 
Background Information: 
This legislation is being presented to create a formal process for Student Government to provide grant 
funding directly toward student expenses. The proposed programs would initially focus on two areas: 
textbook costs and housing costs associated with qualifying summer internships. 
 
Under the proposed structure, the Student Senate would determine funding for each grant through the 
annual budget process. The Office of the Treasurer, in coordination with the SGA Business Manager, 
would then oversee the administration and distribution of those funds. This structure allows Student 
Government to support student success while maintaining Senate oversight of the amount allocated to 
each program. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, Deputy Student Body Treasurer 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would create two Student Government grant programs. The John Thrasher 
Textbook Grant would allow FSU students to receive up to $200 per fiscal year toward textbook 
purchases through Bill's Bookstore. The Warren Mazek Internship Housing Grant would provide eligible 
students participating in qualifying summer internships with $1,000 toward housing costs. The 
programs would be administered by the Office of the Treasurer, with funding determined annually by 
the Student Senate.

Short Title: To Establish the Law School Preparation Council 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a new Affiliated Project between 
SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-
law students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning about the law, with the resources 
available from the SGA, Pre-law advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 
Background Information: 
FSU ranks within the top 10 of undergraduate feeder institutions for Law School, producing a large pool 
of applicants to Law Schools across the United States. Despite this, overall support for pre-law 
programming and development across the University is low. The FSU Law School and Pre-Law team 
recognized this, attempting to launch more programming for these groups in the Fall semester. To 
compliment this programming, this legislation aims to work with these campus partners to support the 
success of pre-law students across the University. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Legislative consultation included the former Law School Council (funding board) Chair, SGA Advising, 
Pre-Law advising, the Pre-Law President’s council, Phi Alpha Delta, Prep and Conquer, Lex et Lux 
Society, Black Future Attorneys, Hispanic Future Attorneys, Chair of Judiciary, and the FSU Law 
School. The sponsors additionally held a Townhall on this legislation, inviting the opinions of pre-law 
students, and heavily advertised this to the student body, receiving large amounts of support across the 
pre-law sphere. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would create a new Affiliated Project to support the pre-law sphere at FSU, focusing on 
uplifting and aiding RSOs, Pre-Law and Law School admin, and supporting success of students 
entering law school.

Short Title: Restructuring Forms of Legislation Act 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This Bill removes specific reference to legislation forms and instead refers to them as 
“legislation.” This is to ensure that if legislation forms change in the future, Student Body 
Statutes don’t need to be largely altered to reflect the given changes. 
 
Background Information: 
Due to recent clarifications regarding forms of legislation, it was decided to reclarify how legislation 
should be referred to in Student Body Statute. Because of this, an agreement was made to refer to 
forms of legislation broadly in order to prevent large alterations of Student Body Statutes, should forms 
of legislation once again change. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
This legislation was written in correspondence and discussion with the Senate President, to reaffirm the 
language being used and replaced. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation will prevent large changes to Student Body Statutes every time a change is made to 
legislative forms, as we’ve seen increased alterations of in the past few Senates. All lists of types of 
legislation will be shortened to “legislation” and singular references to a legislative type will be amended 
to “piece of legislation” in order to ensure these desired effects.

Short Title: Creating Student Government Grant Programs 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 309 of the Student Body Statutes to establish a structure for Student 
Government grant programs. It would create the John Thrasher Textbook Grant and the Warren Mazek 
Internship Housing Grant to provide financial support for qualifying student expenses. 
 
Background Information: 
This legislation is being presented to create a formal process for Student Government to provide grant 
funding directly toward student expenses. The proposed programs would initially focus on two areas: 
textbook costs and housing costs associated with qualifying summer internships. 
 
Under the proposed structure, the Student Senate would determine funding for each grant through the 
annual budget process. The Office of the Treasurer, in coordination with the SGA Business Manager, 
would then oversee the administration and distribution of those funds. This structure allows Student 
Government to support student success while maintaining Senate oversight of the amount allocated to 
each program. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, Deputy Student Body Treasurer 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would create two Student Government grant programs. The John Thrasher 
Textbook Grant would allow FSU students to receive up to $200 per fiscal year toward textbook 
purchases through Bill's Bookstore. The Warren Mazek Internship Housing Grant would provide eligible 
students participating in qualifying summer internships with $1,000 toward housing costs. The 
programs would be administered by the Office of the Treasurer, with funding determined annually by 
the Student Senate.

Short Title: To Establish the Law School Preparation Council 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a new Affiliated Project between 
SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-
law students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning about the law, with the resources 
available from the SGA, Pre-law advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 
Background Information: 
FSU ranks within the top 10 of undergraduate feeder institutions for Law School, producing a large pool 
of applicants to Law Schools across the United States. Despite this, overall support for pre-law 
programming and development across the University is low. The FSU Law School and Pre-Law team 
recognized this, attempting to launch more programming for these groups in the Fall semester. To 
compliment this programming, this legislation aims to work with these campus partners to support the 
success of pre-law students across the University. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Legislative consultation included the former Law School Council (funding board) Chair, SGA Advising, 
Pre-Law advising, the Pre-Law President’s council, Phi Alpha Delta, Prep and Conquer, Lex et Lux 
Society, Black Future Attorneys, Hispanic Future Attorneys, Chair of Judiciary, and the FSU Law 
School. The sponsors additionally held a Townhall on this legislation, inviting the opinions of pre-law 
students, and heavily advertised this to the student body, receiving large amounts of support across the 
pre-law sphere. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would create a new Affiliated Project to support the pre-law sphere at FSU, focusing on 
uplifting and aiding RSOs, Pre-Law and Law School admin, and supporting success of students 
entering law school.

21 (1) Chair of the Council -- The Chair shall be responsible for organizing the meetings of 
22 the Council, shall be responsible for recording the votes of the Council, shall be 
23 responsible for representing the Council in an official capacity, and shall be 
24 responsible for conducting interviews and forwarding candidates for positions not 
25 appointed by the Student Body President. This position shall be filled via 
26 appointment by the Student Body President and confirmation by the Student Senate. 

27 (2) Vice-Chair of the Council -- The Vice-Chair shall be responsible for all duties in the 
28 absence of the Chair, and shall be responsible for taking attendance of the council at 
29 all its official meetings. The Vice-Chair shall additionally perform any functions as 
30 deemed necessary by the Chair. This position shall be filled via appointment by the 
31 Student Body President and confirmation by the Student Senate. 

32 (3) Treasurer -- The Treasurer shall be responsible for the proper stewardship of the 
33 monies of the LSPC. The Treasurer shall represent the LSPC in coordination with the 
34 Chair at all instances where finances are concerned, including, but not limited to, the 
35 annual budget process. The Treasurer shall additionally provide recommendations to 
36 the council for the acquisition of monies at fundraisers or other events. This position 
37 shall be filled via appointment by the Student Body President and confirmation by the 
38 Student Senate. 

39 (4) Registrar -- The Registrar shall be responsible for the maintenance of all meeting 
40 minutes of the Council and its record-keeping. The Registrar shall also be the liaison 
41 between affiliate RSOs and the council, ensuring that the needs of all the affiliate 
42 RSOs are met and the council is properly engaging in programming to support its 
43 affiliates on campus. The Registrar shall recommend event suggestions to the 
44 council whenever necessary. The Registrar shall also maintain membership and the 
45 maintenance of the LSPC’s mailing list. This position shall be filled via appointment 
46 by the Student Body President and confirmation by the Student Senate. 

 Page 4 of 8
47 (5) Law Student Representative -- The Law Student Representative shall be an 
48 individual currently enrolled at FSU Law School who shall be responsible for voting 
49 on the council and giving suggestions to the council for events that would support 
50 undergraduate student success. The purpose of the Representative is to give insight 
51 to the undergraduate population about how they succeeded in entering law school 
52 and to attempt to replicate that amongst the members. This position shall be filled by 
53 a nomination of the Chair of the Council and confirmation by a majority of the voting 
54 members currently present on the board. 

55 (6) Training Director -- The Training Director shall be responsible for the compilation of 
56 LSAT resources for the members of the LSPC and shall also be responsible for 
57 acquiring speakers for the LSPC’s events. The Training Director shall work with the 
58 advisors and the Law School Representative to ensure the council’s membership has 
59 adequate access to law school admission resources, testing dates and locations, and 
60 any other resource the council deems necessary for student success. This position 
61 shall be filled by a nomination of the Chair of the Council and confirmation by a 
62 majority of the voting members currently present on the board. 

63 (7) Advisor -- The Advisor shall be a pre-law advisor at FSU, who shall be tasked with 
64 supporting the council in its endeavors and in accomplishing its goals. The Advisor 
65 shall serve an indefinite term of office, only to be removed by a unanimous vote of 
66 the council. The Advisor shall have voting power on the council. This position shall 
67 be filled by a nomination of the Chair of the Council and confirmation by a majority of 
68 the voting members currently present on the board. 

69 (8) Law School Designee -- The Law School Designee shall be an individual designated 
70 by the FSU Law School, in order to liaise and cooperate between the LSPC and the 
71 Law School for Undergraduate pre-law engagement. The Law School Designee shall 
72 serve an indefinite term of office, only to be removed by the decision of the Law 
73 School. This position shall be filled by unilateral appointment by the Law School, with 
74 whatever methods the Law School deems fit. 

75 c. The Council shall be relieved of duty at the end of the Spring semester, regardless of how 
76 long they have actually served in the position. Following the election of the Student Body 
77 President, the positions will be filled over the course of the Summer Senate Session pending 
78 approval and confirmation by the Student Senate. This shall not be construed as limiting the 
79 Senate’s ability to confirm only to the Summer, merely indicating the ideal timeline for the 
80 approval of candidates to the LSPC. 

81 d. The Council may establish any other operational policies that do not conflict with its statutory 
82 obligations and restrictions, which shall be treated as policy in accordance with SBS § 416, 
83 which shall not require Senate approval for revision and adoption. 

84 3. Membership 

85 a. Membership shall be open to any student at Florida State University, regardless of interest in 
86 Pre-Law. Members do not need to be associated with any affiliate organization of the LSPC 
87 in order to enroll as a member in the LSPC and shall become a member by presenting their 
88 student ID for verification purposes to the Registrar and by presenting their student email 
89 address to be added to the council’s email distribution network. 

90 b. There shall be no dues required for an individual to be a member of the LSPC. 

91 4. Affiliated RSOs 

92 a. The Law School Participation Council shall create an avenue for pre-law-oriented RSOs to 
93 affiliate with the council. The requirements for affiliation are the following: 

 Page 5 of 8
 94 (1) The RSO must be currently active by verification of the Office of Student 
 95 Organizations and Involvement (SOI). 

 96 (2) The RSO must be, in full or the majority part, dedicated to pre-law advocacy and/or 
 97 programming. 

 98 (A) If any doubt exists as to whether or not an RSO is dedicated to pre-law 
 99 programming, either a letter from SOI stating they are majority dedicated to 
100 pre-law advocacy and/or programming, or a majority vote of the council shall 
101 suffice to resolve the doubt. 

102 (3) The RSO must be majority made up of undergraduate students. 

103 b. An Affiliate RSO gains the following benefits: 

104 (1) The ability to cost-share events with the LSPC, subject to fund availability and the 
105 approval of a majority of the council. 

106 (2) The advertisement of the affiliated RSO through the LSPC’s mailing list. 

107 (3) The ability to co-host events with the LSPC, to bolster the recognition of the affiliate 
108 RSO to the pre-law student body. 

109 (4) The ability to utilize and disseminate resources from the LSPC to their RSO’s 
110 membership. 

111 (A) If an RSO chooses to charge dues as a requirement for membership in their 
112 organization, they are not entitled to resources for the purpose of exclusive 
113 access to their RSO. Any resource the LSPC disseminates must be available 
114 to everyone in the student body. 

115 (5) The appointment of Ambassadors to represent their RSO to the Registrar, who will 
116 serve in an advising capacity to ensure events are planned well, and planned with 
117 other RSOs when appropriate. 

118 c. The Council may not, under any circumstances, attempt to place conditions besides the 
119 basic requirements to be an affiliated RSO, including but not limited to changing an RSO’s 
120 practices, rules, or leadership. 

121 d. Affiliation of RSOs shall be confirmed on a shall-confirm basis by a majority vote of the 
122 council, only taking into consideration whether or not an RSO meets the minimum 
123 requirements to be an affiliate. 

124 e. Should the council in any way abridge the ability for an RSO to be an affiliate of the LSPC, 
125 the RSO shall be given standing to request the Student Supreme Court’s intervention to 
126 determine whether or not an RSO should be given affiliated status. 

127 

128 Section 2. Effective Date. 

129 The provisions of this bill shall take effect upon signature of the Vice President of Student Affairs.

 78th STUDENT SENATE 
 Legislation Cover Sheet 

 Senate Bill #: 045 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Perantoni, Nturubika 
 Co-sponsor(s): Torres, Dewey, Kaplan, Tizon, Hidalgo, Ramirez, Cineas, Costello, Aihe, 
 Serpenguzel, Friall 

Short Title: To Establish the Law School Preparation Council 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a new Affiliated Project between 
SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-
law students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning about the law, with the resources 
available from the SGA, Pre-law advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 
Background Information: 
FSU ranks within the top 10 of undergraduate feeder institutions for Law School, producing a large pool 
of applicants to Law Schools across the United States. Despite this, overall support for pre-law 
programming and development across the University is low. The FSU Law School and Pre-Law team 
recognized this, attempting to launch more programming for these groups in the Fall semester. To 
compliment this programming, this legislation aims to work with these campus partners to support the 
success of pre-law students across the University. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Legislative consultation included the former Law School Council (funding board) Chair, SGA Advising, 
Pre-Law advising, the Pre-Law President’s council, Phi Alpha Delta, Prep and Conquer, Lex et Lux 
Society, Black Future Attorneys, Hispanic Future Attorneys, Chair of Judiciary, and the FSU Law 
School. The sponsors additionally held a Townhall on this legislation, inviting the opinions of pre-law 
students, and heavily advertised this to the student body, receiving large amounts of support across the 
pre-law sphere. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would create a new Affiliated Project to support the pre-law sphere at FSU, focusing on 
uplifting and aiding RSOs, Pre-Law and Law School admin, and supporting success of students 
entering law school.
