INTERNAL AFFAIRS COMMITTEE 
 September 28, 2026 at 6:30 PM 
 Location: fla.st/sga-meet-ia 
 MEETING MINUTES 

 Call to Order 
 Chair Bigenho called the meeting to order at 6:33 PM. 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 
 
 Chair Bigenho acknowledged the Land Acknowledgement. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
 Vice Chair Gaynor administered Roll Call and Verified Quorum. 
 
 Present: Bigenho, Aihe, Macedo, Dominiquez Dambre, Frazee, Gaynor, 
 Hamlin, Le, Ramirez, Gentile 
 Absent: Kaplan, Behar, White, Rivas 

 Public Comment 
 
 • Derrick Dunn, President of Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity, speaks 
 in pro of upcoming legislation regarding the Law School Preparation 
 Council. 

 Opening Announcements 
 
 • Chair Bigenho announces that the meeting will be an interesting one, 
 featuring two confirmations and one bill. He encourages senators to continue reading legislation ahead of time and asking insightful 
 questions. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor expresses gratitude for the committee members 
 being flexible in regard to meeting scheduling. He emphasizes the 
 sentiments presented by Chair Bigenho. 

Old Business 

New Business 
 
 • Senator Macedo motions to unlock the agenda to consider Bill #78-045 
 ahead of Candidate Dave and Candidate Darnell Innocent. 
 • Senator Gentile seconds the motion to unlock the agenda for the 
 purposes outlined by Senator Macedo 
 • The motion passes and the agenda is unlocked. 

• Bill #78-045 
 
 ■ Sponsor Perantoni gives an opening statement encouraging senators to 
 pass Bill #78-045, which will establish the Law School Preparation Council 
 to aid undergraduate students at FSU who intend to pursue graduate 
 studies in the legal field. He explains that the bill has been an ongoing 
 project since May 2026, and has worked closely with various law-related 
 Registered Student Organizations and the FSU Law School. He 
 emphasizes that the bill will create an affiliated project to serve the nearly 
 4,500 pre-law students on campus, many of whom have been academically 
 and professionally underserved by campus programming. Sponsor 
 Perantoni emphasizes that a large goal of the affiliated project is to provide 
 stable and continuous support for pre-law undergraduates at Florida State 
 University, a contrast to the current and fragmented resources available to 
 students. 

 • Sponsor yields with 1:46 for their closing. 
 • Chair Bigenho opens a period of general questioning. 
 • Senator Dominiquez Dambre questions Sponsor Perantoni 
 regarding what events the council plans to host. 
 • Sponsor Perantoni states that the council will partake in service 
 events, disciplinary events at FSU, speaker events, tournaments, 
 LSAT prep events/resources, and other law-related programming. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor asks Sponsor Perantoni to verify that there are 
 no internal elections on the council. 
 • Sponsor Perantoni clarifies that the bill neither prohibits nor 
 establishes internal elections for the council. Initially, members 
 would be selected by the President, but the council would maintain 
 the power to adopt internal policies that created an election system. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor requests that Sponsor Perantoni how 
 membership is going to be monitored within the council. • Sponsor Perantoni states that membership records will be 
 maintained by the Vice Chair of the council. He explains that there 
 are few restrictions on membership, but benefits include resources 
 and access to mailing lists that supply information regarding pre-law 
 organizations, resources, and events on campus. He states that any 
 questions involving how electoral processes may run cannot be 
 answered at the current time, because elections were not something 
 considered in the creation of the bill. 
• Senator Fordham asks Sponsor Perantoni to clarify how 
 undergraduate students would be responsible for undergraduate 
 disciplinary hearing assistance. 
• Sponsor Perantoni clarifies that FSU policy already allows 
 undergraduate students to represent other undergraduates in 
 disciplinary hearings, as long as it is requested by the individual in 
 the hearing, and states that the council will aim to connect those 
 who desire that service to undergraduates willing to provide it. 
• Senator Frazee asks Sponsor Perantoni to elaborate on why this 
 initiative is being introduced as an affiliated project and not a RSO. 
• Sponsor Perantoni states that the initiative is an affiliated project so 
 that administration members can oversee it, and so it is a unifying 
 force between different RSOs, instead of a competing one. 
• Chair Bigenho relinquishes the chair. 
• Vice Chair Gaynor assumes the chair. 
• Senator Bigenho asks Sponsor Perantoni to clarify what makes the 
 council distinctly an affiliated project and not an RSO, specifically 
 because RSOs are still able to have advisors. 
• Sponsor Perantoni states that RSOs are ineligible to receive funding 
 if they have an advisor as a member of their executive board. 
 Because the council is designed to give advisors and law school 
 members formal voting power, surpassing the level of involvement 
 that is typically seen for advisors in RSOs, it is more logical for the 
 initiative to be an affiliated project. 
• Senator Bigenho questions Sponsor Perantoni about how creating 
 the council as an RSO would compete with existing RSOs if there 
 are existing coalitions between similar RSOs in other areas of 
 campus. Continuing, Senator Bigenho asks Sponsor Perantoni to 
 specify where in the RSO handbook the funding barriers are 
 explained. 
• Sponsor Perantoni reiterates that the "advisors" that will sit on the 
 council will have power as a voting entity within proceedings. He 
 explains that the terminology "advisor" comes from the fact that they 
 will be Law School Advisors, but states a willingness to adjust 
 language is necessary. In reference to Senator Bigenho citing 
 COBAL as an RSO centered around bringing a collection of RSOs 
 together, Sponsor Perantoni states that a primary reason for 
 COBALs success is its management by BSU. He states that there 
 are no existing SGA organizations, like a student union, that would 
 neatly house the Law School Preparation Council. 
• Senator Bigenho aks Sponsor Perantoni to clarify what 
 organizations he's met with, and what their general feedback has 
 been. • Sponsor Perantoni clarifies that outreach to each individual 
 organization is logistically difficult, and much of the outreach that 
 has occurred surrounding the bill has been through the President's 
 Council. Though there are no individual statements, the general 
 feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. 
 • Senator Fordham questions Sponsor Perantoni regarding a specific 
 statement in the bill, and whether Student Senate has the power to 
 assign a responsibility to the Assistant Dean of Student Affairs of 
 FSU Law School. 
 • Sponsor Perantoni clarifies that assigning a responsibility to the 
 Assistant Dean is possible as long as the position consents, which is 
 the case regarding Bill #78-045. 
 • Senator Bigenho asks Sponsor Perantoni about who is in 
 President's Council, and if FSU Mock Trial was consulted. 
 • Sponsor Perantoni states that FSU Mock Trial was contacted about 
 the bill, but has not made a substantial comment. 
 • Senator Bigenho motions to move into roundtable discussion. 
 • Senator Frazee seconds the motion to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Senator Gentile speaks in pro of the bill. 
 • Senator Bigenho requests that Sponsor Perantoni edits the cover 
 page prior to Senate Wednesday to include more information 
 regarding campus outreach and structural choices. 
 • Sponsor Perantoni states that he will get as many quotes as he can 
 before the bill makes it to the senate floor, and encourages 
 committee to view line-item edits made to the bill while in Student 
 Life. 
 • Senator Dominiquez Dambre speaks in pro of the bill. 
 • Senator Fordham speaks in pro of the bill. 
 • Senator Macedo motions to call the question. 
 • Senator Bigeno seconds the motion to call the question. 
 • Sponsor Perantoni gives a closing statement thanking the 
 committee for their feedback and providing contact information for 
 those with additional questions or concerns. 

The question is called. 
Chair Gaynor administers roll call and conducts the vote. 
The bill passes in a 8-0-2 vote. 
 
Chair Gaynor relinquishes the chair. 
Senator Bigenho resumes the chair. 

 • Senator Macedo motions to return to the orders of the day. 
 • Senator Fordham seconds the motion. 
 • The motion passes and the committee returns to consider 
 Candidate Dave for the role of Freshman Class Council President. 
 • Vinati Dave - Freshman Class Council - President (Assigned to Internal 
 Affairs, 09.23.2026) (Passed Internal Affairs, 09.28.2026) 
 
 ■ Candidate Dave gives an opening statement imploring senators to confirm 
 her as the President of the Freshman Class Council. 

 • Candidate yields with 0:24 for their closing. 
 • Chair Bigenho opens a period of general questioning. 
 • Senator Macedo motions to allow non-senators to speak. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor seconds the motion to allow non-senators to 
 speak. 
 • Senator Macedo asks the Senior Class Council members present in 
 the meeting what they have to say about the Freshman Class 
 Council candidates. 
 • All Senior Class Council members present at the time of the meeting 
 speak in pro of Candidate Dave and Candidate Darnell Innocent. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor asks Candidate Dave how she plans to build a 
 lasting structure of leadership that serves the Class of 2030. 
 • Candidate Date states that hearing advice and mentorship from 
 upperclassmen class council members will guide her through the 
 position. 
 • Senator Macedo asks Candidate Dave what her primary goal for the 
 school year is. 
 • Candidate Dave states that promoting campus events and 
 resources is her primary goal. 
 • Senator Macedo asks Candidate Dave how Freshman Class 
 Council will differentiate from introductory programming such as an 
 Engage 100 course or Market Wednesday. 
 • Candidate Dave mentions highlighting existing resources and 
 partnering with other organizations with campus will be a focus for 
 class council. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor motions to move into roundtable discussion. 
 • Senator Macedo seconds the motion to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor speaks in pro of Candidate Dave. 
 • Senator Ramirez speaks in pro of Candidate Dave. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor motions to call the question. 
 • Senator Macedo seconds the motion to call the question. 
 • Candidate Dave gives a closing statement thanking the committee 
 for their time and reiterating her passion for serving the Class of 
 2030. 

 The question is called. 
 Vice Chair Gaynor administers the roll call and conducts the vote. 
 The candidate passes in a 8-1-1 vote. 
• Mike Darnell Innocent - Freshman Class Council - Vice President (Assigned 
 to Internal Affairs, 09.23.2026) (Passed Internal Affairs, 09.29.2026) 
 
 ■ Candidate Darnell Innocent gives an opening statement imploring senators 
 to confirm him as the Vice President of Freshman Class Council. • Candidate yields with 0:10 for their closing. 
 • Chair Bigenho opens a period of general questioning. 
 • Senator Macedo asks Candidate Darnell Innocent how he plans to 
 balance potential conflict with the President of Freshman Class 
 Council 
 • Candidate Darnell Innocent states that he plans to resolve potential 
 disagreement with President by consulting advisors and other 
 members of the FCC executive board. 
 • Senator Macedo asks Candidate Darnell how he plans to manage 
 funding with his proposed "social sunday" programming idea. 
 • Candidate Darnell states that he hopes to create events that are as 
 cost-effective as possible, though he is still learning the university 
 policies and structures that govern such programming possibilities. 
 • Senator Macedo motions to move into roundtable discussion. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor seconds the motion to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor speaks in pro of the candidate 
 • Senator Aihe asks Candidate Darnell Innocent how he plans to 
 collaborate with other class councils. 
 • Candidate Darnell Innocent clarifies that he will collaborate with 
 other class councils through all-council meetings and volunteering 
 opportunities for other classes. 
 • Senator Macedo motions to call the question. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor seconds the motion to call the question. 
 • Candidate Darnell Innocent gives a closing statement thanking the 
 committee for their time and reaffirming his desire to serve as 
 FReshman Class Council Vice President. 

 The question is called. 
 Vice Chair Gaynor administers the roll call and conducts the vote. 
 The candidate passes in a 7-1-0 vote. 

Closing Announcements 
 
 • Chair Bigenho thanks the committee for their patience and 
 commitment, and wishes members luck with upcoming exams. He 
 expresses gratitude for Vice Chair Gaynor, welcomes new members to 
 Internal Affairs, and reminds the committee to continue staying 
 engaged in meetings. 
 • Vice Chair Gaynor expresses gratitude for the comittee's patience 
 during his time in Chair and excitement regarding discussions that took 
 place. 

Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 
 • Final roll call is taken. 
 • Senator Macedo motions to adjourn. • Vice Chair Gaynor seconds the motion to adjourn. 

 Meeting adjourned at 7:46 PM

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can.

 Senate Resolution #: 045 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis

 A RESOLUTION 
 Restructuring Forms of Legislation 

 1 WHEREAS, the terms used by the Student Senate to refer to forms of legislation have changed several 
 2 times over the past few Senates; and 
 3 
 4 WHEREAS, if legislative forms were to be referred to more broadly in Rules of Procedure, there would 
 5 be no need to change every section when legislative forms changed; and 
 6 
 7 WHEREAS, referring to legislative forms in a broader term is easier to understand and will make Rules 
 8 of Procedure easier to read; 
 9 
10 NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the 78th Student Senate at Florida State University that: 
11 Rule 5.9 of the Student Senate Rules of Procedure, entitled “Committee Referral,” shall be revised to 
12 read as follows; 
13 
14 The Student Senate President shall refer all bills and constitutional amendments to the appropriate standing 
15 committee for consideration and action, and the Student Senate President may refer any proclamation or 
16 resolution to committee or directly to the calendar for second reading. In the case of a bill legislation being 
17 referred to multiple committees, the committee assignments shall not be bound by a specific sequential 
18 order. The bill legislation must receive approval from all relevant committees, regardless of the order, to be 
19 placed on Second Reading. Each committee shall hear the most recently passed version of the legislation 
20 bill. A bill piece of legislation passing an individual committee shall proceed with any amendments to the 
21 next committee for consideration. Failure of a bill legislation by any assigned committee shall result in the 
22 defeat of the bill legislation and it shall be removed from the Calendar. 

23 a. Any senator can move to appeal a referral by the President and motion for a different or additional 
24 committee to hear the bill legislation or that, in the case of multiple committee assignments, a bill the 
25 legislation not be referred to a specific committee. Such motions require a majority vote to pass. This 
26 provision shall not be interpreted as limiting the Student Senate President's discretion to refer any 
27 measure to any other committees. 
28 b. A senator may also move that a bill legislation on first reading be read in its entirety by the presiding 
29 officer and moved to second reading the same session it is introduced. This motion requires approval 
30 by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senators present. 

 Page 1 of 6 

 Page 3 of 9
31 c. The Student Senate President may refer any resolution to committee(s) or directly to the calendar for 
32 second reading, except for changes to the Rules of Procedure or resolutions commending or 
33 condemning a specific person or group, which must go to the Rules and Calendar Committee. 
34 d. If a bill or resolution piece of legislation is unanimously approved by all of its assigned committees, not 
35 including abstentions, the Student Senate President shall have the discretion to place the legislation 
36 bill or resolution on the Consent Calendar. Constitutional amendments and Major Legislation may not 
37 be placed on the Consent Calendar. 
38 (1) Any Bill allocating or transferring funds from Senate Projects Transfer Bills cannot be 
39 considered on the Consent Calendar. 

40 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that: 

41 Rule 5.15 of the Student Senate Rules of Procedure shall be revised to read as follows; 

42 In the event that the Student Senate President refers any piece of legislation bill, resolution, or constitutional 
43 amendment, in accordance with Rule 5.07 to a committee, failure to call a meeting will result in an absence 
44 for the committee Chair and Vice Chair with the exclusion of breaks and holidays in accordance with the 
45 Florida State University Academic Calendar unless excused by the Student Senate President. 

46 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that: 
47 Rules 8 of the Student Senate Rules of Procedure, entitled “Senate Business,” shall be revised to read 
48 as follows; 

49 1. When in session, the Senate shall meet weekly on Wednesdays. The meeting shall be called to order 
50 at 7:30 p.m. All regularly scheduled meetings of the Student Senate shall be publicly posted or 
51 advertised on the Student Government website. Any such advertisement shall include the time and 
52 place of the Senate meeting. 
53 a. The Senate shall stand adjourned at 11:00 pm. 
54 (1) Any outstanding business shall be tabled at 10:50 p.m. and heard during “Unfinished 
55 Business” in the following Senate meeting. The Senate shall then immediately move 
56 into statements of dissent, advisor announcements, and final roll call, without deviating 
57 from this order. 
58 b. During summer sessions of the Senate, the Student Senate President may be empowered to 
59 call meetings on a biweekly basis. 
60 2. The Student Senate President shall call a special session of the Senate at their discretion or if 
61 requested by a majority vote of the Senate in the form of a petition. All Senators shall be notified of 
62 this special session by the Senate Advisor at least 24 hours prior to the special session being held, 
63 and shall follow the calendar as listed this rule. 
64 a. A petition to call a special session shall include Senators’ names, seats, and FSU IDs. 
65 3. The Calendar shall govern the order of consideration of measures by the Student Senate and shall be 
66 as follows: 
67 a. Call to Order 
68 b. Pledge of Allegiance 
69 c. Moment of Silent Reflection 
70 d. Reading of the Indigenous Land Acknowledgement 
71 e. Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
72 f. Presentations and Awards 
73 g. Public Comments from Students, RSOs, and Members of the Campus Community 
74 h. Messages from SGA Entities 
75 i. Report of Senate Officers 
76 j. Report of the Senate Liaisons 
77 k. Senate Confirmations 
78 l. Consent Calendar 
79 (1) Corrections and Approval of Senate and Committee Follow-up Memos 
80 (2) Report of Remaining Fund Balances 
81 m. Items Pulled from the Consent Calendar 
82 n. Constitutional Amendments 

 Page 4 of 9
 83 o. Legislation on First Reading 
 84 p. Legislation on Second Reading 
 85 q. Unfinished Business 
 86 r. New Business 
 87 s. Statements of Dissent 
 88 t. Closing Announcements 
 89 u. Advisor Announcements 
 90 v. Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 91 4. The Calendar cannot be changed on the Senate floor of a Senate meeting without a motion to Unlock 
 92 the Calendar If objected to, a two-thirds vote is required for the motion to pass. To return to the normal 
 93 agenda, any Senator may move to return to the orders of the day. If objected to, a two-thirds vote is 
 94 required to overturn the motion. 
 95 5. Any legislation resolution, bill, or proclamation, to be included on the calendar of a Senate meeting, 
 96 must be submitted to the Senate Advisor, Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and 
 97 Senate Clerk no later than midnight on the Friday before the Senate meeting. 
 98 6. If a Senator wishes to introduce any legislation bill, resolution, or proclamation for First Reading after 
 99 the submission deadline, it shall require a three-fourths (3/4) vote to be introduced during that Senate 
100 meeting. This Senator must provide a copy of the item to all senators prior to the meeting for the 
101 motion to be considered. 
102 7. The Senate Clerk shall publish the calendar. In their absence, the Senate Advisor shall perform this 
103 duty. 
104 8. The Senate Historian shall record the Journal of the official proceedings of the Senate. In the 
105 Historian’s absence, the Senate President shall have the power to assign this duty. 
106 9. Either the Senate Historian or Advisor shall publish the Senate Journal each week no later than forty-
107 eight hours prior to a regular session of the Senate. Journal entries shall include, but not be limited to: 
108 a. Times of convening and adjournment. 
109 b. A List of Senators present and absent for first roll call. 
110 c. Name of presiding officer(s). 
111 d. Any messages to the Senate from the public or other SGA and university entities. 
112 e. A description of all measures introduced and date of entry. 
113 f. A summary of all committee reports. 
114 g. “Upcoming events” cards. 
115 h. A list of all legislation that has been signed by the Student Senate President and transmitted 
116 to the proper respondent(s) since the previous Senate meeting. 
117 i. Description of any floor amendments or committee amendments offered and their disposition. 
118 j. Any material votes required by the Student Body Constitution, Statutes, or these rules. 
119 k. Any submitted Statements of Dissent. 
120 l. All roll call votes. 
121 m. A list of Senators present and absent for the final roll call. 
122 10. A copy of each bill, resolution, constitutional amendment, and calendar each piece of legislation shall 
123 be provided electronically to each Senator prior to and available at each meeting at which it will be 
124 considered: 
125 a. The management of electronic document distribution shall be assigned to the duties of the 
126 SGA Staff. 
127 b. It shall be the responsibility of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore to display Senate 
128 documents during Senate meetings. 
129 c. A limited amount of printed copies will continue to be made available for guests in the Senate, 
130 the number of which shall be at the discretion of SGA Staff. 
131 11. At their discretion, the Student Senate President may request that students wishing to speak during 
132 the Student and RSO Comments section of the agenda fill out a “Request to Address” card. 
133 12. The Special Introductions portion of Senate meetings shall be reserved time where guests invited at 
134 the discretion of the Student Senate President may address the Senate. Any Senator may move for 
135 other speakers to be permitted, subject to a majority vote. This motion shall be debatable. 
136 13. The presiding officer may call for the Senate to recess for a specified amount of time. This action shall 
137 require a majority vote if objected to by any senator. Any Senator may also make a non-debatable 
138 motion to recess, which shall require a second, and a majority vote for passage if objected to. The 
139 presiding officer shall call the meeting to order at the expiration of the time specified in such a motion. 

 Page 5 of 9
140 14. Upon the completion of all items on the Senate’s Calendar, the presiding officer shall entertain a 
141 motion to adjourn the meeting, which shall require a second and a majority vote for passage if objected 
142 to. 
143 15. Consent Calendar: The presiding officer shall individually read the description of, and entertain 
144 individual motions to approve, each item placed on the Consent Calendar. Any Senator may object to 
145 any legislation bill or resolution being considered on the Consent Calendar without the need the need 
146 for a vote, at which point the legislation bill or resolution shall be considered pulled from the Consent 
147 Calendar. 
148 a. Any legislation bills or resolutions pulled from the Consent Calendar shall be considered in 
149 normal order during Second Reading. 
150 b. If a piece of legislation bill or resolution requires a compulsory recorded vote, or is otherwise 
151 unable to be passed by consent, the Senate shall take a recorded vote after a motion to 
152 approve is made by any Senator, if it is not pulled. 
153 c. Consent Resolutions from the Programming and Resource for Travel Allocations committees 
154 shall not be pulled from the Consent Calendar, and must be heard pursuant to provisions in 
155 Student Body Statutes or these Rules of Procedure. 

156 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that: 
157 Rule Ten of Student Senate Rules of Procedure, entitled “Submission and Consideration of Measures,” 
158 shall be revised to read as follows; 

159 1. Definitions: 
160 a. A "Constitutional Amendment" shall be any measure proposing a change, deletion or addition 
161 to the Student Body Constitution. 
162 b. A "Bill" shall be any measure proposing an amendment to the Student Body Statutes or any 
163 measure appropriating money. 
164 c. A "Resolution" shall be defined as a formal statement/amendment of Senate policy or intent. 
165 d. An "Allocation Resolution" shall be defined as a resolution approving, and allocating funding 
166 recommendations originating from Student Government Association funding boards or 
167 committees established in Student Body Statutes or allocating or transferring Student 
168 Government funds to student organizations through processes expressly authorized by 
169 statute. 
170 e. A "Proclamation" shall be defined as a formal public declaration or official announcement 
171 issued by the Senate to recognize a specific individual, group, event, or cause. 
172 f. An "Amendment" shall be efined as a written document proposing a change to a pending 
173 measure, including a Bill, Resolution, Proclamation, or Constitutional Amendment. 
174 Amendments mist be submitted via the designated Amendment Form. 
175 (1) A "Friendly Amendment" shall be defined as a proposed amendment that is accepted 
176 by the primary sponsor of the measure and receives no objections from the Senate 
177 allowing for its immediate adoption without debate. 
178 g. A "Nomination" shall be the name of any person who has been forwarded to fill a vacant 
179 position in Student Government that requires confirmation by the Senate. 
180 h. “Confirmation” shall be defined as the approval of a nomination by the Senate, in which case 
181 the nominee shall then immediately assume office. 
182 i. “Statement of Dissent” shall be defined as a written explanation expressing disagreement with 
183 any motion, action, or measure made the Senate. 
184 2. Any bill, resolution, or proclamation filed on time shall be drawn up by the Senate Staff and distributed 
185 to members of the Senate via CivicPlus. 
186 3. Any bills affecting Student Government funds which are restrictive shall state all restrictions, earmarks, 
187 stipulations and provisions as part of the proviso of the bill. 
188 4. All appropriations bills must be accompanied by an information form detailing the need for the money, 
189 the specific uses for the money, and alternative methods of funding which have been investigated. 
190 5. All bills, constitutional amendments, resolutions, and proclamations legislation shall include a purpose 
191 and description section detailing a statement of legislative intent cover sheet with the legislation’s 
192 purpose. No bill legislation shall be placed on second reading without a cover sheet statement of 
193 legislative intent. 
194 6. All legislation constitutional amendments, bills, resolutions, and proclamations shall be submitted on 
195 the appropriate forms as designated by the Student Senate President. 

 Page 6 of 9
196 7. Any measure being brought before the Senate for the first time shall be placed on first reading, unless 
197 otherwise moved. 
198 8. Any measure reported out of committee(s) shall be placed on second reading to be heard by the full 
199 Senate at the next meeting. 
200 9. All nominees to Student Government offices requiring Senate confirmation shall have their completed 
201 applications forwarded to the appropriate Senate committee for consideration. The committee shall 
202 interview and question the nominee and then vote on whether to forward or deny them. Following the 
203 vote of the committee, all nominees forwarded by the committee shall be called to the floor of the 
204 Senate at its next meeting. The structure of debate for Senate confirmations shall be as follows: 
205 a. Nominees shall be allowed to give an opening statement lasting no longer than five (5) 
206 minutes, with their remaining time being allocated to their closing. 
207 b. Nominees may be questioned by any Senator on matters of their experience, qualifications, 
208 and goals for the respective position. 
209 c. Upon passage of a motion to enter debate by majority vote, Senators may speak freely as to 
210 the qualifications of any candidate. Nominees shall be permitted to remain in the Senate 
211 Chamber during debate if they so choose. 
212 d. Upon the passage of a motion to call the question on a candidate for confirmation, each 
213 nominee shall have the time remaining from their opening statement to give a closing 
214 statement as to why they should be confirmed. 
215 10. The primary sponsor of any piece of legislation bill, constitutional amendment, or resolution may 
216 withdraw consideration of the document from the Calendar of the Senate at any time without the need 
217 for a formal motion. 
218 a. In the event one or both primary sponsors are unable to present legislation due to extenuating 
219 circumstances, a present cosponsor may be delegated to present subject to the opinion of the 
220 presiding officer. 
221 11. Any amendment to a measure must be submitted via the amendment form hosted by the SGA 
222 Webmaster and must contain the exact language of the proposed amendment including that which 
223 shall be inserted and/or deleted. A direct copy of each submission shall be sent to the Student Senate 
224 President, Student Senate President Pro Tempore, Student Senate Clerk, Student Senate Historian, 
225 Student Senate Parliamentarian, any relevant Standing Committee emails, Senate Program Advisor, 
226 and the Program director of Student Governance and Advocacy. Additionally, a copy of the submission 
227 shall be sent back to the sponsor (submitter). 
228 a. Motions to amend may be made during any round of debate and shall require a second. If the 
229 proposed amendment is germane and receives no objections, the presiding officer shall ask 
230 the primary sponsor if the amendment is favorable. If the sponsor finds the amendment 
231 favorable, the original measure shall be amended, and debate shall proceed on the measure 
232 as amended. 
233 (1) A motion to amend made on the Senate floor must still be submitted to the amendment 
234 form before the adjournment of the meeting, 
235 b. If the motion to amend is objected to or the sponsor does not find the amendment favorable, 
236 debate on the primary measure shall halt and the Senate shall consider the amendment as a 
237 stand-alone measure. The Senator who made the motion to amend shall be considered the 
238 sponsor for purposes of debate. 
239 (1) Debate on the amendment shall not address the merits of the original measure, unless 
240 it is pertinent to the merits of the amendment. Additionally, questions and points of 
241 information should only inquire on the facts of the amendment itself. 
242 c. Unless otherwise specified by the Student Body Constitution or Student Body Statutes, a 
243 motion to amend shall require a majority vote to pass. 
244 d. All amendments that appropriate or transfer funds to organizations that are not part of the 
245 originally submitted bill or allocation resolution must be individually debated on the Senate 
246 floor, regardless if the sponsor accepts them as friendly or unfriendly. 
247 12. The Senate may, at any time following the proper motion, move to committee caucus for the purpose 
248 of expediting the consideration of any measure. A motion to move to committee caucus shall require 
249 a two-thirds vote of the Senate. The Student Senate President, or other presiding officer, shall 
250 reconvene the Senate at the end of the caucus. 
251 13. Any Senator may, at any time, move to meet as a committee of the whole for the purpose of discussing 
252 any Senate business. A motion to convene as a committee of the whole may pass by consent or, if 

 Page 7 of 9
253 objected to, shall require a two-thirds vote of the Senate. A motion to adjourn such a committee 
254 meeting and return to a regular Senate meeting shall require a majority vote. 
255 a. The Student Senate President shall preside over a committee of the whole, unless they choose 
256 to relinquish the Chair. 
257 b. The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall act as the Vice Chair of a committee of the 
258 whole, unless they choose to relinquish their position. 
259 c. When the Senate reconvenes, any senator may move to accept the decision of the committee 
260 as the decision of the whole. 
261 d. Should the Senate enter a committee of the whole, only members of the original committee 
262 who were on the prevailing side of a motion may move for a reconsideration of the vote on the 
263 said motion. 
264 14. Any senator may, during New Business, move to add a Statement of Dissent into the record. 
265 a. The statement must solely address a singular action, motion, or measure made during that 
266 meeting. 
267 b. There may only be one statement submitted per any action, motion, or measure per Senator. 
268 c. Senators who did not make the action, motion, or measure on the floor may cosign the 
269 Statement with the consent of the Senator who made the action, motion, or measure. 
270 d. The statement must be submitted to Senate Staff within two (2) school days following the 
271 meeting of the senate when the action, motion, or measure was made. 
272 15. A resolution proclamation recognizing all Florida State University students that have deceased shall 
273 be heard on the floor of the Senate during the meeting prior to the last Senate meeting of the session, 
274 or “Sine Die.” 
275 a. The list of students will be provided by the SGA Director. 
276 b. This resolution proclamation shall be proposed and advertised one (1) week prior to it being 
277 heard. 
278 c. This resolution proclamation shall be referred to the Student Life Committee after its first 
279 reading and shall be reported out of the committee in one (1) week. 
280 d. No other resolutions recognizing students that have passed shall be considered unless this 
281 rule is waived by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate. 

 DONE AND ADOPTED by the 78th Student Senate at Florida State University this DAY of 
 MONTH, YEAR. 

 SENATE VOTE: Senate Clerk to Add Vote Count 

 COMMITTEE REFERENCES AND DATES OF PASSAGE: 
  Senate Clerk to Add Committee References and Dates of Passage 

 By: ____________________________ 
 Alexia Holliday 
 Student Senate President 
 
 Date: _____________________________ 

 Page 8 of 9

 78th STUDENT SENATE 
 Legislation Cover Sheet 

 Senate Resolution #: 045 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis 
 Co-sponsor(s): Holliday, Torres, Rivas, Perantoni 

Short Title: Restructuring Forms of Legislation Resolution 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This Resolution removes specific reference to legislation forms and instead refers to them as 
“legislation.” This is to ensure that if legislation forms change in the future, Senate Rules of 
Procedure don’t need to be largely altered to reflect the given changes. 
 
Background Information: 
Due to recent clarifications regarding forms of legislation, it was decided to reclarify how legislation 
should be referred to in Senate Rules of Procedure. Because of this, an agreement was made to refer 
to forms of legislation broadly in order to prevent large alterations of Senate Rules of Procedure, should 
forms of legislation once again change. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
This legislation was written in correspondence and discussion with the Senate President, to reaffirm the 
language being used and replaced. 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation will prevent large changes to Senate Rules of Procedure every time a change is made 
to legislative forms, as we’ve seen increased alterations of in the past few Senates. All lists of types of 
legislation will be shortened to “legislation” and singular references to a legislative type will be amended 
to “piece of legislation” in order to ensure these desired effects. 
 
Attachment(s): 
Attachment #1: Proposed Resolution

 AN ACT 

 To Create SGA Grant Programs 

 1 Be it enacted by the 78th Student Senate at Florida State University that: 

 2 Section 1. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 309, “Student Government 
 3 Grants”. 

 4 Section 309 of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, entitled “Student Government Grant” 
 5 is hereby amended to read as follows: 

 6 1. Purpose: The Student Government at Florida State University, seeing the distinct need to 
 7 support student success and deliver back student monies to the student body, creates this 
 8 statute to govern the proper management of grants listed within this title. 
 9 2. Governing Structure: All grants shall be officially managed by the Office of the Treasurer, 
10 with disbursement to be coordinated between the Treasurer and the SGA Business 
11 Manager. The Student Senate shall be responsible for hearing grant funding requests yearly 
12 during the budget process, and allocating yearly block grants to be further distributed by 
13 the Office of the Treasurer. 
14 a. The Senate shall adopt a policy pursuant to Chapter 416 governing the proper 
15 allocation of block grants for each grant listed in this Chapter.

Short Title: Creating Student Government Grant Programs 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 309 of the Student Body Statutes to establish a structure for Student 
Government grant programs. It would create the John Thrasher Textbook Grant and the Warren Mazek 
Internship Housing Grant to provide financial support for qualifying student expenses. 
 
Background Information: 
This legislation is being presented to create a formal process for Student Government to provide grant 
funding directly toward student expenses. The proposed programs would initially focus on two areas: 
textbook costs and housing costs associated with qualifying summer internships. 
 
Under the proposed structure, the Student Senate would determine funding for each grant through the 
annual budget process. The Office of the Treasurer, in coordination with the SGA Business Manager, 
would then oversee the administration and distribution of those funds. This structure allows Student 
Government to support student success while maintaining Senate oversight of the amount allocated to 
each program. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, Deputy Student Body Treasurer 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would create two Student Government grant programs. The John Thrasher 
Textbook Grant would allow FSU students to receive up to $200 per fiscal year toward textbook 
purchases through Bill's Bookstore. The Warren Mazek Internship Housing Grant would provide eligible 
students participating in qualifying summer internships with $1,000 toward housing costs. The 
programs would be administered by the Office of the Treasurer, with funding determined annually by 
the Student Senate.

Short Title: To Establish the Law School Preparation Council 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a new Affiliated Project between 
SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-
law students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning about the law, with the resources 
available from the SGA, Pre-law advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 
Background Information: 
FSU ranks within the top 10 of undergraduate feeder institutions for Law School, producing a large pool 
of applicants to Law Schools across the United States. Despite this, overall support for pre-law 
programming and development across the University is low. The FSU Law School and Pre-Law team 
recognized this, attempting to launch more programming for these groups in the Fall semester. To 
compliment this programming, this legislation aims to work with these campus partners to support the 
success of pre-law students across the University. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Legislative consultation included the former Law School Council (funding board) Chair, SGA Advising, 
Pre-Law advising, the Pre-Law President’s council, Phi Alpha Delta, Prep and Conquer, Lex et Lux 
Society, Black Future Attorneys, Hispanic Future Attorneys, Chair of Judiciary, and the FSU Law 
School. The sponsors additionally held a Townhall on this legislation, inviting the opinions of pre-law 
students, and heavily advertised this to the student body, receiving large amounts of support across the 
pre-law sphere. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would create a new Affiliated Project to support the pre-law sphere at FSU, focusing on 
uplifting and aiding RSOs, Pre-Law and Law School admin, and supporting success of students 
entering law school.

Short Title: Awarding the FSU Marching Chiefs with the Student Senate Award for Excellence 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This resolution recognizes the extraordinary work of the FSU Marching Chiefs and their directors: 
Patrick Dunnigan, David Plack, and Devan L. Moore. This resolution acknowledges the historical 
significance as the FSU Marching Chiefs will be the first collegiate university from Florida to be invited 
to perform in the 2027 Macy's Thanksgiving Parade. 
 
Background Information: 
This resolution and this award recognize the extraordinary achievements of the FSU Marching 
Chiefs, directors, and other related contributors to the program in being invited to the highly 
distinguished 101st Macy's Thanksgiving parade. This celebrates the Florida State Marching Chiefs 
being the first collegiate marching band from Florida selected to perform in the parade. The Macy's 
thanksgiving parade generates over 30 million viewers from across the globe for its historically beloved 
performance that has existed since 1924. Over 400 marching chiefs will attend the parade, 
representing FSU on a global platform; however, this is not the first time the Marching Chiefs have 
represented FSU on a global platform. The marching chiefs have famously performed in Syria, Jordan, 
England, France, and Ireland; they have continued their reputation for excellence with their cordial 
invite to the prestigious Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. 

Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 

Outreach with Senate leadership, and directors Patrick Dunnigan, David Plack, and Devan L. Moore 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This resolution would award the FSU Marching Chiefs as a collective the highly esteemed Student 
Senate Award for Excellence. It will highlight the hard work and dedication of all staff, students, and 
alumni who have played an active and significant role in the media attention and positive reputation of 
Florida State. This resolution will also show appreciation to the graduating Marching Chief students 
who have dedicated their collegiate careers towards this organization and are graduating into the next 
phase of their lives before the 2027 Macy's Thanksgiving Parade performance.

sections.text:
THE SEVENTY-EIGHTH STUDENT SENATE 
 Calendar: September 23, 2026 
 Location: Senate Chambers 
 Time: 7:30 PM 
 Submit Public Comment Here 

 Call to Order 

 Pledge of Allegiance 

 Moment of Silent Reflection 
Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 

 Presentations and Awards 
 • Civil Rights Institute Presentation 

 • CAPS Presentation 

 Public Comments from Students, RSOs, and Members of the Campus Community 
 • Public Comment #001

 (Assigned to Internal Affairs, 09.09.26) (Tabled in Internal Affairs 
 09.14.2026)

 09.09.2026) (Tabled in Finance, 09.15.2026, 09.22.2026)

 (Passed Judiciary, 09.22.2026)

 09.16.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 09.22.2026)

 (Passed Judiciary, 09.22.2026)

 Affairs, 09.23.2026) 

 • Mike Darnell Innocent - Freshman Class Council - Vice President 
 (Assigned to Internal Affairs, 09.23.2026) 

 • Andrew Kiffel - Senate- COSSP Seat 5 (Assigned to Rules, 09.23.2026) 

 • Candidates Forwarded from the SGA Judicial Branch

 Judiciary, 09.22.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 09.22.2026) 

 • Luke Dratch – Deputy Supervisor of Elections (Assigned to Judiciary, 
 09.22.2026) (Tabled in Judiciary, 09.22.2026) 

 Consent Calendar 
 • Corrections and Approval of Senate and Committee Minutes 

 • Remaining Balances (Attached) 

CPC Question Sponsored by 
Memo (Placed 
on Consent 
Calendar per 
SBS 
§705.4(d)) 

 Items Pulled from the Consent Calendar 

 Constitutional Amendments Legislation on First Reading 
Bill #78-044 Sponsored by Collin Mungall, Riley Perantoni 
 This bill would amend Chapter 309 of the Student Body Statutes to 
 establish a structure for Student Government grant programs. It 
 would create the John Thrasher Textbook Grant and the Warren 
 Mazek Internship Housing Grant to provide financial support for 
 qualifying student expenses. (Assigned to Judiciary, Finance, 
 Student Life, 09.23.2026) 

Bill #78-045 Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, Enock Nturubika 
 This legislation would create the Law School Preparation Council, a 
 new Affiliated Project between SGA, FSU’s Law School, and Pre-law 
 advisors. The goal of this Council is to support and connect pre-law 
 students, those interested in law, or those curious about learning 
 about the law, with the resources available from the SGA, Pre-law 
 advising and RSOs, and the Law School. This bill would establish a 
 governing structure for the Affiliated Project and operational goals. 
 (Assigned to Judiciary, Finance, Internal Affairs, Student Life, 
 09.23.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Sophia Torres 
#78-046 This resolution recognizes the extraordinary work of the FSU 
 Marching Chiefs and their directors: Patrick Dunnigan, David Plack, 
 and Devan L. Moore. This resolution acknowledges the historical 
 significance as the FSU Marching Chiefs will be the first collegiate 
 university from Florida to be invited to perform in the 2027 Macy's 
 Thanksgiving Parade. (Assigned to Student Life, 09.23.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis 
#78-045 This Resolution removes specific reference to legislation forms and 
 instead refers to them as “legislation.” This is to ensure that if 
 legislation forms change in the future, Senate Rules of Procedure 
 don’t need to be largely altered to reflect the given changes. 
 (Assigned to Rules, 09.23.2026) 

Bill #78-046 Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis 
 This Bill removes specific reference to legislation forms and instead 
 refers to them as “legislation.” This is to ensure that if legislation 
 forms change in the future, Student Body Statutes don’t need to be 
 largely altered to reflect the given changes. (Assigned to Judiciary, 
 09.23.2026) 

 Legislation on Second Reading 
Allocation Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, James Tizon 
Resolution This resolution proposes the allocation of $7,635.09 to four RSOs 
#78-012 who requested funding from the RSOAC. (Placed on Second 
 Reading by Senate President pursuant to SBS § 812.5(d), 
 09.23.2026) Proclamation Sponsored by Vanessa Aihe 
#78-018 This proclamation serves to memorialize and celebrate the awards, 
 honors, and responsibilities given to our student representatives that 
 attended the National Association of Colleges and Universities’ 
 (NACURH) 2026 conference. Specific details about the awards given 
 are mentioned in the legislation. (Assigned to Student Life, 
 09.16.2026) (Passed Student Life, 09.17.2026) 

Proclamation Sponsored by Enock Nturubika 
#78-020 This proclamation recognizes the 250th Anniversary of American 
 Independence as an opportunity to reflect on the nation's ongoing 
 pursuit of civil rights while honoring Florida State University's civil 
 rights legacy and the contributions of the Civil Rights Institute. It 
 asserts the Student Senate's commitment to promoting civic 
 engagement, historical education, equal opportunity, and continued 
 student participation in programs and initiatives that preserve and 
 advance civil rights for all members of the FSU community. 
 (Assigned to Student Life, 09.16.2026) (Passed Student Life, 
 09.17.2026) 

Bill #78-043 Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, Morgan Gurtis 
 This legislation would do two main things: first, make it so elected 
 RSOAC members term out, and disband elected positions on 
 December 1st; second, make it so the Fall election will not have 
 election for elected RSOAC Commissioners. (Assigned to Finance, 
 Judiciary, 09.16.2026) (Passed Finance, Judiciary, 09.22.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis, Alexia Holliday 
#78-044 This resolution restructures Rule Nine of Rules of Procedure to move 
 Statements of Dissent under New Business, and Rule Ten to update 
 Senate debate procedures. These procedural changes will set a 
 maximum time for debate and integrate Robert’s Rules of Order 
 more clearly. (Assigned to Rules, 09.16.2026) (Passed Rules, 
 09.18.2026) 

Proclamation Sponsored by Janet Rodriguez-Garcia, Angela Rico 
#78-019 This proclamation seeks to recognize September as Suicide 
 Prevention Month and aims to increase awareness of suicide 
 prevention. It highlights the importance of encouraging students to 
 engage in conversations surrounding mental health, reduce stigma 
 associated with seeking mental-health support, and promotes 
 awareness of resources available to students who may be 
 experiencing suicidal thoughts, supporting someone in crisis, or 
 grieving the loss of someone to suicide. The legislation further 
 addresses the need to foster a supportive campus community in 
 which students feel connected and empowered to seek assistance 
 when needed. (Assigned to Student Life, 09.16.2026) (Passed 
 Student Life, 09.17.2026) New Business 

Statements of Dissent 

Closing Announcements 
• Service with Senate - September 24th, 10:00AM to 1:00PM, Kearney Center 
 Volunteering - 10 Slots 

• UF Tour - October 20th (Tentative) 

• T-Shirts and Tote Bags Soon 

Advisor Announcements 

Final Roll Call and Adjournment

11 travel opportunities, and other initiatives. Funding is available on a first-come, first-served basis and 
12 is contingent upon the availability of funds. The RSOAC shall be recognized as a Funding Board of 
13 the Student Senate and shall be considered an entity of the Senate solely for purposes of 
14 administrative function, including but not limited to Senate Leadership oversight, the ability of Senate 
15 Leadership to attend meetings as voting ex officio, attendance and meeting minutes, and other 
16 related procedural or administrative matters. 

17 2. Committee Structure 

18 a. The RSOAC shall be comprised of seventeen (17) twelve (12) voting student members: 
19 

20 (1) The Chair and Vice Chair of the Student Senate Finance Committee; 

21 (2) Two (2) additional Senators appointed by the Student Senate President; 

22 (3) Five (5) students-at-large elected during the Fall SGA elections, pursuant to Section 
23 13 of this Chapter; 

24 (4) Two (2) students-at-large designated by the Student Body President; 

25 (5) Four (4) students-at-large designated by the Student Body Treasurer; 

26 (6) One (1) member-elect of the Campus Recreation Board designated by the outgoing 
27 Chair of the Campus Recreation Board; 

28 (7) One (1) member of the Union Board designated by the Chair of the Union Board. 

29 b. All appointments to the RSOAC shall be financially certified prior to being a voting member of 
30 the committee. 

31 c. Committee appointments should be made and designated by the appropriate entity before 
32 the annual Fall SGA Inauguration. 

33 d. Committee members shall serve a one-year term beginning and ending with the Fall SGA 
34 Inauguration. 

35 e. Committee members must meet the enrollment requirements provided in §100.6. 

36 f. Committee members are subject to the requirements of Chapter 205, Student Body Statutes 
37 (the SGA Code of Ethics) including the requirement to avoid conflicts of interest. As such, 
38 committee members are required to abstain from voting on any funding recommendation that 
39 would benefit an organization of which they are a member or affiliated within any capacity. 

 Page 4 of 15
40 g. Following the certification of Fall SGA election results and prior to the Fall Senate 
41 organizational meeting, an organizational meeting of the RSO Allocation Committee shall be 
42 convened. This meeting shall be scheduled and hosted by outgoing Senate Leadership. 
43 During this meeting, the committee shall: 

44 (1) Receive a joint training session conducted by SGA Accounting and the Office of 
45 Student Organizations and Involvement, covering financial procedures, RSO 
46 eligibility, and committee responsibilities. The outgoing Chair and Vice Chair of the 
47 RSO Allocation Committee shall be invited to assist with the training and help 
48 transition the new committee; and 

49 (2) Elect a Chair and Vice Chair from all members of the committee. 

50 (3) Review the most recent annual evaluation of the RSOAC program prepared by the 
51 Student Body Treasurer, as required by Section 11 of this Chapter, in order to 
52 understand past performance, challenges, and recommendations for program 
53 improvement. 

54 3. Leadership 

55 a. Committee leadership elections shall occur during the organizational meeting held following 
56 Fall elections and prior to the Fall SGA Inauguration, as outlined in Section 2(g). 

57 b. Committee leadership elections shall follow the procedures in §400.7, Student Body Statutes 
58 and Rule 5.5 of the Senate Rules of Procedure. 

59 c. The Chair of the RSOAC may not simultaneously serve as Chair or Vice Chair of another 
60 SGA committee or entity. 

61 d. The Chair or Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee may be removed by either: The 
62 Student Senate President, for cause, with written notice to the committee and the Senate 
63 President Pro Tempore; or a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the voting members of the RSO 
64 Allocation Committee. 

65 (1) Upon removal of the Chair or Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee, or if a 
66 vacancy otherwise occurs, the committee shall, at its next regular meeting, elect a 
67 replacement from among its members by majority vote, subject to confirmation of 
68 eligibility. 

69 (2) The Student Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore shall be notified 
70 within two (2) business days of any vacancy or replacement election. 

71 e. Duties of the Vice Chair 

72 (1) The Vice Chair shall be responsible for recording and maintaining official minutes of 
73 all RSO Allocation Committee meetings. 

74 (2) The Vice Chair shall publish and transmit all minutes to the Student Senate 
75 President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Historian and ensure their 
76 publication within the timeframe required. 

77 (3) The Vice Chair shall be responsible for the collection and maintenance of scoring 
78 materials and administration of the committee’s evaluation rubric during meetings, 
79 ensuring that all votes and scores are properly documented and retained. 

80 f. Duties of the Chair 

 Page 5 of 15
 81 (1) The Chair shall serve as the chief point of communication between the RSO 
 82 Allocation Committee, all Registered Student Organizations, and the Student Senate. 

 83 (2) The Chair shall coordinate with the SGA Accounting Office and the Office of Student 
 84 Organizations & Involvement to provide timely notice of funding outcomes and 
 85 committee decisions to all applicants. 

 86 g. Joint Responsibilities 

 87 (1) The Chair and Vice Chair shall be jointly responsible for preparing and publishing the 
 88 agenda of each RSO Allocation Committee meeting. 

 89 (2) The agenda shall include all funding requests scheduled for consideration, relevant 
 90 documentation, and any items of general business, and must be distributed in 
 91 accordance with this Chapter and Chapter 203 of the Student Body Statutes. 

 92 4. Committee Operations 

 93 a. Quorum shall consist of at least five (5) seven (7) members. 

 94 b. The committee shall establish a regular, weekly meeting schedule and must meet on 
 95 Thursdays, and shall have a meeting end time of no later than 10:00 PM ET. However, the 
 96 time of conclusion may be waived by a 2/3 vote of the committee. 

 97 c. Funding requests must be submitted no later than 12:00 PM ET (noon) on the Monday prior 
 98 to the Thursday meeting at which they will be considered. 

 99 d. Requests submitted after the Monday deadline shall be scheduled for the following week’s 
100 meeting unless otherwise approved by the Chair. 

101 e. All funding requests shall be reviewed by the SGA Accounting Office for authenticity in RSO 
102 registration status prior being forwarded to the Chair of the RSOAC. The SGA Accounting 
103 Office retains decision making authority in regards to the validity of all requests submitted to 
104 the RSOAC. 

105 f. The agenda for each Thursday meeting shall be distributed to committee members and 
106 sponsoring RSOs by Tuesday at 5:00 PM. 

107 g. The Vice Chair shall maintain an attendance log for all scheduled meetings of the RSOAC. 
108 This log shall be transmitted to the Senate President Pro Tempore and posted with the 
109 committee minutes. 

110 (1) An absence means failure to attend a noticed meeting of the RSOAC. 

111 (2) An excused absence may be granted by the Chair for circumstances including, but 
112 not limited to, academic obligations, documented illness, religious observances, 
113 University-sponsored activities, or emergencies. Members shall notify the Chair as 
114 soon as practicable and, when feasible, at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance. 

115 (3) Unexcused absence means any absence not excused under 4(g)(2). 

116 (4) Upon a third (3rd) unexcused absence within a member’s one-year term, an elected 
117 student-at-large member shall be immediately suspended from the RSOAC and the 
118 matter shall be forwarded to the Senate Rules Committee within two (2) business 
119 days. The suspended member shall not be counted toward quorum and shall not 
120 vote pending disposition. 

 Page 6 of 15
121 (5) The Senate Rules Committee shall apply the same process used for Student 
122 Senators regarding attendance and fitness to serve. If the Rules Committee finds 
123 that the individual cannot continue to serve in their capacity, it shall recommend 
124 impeachment to the Senate Judiciary Committee. The Rules Committee may, by 
125 majority vote and upon written justification of extraordinary circumstances, grant 
126 additional excused absences or a one-time waiver not to exceed two (2) additional 
127 absences for the remainder of the term. Any waiver granted shall be reported to the 
128 Senate at the next regular meeting. 

129 (6) If any designated representative of an entity accrues more than three (3) unexcused 
130 absences within their term, the representative shall be removed from the RSOAC, 
131 and the Chair shall request a new designee from the designating authority. The 
132 designating authority may, at their discretion, decide to redesignate the same 
133 individual. If a replacement is not named within five (5) business days of notice, the 
134 seat shall remain vacant until filled and shall not count toward quorum while vacant. 

135 (7) Absences accumulate per term of service (from Fall Inauguration to the subsequent

137 Suspended or removed members within this Chapter do not count toward quorum 
138 during suspension or after removal.to regularly noticed RSOAC meetings. 

139 5. Funding Recommendation Process 

140 a. The Student Senate shall retain final authority over the approval of all RSOAC funding 
141 recommendations. 

142 b. Funding recommendations made by the RSO Allocation Committee shall be transmitted to 
143 the Student Senate in the form of an allocation resolution sponsored by the Chair and Vice

145 RSOAC. 

146 c. Allocation Resolutions must be submitted by the Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee via 
147 the Senate Legislation Submission form no later than 11:59 PM ET (midnight) on the Friday 
148 following the Thursday RSOAC meeting, to be included on the next week’s Senate agenda 
149 with all other legislation. 

150 d. Allocation Resolutions shall be placed on the agenda for the following Wednesday Senate 
151 meeting. The Senate President shall have the discretion to place these resolutions on either 
152 the Consent portion or the Second Reading portion of the agenda. 

153 e. Before any allocation resolution may be amended, a motion to open the allocation resolution 
154 must be made and agreed to by a simple majority, which shall be followed by an opening 
155 and debate. Upon adoption of such motion by a two-thirds (2/3) roll-call vote, individual 
156 amendments may then be entertained. Each amendment shall require a separate motion, 
157 debate, and two-thirds roll-call vote. However, the Student Senate shall not increase funding 
158 for any Registered Student Organization that the RSO Allocation Committee voted to 
159 recommend zero funding for. 

160 (1) All adopted amendments must be documented and emailed to the Senate Clerk, 
161 Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Historian within one 
162 (1) hour of the conclusion of the meeting by the amendment’s sponsor. 

163 (2) Amendments to Allocation Resolutions may be submitted in advance of the meeting 
164 to the Senate President and Senate Clerk to be listed on the agenda. 

165 6. Eligibility Criteria for Student Organizations 
166 

 Page 7 of 15
167 a. All organizations applying for funding must be currently registered with the Office of Student 
168 Organizations & Involvement and in good conduct standing with Florida State University. 

169 b. Student organizations may not receive funding from the RSO Allocation Committee if they 
170 have also received funds from the College Leadership Council Funding Board, the Sport 
171 Club Distribution Council, or line-item funding in the annual SGA budget in the same fiscal 
172 year. 

173 7. Funding Guidelines and Restrictions 

174 a. All requests must be for eligible uses of Student Activity & Service Fee revenues, as 
175 provided in the SGA Financial Manual. 

176 b. The Student Body Treasurer shall coordinate with the Department of Student Engagement to 
177 establish an online system for submitting funding requests. 

178 c. Funding requests shall generally be required to include a description of the intended use of 
179 funds and why the requested funding is needed. Student organizations shall be required to 
180 provide an estimate of the number of FSU students that are likely to attend an event or travel 
181 opportunity funded by SGA. 

182 d. Pursuant to §1009.24, Florida Statutes, SGA funding may only be used to benefit the student 
183 body in general. As such, funding from the RSO Allocation Committee may not benefit 
184 activities for which an admission fee is charged to students. Further, student organizations 
185 that charge membership fees may not exclude any student from participation in any events 
186 or programs funded by SGA as a result of a student’s inability to pay such fees. 

187 e. Funds may not be used to cover membership dues or fees associated with a student’s or 
188 organization’s national or international affiliations. 

189 f. The committee shall not recommend funding for events or programs that are likely to have 
190 only group members attend and/or have no general benefit to the student body. 

191 g. The committee shall not recommend funding for events that are exclusive to a club or 
192 organization’s executive board. 

193 h. Requests for clothing may only be approved once per fiscal year. Any clothing funded by 
194 SGA must directly promote the student organization. 

195 i. Organizations seeking funding for service trips must first demonstrate that they made a 
196 good-faith effort to participate in an open or public service opportunity offered by the Center 
197 for Leadership and Service, if such an opportunity was available. If participation in such a trip 
198 was not feasible due to scheduling, availability, or capacity, the organization may pursue 
199 independent service trip funding through the RSO Allocation Committee. In such cases, 
200 documentation of the organization’s outreach to CLS and explanation of why participation in 
201 a CLS-facilitated trip was not possible must be provided with the funding request. 

202 j. Student organizations shall submit their request prior to the RSOAC meeting via a recording 
203 of their presentation, ideally with a slideshow to assist their request. 

204 (1) The presentation's recording may not be longer than 7 minutes, and must detail the 
205 specifics about their request for the full awareness of the SROAC membership. 

206 (2) Time may be designated at the discretion of the Chair of the RSOAC to watch these 
207 pre-submitted presentations during the meeting, or members may be required to 
208 watch these presentations prior to the meeting. 

 Page 8 of 15
209 (3) All video presentations must be submitted alongside the organization's application to 
210 the RSOAC. 

211 (4) A representative of the Student Organization must attend the RSOAC meeting they 
212 will be considered in, for the purposes of answering questions about the 
213 presentation. 
214 

215 (A) If there are no representatives from the organization, the request will be 
216 tabled. 

217 (B) If, at the next meeting of the RSOAC, there is no attending representative, 
218 the request shall be zero funded. 

219 8. Funding Limits 

220 a. Travel 

221 (1) Maximum of $250 per student. 

222 b. Annual Cap per Organizations 

223 (1) No organization may receive more than 3.5% of the total budget allocated to the 
224 RSOAC in the annual budget process during a single fiscal year, regardless of the

226 (2) For purposes of this section, “total funding” includes all allocations for travel, events, 
227 programming, or any other expenditures recommended by the RSO Allocation 
228 Committee and approved by the Student Senate. 

229 c. Single Allocation Rule 

230 (1) An organization may not receive funding for more than one (1) request within the 
231 same allocation resolution transmitted to the Student Senate. 

232 d. The Committee shall have discretion to recommend that the Student Senate exceed the 
233 funding limit for Travel or Events/Programming with the usage of Senate Projects funding, 
234 said recommendation shall be listed in the scoring rubrics “Evaluator Notes” section. 

235 9. Funding Allocation Schedule 

236 a. In order to comply with University purchasing and travel guidelines, of the funding allocated 
237 to the RSO Allocation Committee in the annual SGA budget: 

238 (1) 5% shall be available for allocation beginning July 1 each year through the end of the 
239 Summer semester; 

240 (2) 47.5% shall be available for allocation in the Fall semester, in addition to any 
241 unexpended funds from earlier in the fiscal year; and 

242 (3) 47.5% shall be available in the Spring semester, in addition to any unexpended funds 
243 from earlier in the fiscal year. 

244 b. All final funding allocations must be approved by the Student Senate at least 30 calendar 
245 days before the event or travel is to take place.

246 c. In addition to the requirement above, funding for events or travel scheduled during the 
247 months of May or June must be approved by the Student Senate before the conclusion of 
248 the Spring semester. There shall be no exceptions to this requirement, which is needed in 
249 order to maintain compliance with the University’s fiscal year-end closeout procedures. 

250 10. Post-Award Requirements 

251 a. All events funded by SGA must be publicly advertised on the University-designated student 
252 organization management platform in a manner visible to the general student body. This 
253 shall serve as the baseline standard for public advertisement. Additional promotion through 
254 means such as social media, digital signage, newsletters, or tabling is encouraged but not 
255 required. 

256 b. Any events, programs, travel, or other activities supported by SGA funding must comply with 
257 the FSU Student Organization Conduct Code as well as all federal, state, and local laws. 

258 c. Every organization receiving funding from SGA must submit a post event evaluation form, 
259 along with receipts for any purchases made, to the SGA Accounting Office, within ten (10) 
260 business days following the event. 

261 d. If the requirements above are not followed by an organization, they shall be barred from 
262 requesting any further funding until their post-award violations are rectified with SGA 
263 accounting. 

264 11. Annual Review Requirement 

265 a. No later than the end of the Fall semester each year, the Student Body Treasurer shall 
266 conduct an evaluation of the RSOAC program. This review shall assess the overall 
267 effectiveness of the program and identify any areas for potential improvement. 

268 b. This evaluation shall include: 

269 (1) The number and nature of instances in which standard funding rules or limits were 
270 waived; 

271 (2) An analysis of how such waivers impacted student organizations and the broader 
272 student body; 

273 (3) The adequacy of the current funding level for the program; 

274 (4) Recommendations for enhancing the program’s structure, parameters, and allocation 
275 limits; and 

276 (5) A breakdown of the number and types of organizations that receive funding, 
277 including both organizational status (USSO, ASO, GSO) and programmatic category 
278 (e.g. academic, cultural, special interest, political, community service). 

279 c. Following the evaluation, the Student Body Treasurer shall prepare a report of findings and 
280 recommendations. This report shall be submitted to the Student Senate Budget Committee 
281 during the annual SGA budget planning cycle.

 78th STUDENT SENATE 
 Legislation Cover Sheet 

 Senate Bill #: 043 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Perantoni, Gurtis 
 Co-sponsor(s): Rodriguez, Bigenho 

Short Title: To Change Elected Members of RSOAC 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would do two main things: first, make it so elected RSOAC members term out, and 
disband elected positions on December 1st; second, make it so the Fall election will not have election 
for elected RSOAC Commissioners. 
 
Background Information: 
This legislation comes together with a larger RSOAC Committee reform underway between the Senate, 
Executive, and Advisors, focusing on transferring general responsibility for initial allocations from the 
Committee to the office of the Treasurer. This section is being proposed first for the fact that the Fall 
Election is considering elected RSOAC Members, and we want to make it clear prior to the elections of 
this change to elected membership. This allows the larger reform bill to continue to be revised and 
workshopped whilst the Senate makes clear what we are working on with RSOAC Membership. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
RSOAC Leadership, Treasury, Finance, Internal Affairs, Judiciary, Elections Office. All legislative 
consultants (besides elections) are additionally on with the larger reform. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would remove elected members on RSOAC on inauguration, and the legislation would 
have these positions not have to go through the election process this Fall.

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can.
