 AN ACT 

 To Change Elected Members of RSOAC 

1 Be it enacted by the 78th Student Senate at Florida State University that: 

 Page 1 of 12 

 Page 3 of 15
 2 Section 1. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 812, “RSO Allocation 
 3 Committee”. 

 4 Section 812 of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, entitled “RSO Allocation Committee” 
 5 is hereby established to read as follows: 

 6 Chapter 812 RSO Allocation Committee (RSOAC) 

 7 1. Purpose: The Registered Student Organization Allocation Committee (RSOAC) shall be responsible 
 8 for reviewing and recommending funding allocations in support of Registered Student Organizations 
 9 (RSOs) that meet established eligibility requirements. This program is designed to assist RSOs in 
10 carrying out their missions and enhancing campus life through student-led programming, events, 
11 travel opportunities, and other initiatives. Funding is available on a first-come, first-served basis and 
12 is contingent upon the availability of funds. The RSOAC shall be recognized as a Funding Board of 
13 the Student Senate and shall be considered an entity of the Senate solely for purposes of 
14 administrative function, including but not limited to Senate Leadership oversight, the ability of Senate 
15 Leadership to attend meetings as voting ex officio, attendance and meeting minutes, and other 
16 related procedural or administrative matters. 

17 2. Committee Structure 

18 a. The RSOAC shall be comprised of seventeen (17) twelve (12) voting student members: 
19 

20 (1) The Chair and Vice Chair of the Student Senate Finance Committee; 

21 (2) Two (2) additional Senators appointed by the Student Senate President; 

22 (3) Five (5) students-at-large elected during the Fall SGA elections, pursuant to Section 
23 13 of this Chapter; 

24 (4) Two (2) students-at-large designated by the Student Body President; 

25 (5) Four (4) students-at-large designated by the Student Body Treasurer; 

26 (6) One (1) member-elect of the Campus Recreation Board designated by the outgoing 
27 Chair of the Campus Recreation Board; 

28 (7) One (1) member of the Union Board designated by the Chair of the Union Board. 

29 b. All appointments to the RSOAC shall be financially certified prior to being a voting member of 
30 the committee. 

31 c. Committee appointments should be made and designated by the appropriate entity before 
32 the annual Fall SGA Inauguration. 

33 d. Committee members shall serve a one-year term beginning and ending with the Fall SGA 
34 Inauguration. 

35 e. Committee members must meet the enrollment requirements provided in §100.6. 

36 f. Committee members are subject to the requirements of Chapter 205, Student Body Statutes 
37 (the SGA Code of Ethics) including the requirement to avoid conflicts of interest. As such, 
38 committee members are required to abstain from voting on any funding recommendation that 
39 would benefit an organization of which they are a member or affiliated within any capacity. 

 Page 4 of 15
40 g. Following the certification of Fall SGA election results and prior to the Fall Senate 
41 organizational meeting, an organizational meeting of the RSO Allocation Committee shall be 
42 convened. This meeting shall be scheduled and hosted by outgoing Senate Leadership. 
43 During this meeting, the committee shall: 

44 (1) Receive a joint training session conducted by SGA Accounting and the Office of 
45 Student Organizations and Involvement, covering financial procedures, RSO 
46 eligibility, and committee responsibilities. The outgoing Chair and Vice Chair of the 
47 RSO Allocation Committee shall be invited to assist with the training and help 
48 transition the new committee; and 

49 (2) Elect a Chair and Vice Chair from all members of the committee. 

50 (3) Review the most recent annual evaluation of the RSOAC program prepared by the 
51 Student Body Treasurer, as required by Section 11 of this Chapter, in order to 
52 understand past performance, challenges, and recommendations for program 
53 improvement. 

54 3. Leadership 

55 a. Committee leadership elections shall occur during the organizational meeting held following 
56 Fall elections and prior to the Fall SGA Inauguration, as outlined in Section 2(g). 

57 b. Committee leadership elections shall follow the procedures in §400.7, Student Body Statutes 
58 and Rule 5.5 of the Senate Rules of Procedure. 

59 c. The Chair of the RSOAC may not simultaneously serve as Chair or Vice Chair of another 
60 SGA committee or entity. 

61 d. The Chair or Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee may be removed by either: The 
62 Student Senate President, for cause, with written notice to the committee and the Senate 
63 President Pro Tempore; or a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the voting members of the RSO 
64 Allocation Committee. 

65 (1) Upon removal of the Chair or Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee, or if a 
66 vacancy otherwise occurs, the committee shall, at its next regular meeting, elect a 
67 replacement from among its members by majority vote, subject to confirmation of 
68 eligibility. 

69 (2) The Student Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore shall be notified 
70 within two (2) business days of any vacancy or replacement election. 

71 e. Duties of the Vice Chair 

72 (1) The Vice Chair shall be responsible for recording and maintaining official minutes of 
73 all RSO Allocation Committee meetings. 

74 (2) The Vice Chair shall publish and transmit all minutes to the Student Senate 
75 President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Historian and ensure their 
76 publication within the timeframe required. 

77 (3) The Vice Chair shall be responsible for the collection and maintenance of scoring 
78 materials and administration of the committee’s evaluation rubric during meetings, 
79 ensuring that all votes and scores are properly documented and retained. 

80 f. Duties of the Chair 

 Page 5 of 15
 81 (1) The Chair shall serve as the chief point of communication between the RSO 
 82 Allocation Committee, all Registered Student Organizations, and the Student Senate. 

 83 (2) The Chair shall coordinate with the SGA Accounting Office and the Office of Student 
 84 Organizations & Involvement to provide timely notice of funding outcomes and 
 85 committee decisions to all applicants. 

 86 g. Joint Responsibilities 

 87 (1) The Chair and Vice Chair shall be jointly responsible for preparing and publishing the 
 88 agenda of each RSO Allocation Committee meeting. 

 89 (2) The agenda shall include all funding requests scheduled for consideration, relevant 
 90 documentation, and any items of general business, and must be distributed in 
 91 accordance with this Chapter and Chapter 203 of the Student Body Statutes. 

 92 4. Committee Operations 

 93 a. Quorum shall consist of at least five (5) seven (7) members. 

 94 b. The committee shall establish a regular, weekly meeting schedule and must meet on 
 95 Thursdays, and shall have a meeting end time of no later than 10:00 PM ET. However, the 
 96 time of conclusion may be waived by a 2/3 vote of the committee. 

 97 c. Funding requests must be submitted no later than 12:00 PM ET (noon) on the Monday prior 
 98 to the Thursday meeting at which they will be considered. 

 99 d. Requests submitted after the Monday deadline shall be scheduled for the following week’s 
100 meeting unless otherwise approved by the Chair. 

101 e. All funding requests shall be reviewed by the SGA Accounting Office for authenticity in RSO 
102 registration status prior being forwarded to the Chair of the RSOAC. The SGA Accounting 
103 Office retains decision making authority in regards to the validity of all requests submitted to 
104 the RSOAC. 

105 f. The agenda for each Thursday meeting shall be distributed to committee members and 
106 sponsoring RSOs by Tuesday at 5:00 PM. 

107 g. The Vice Chair shall maintain an attendance log for all scheduled meetings of the RSOAC. 
108 This log shall be transmitted to the Senate President Pro Tempore and posted with the 
109 committee minutes. 

110 (1) An absence means failure to attend a noticed meeting of the RSOAC. 

111 (2) An excused absence may be granted by the Chair for circumstances including, but 
112 not limited to, academic obligations, documented illness, religious observances, 
113 University-sponsored activities, or emergencies. Members shall notify the Chair as 
114 soon as practicable and, when feasible, at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance. 

115 (3) Unexcused absence means any absence not excused under 4(g)(2). 

116 (4) Upon a third (3rd) unexcused absence within a member’s one-year term, an elected 
117 student-at-large member shall be immediately suspended from the RSOAC and the 
118 matter shall be forwarded to the Senate Rules Committee within two (2) business 
119 days. The suspended member shall not be counted toward quorum and shall not 
120 vote pending disposition. 

 Page 6 of 15
121 (5) The Senate Rules Committee shall apply the same process used for Student 
122 Senators regarding attendance and fitness to serve. If the Rules Committee finds 
123 that the individual cannot continue to serve in their capacity, it shall recommend 
124 impeachment to the Senate Judiciary Committee. The Rules Committee may, by 
125 majority vote and upon written justification of extraordinary circumstances, grant 
126 additional excused absences or a one-time waiver not to exceed two (2) additional 
127 absences for the remainder of the term. Any waiver granted shall be reported to the 
128 Senate at the next regular meeting. 

129 (6) If any designated representative of an entity accrues more than three (3) unexcused 
130 absences within their term, the representative shall be removed from the RSOAC, 
131 and the Chair shall request a new designee from the designating authority. The 
132 designating authority may, at their discretion, decide to redesignate the same 
133 individual. If a replacement is not named within five (5) business days of notice, the 
134 seat shall remain vacant until filled and shall not count toward quorum while vacant. 

135 (7) Absences accumulate per term of service (from Fall Inauguration to the subsequent 
136 Fall Inauguration) and reset at the start of each term. This section applies 
137 Suspended or removed members within this Chapter do not count toward quorum 
138 during suspension or after removal.to regularly noticed RSOAC meetings. 

139 5. Funding Recommendation Process 

140 a. The Student Senate shall retain final authority over the approval of all RSOAC funding 
141 recommendations. 

142 b. Funding recommendations made by the RSO Allocation Committee shall be transmitted to 
143 the Student Senate in the form of an allocation resolution sponsored by the Chair and Vice 
144 Chair of the Senate Finance Committee, and co-sponsored by any Senators serving on the 
145 RSOAC. 

146 c. Allocation Resolutions must be submitted by the Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee via 
147 the Senate Legislation Submission form no later than 11:59 PM ET (midnight) on the Friday 
148 following the Thursday RSOAC meeting, to be included on the next week’s Senate agenda 
149 with all other legislation. 

150 d. Allocation Resolutions shall be placed on the agenda for the following Wednesday Senate 
151 meeting. The Senate President shall have the discretion to place these resolutions on either 
152 the Consent portion or the Second Reading portion of the agenda. 

153 e. Before any allocation resolution may be amended, a motion to open the allocation resolution 
154 must be made and agreed to by a simple majority, which shall be followed by an opening 
155 and debate. Upon adoption of such motion by a two-thirds (2/3) roll-call vote, individual 
156 amendments may then be entertained. Each amendment shall require a separate motion, 
157 debate, and two-thirds roll-call vote. However, the Student Senate shall not increase funding 
158 for any Registered Student Organization that the RSO Allocation Committee voted to 
159 recommend zero funding for. 

160 (1) All adopted amendments must be documented and emailed to the Senate Clerk, 
161 Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Historian within one 
162 (1) hour of the conclusion of the meeting by the amendment’s sponsor. 

163 (2) Amendments to Allocation Resolutions may be submitted in advance of the meeting 
164 to the Senate President and Senate Clerk to be listed on the agenda. 

165 6. Eligibility Criteria for Student Organizations 
166 

 Page 7 of 15
167 a. All organizations applying for funding must be currently registered with the Office of Student 
168 Organizations & Involvement and in good conduct standing with Florida State University. 

169 b. Student organizations may not receive funding from the RSO Allocation Committee if they 
170 have also received funds from the College Leadership Council Funding Board, the Sport 
171 Club Distribution Council, or line-item funding in the annual SGA budget in the same fiscal 
172 year. 

173 7. Funding Guidelines and Restrictions 

174 a. All requests must be for eligible uses of Student Activity & Service Fee revenues, as 
175 provided in the SGA Financial Manual. 

176 b. The Student Body Treasurer shall coordinate with the Department of Student Engagement to 
177 establish an online system for submitting funding requests. 

178 c. Funding requests shall generally be required to include a description of the intended use of 
179 funds and why the requested funding is needed. Student organizations shall be required to 
180 provide an estimate of the number of FSU students that are likely to attend an event or travel 
181 opportunity funded by SGA. 

182 d. Pursuant to §1009.24, Florida Statutes, SGA funding may only be used to benefit the student 
183 body in general. As such, funding from the RSO Allocation Committee may not benefit 
184 activities for which an admission fee is charged to students. Further, student organizations 
185 that charge membership fees may not exclude any student from participation in any events 
186 or programs funded by SGA as a result of a student’s inability to pay such fees. 

187 e. Funds may not be used to cover membership dues or fees associated with a student’s or 
188 organization’s national or international affiliations. 

189 f. The committee shall not recommend funding for events or programs that are likely to have 
190 only group members attend and/or have no general benefit to the student body. 

191 g. The committee shall not recommend funding for events that are exclusive to a club or 
192 organization’s executive board. 

193 h. Requests for clothing may only be approved once per fiscal year. Any clothing funded by 
194 SGA must directly promote the student organization. 

195 i. Organizations seeking funding for service trips must first demonstrate that they made a 
196 good-faith effort to participate in an open or public service opportunity offered by the Center 
197 for Leadership and Service, if such an opportunity was available. If participation in such a trip 
198 was not feasible due to scheduling, availability, or capacity, the organization may pursue 
199 independent service trip funding through the RSO Allocation Committee. In such cases, 
200 documentation of the organization’s outreach to CLS and explanation of why participation in 
201 a CLS-facilitated trip was not possible must be provided with the funding request. 

202 j. Student organizations shall submit their request prior to the RSOAC meeting via a recording 
203 of their presentation, ideally with a slideshow to assist their request. 

204 (1) The presentation's recording may not be longer than 7 minutes, and must detail the 
205 specifics about their request for the full awareness of the SROAC membership. 

206 (2) Time may be designated at the discretion of the Chair of the RSOAC to watch these 
207 pre-submitted presentations during the meeting, or members may be required to 
208 watch these presentations prior to the meeting. 

 Page 8 of 15
209 (3) All video presentations must be submitted alongside the organization's application to 
210 the RSOAC. 

211 (4) A representative of the Student Organization must attend the RSOAC meeting they 
212 will be considered in, for the purposes of answering questions about the 
213 presentation. 
214 

215 (A) If there are no representatives from the organization, the request will be 
216 tabled. 

217 (B) If, at the next meeting of the RSOAC, there is no attending representative, 
218 the request shall be zero funded. 

219 8. Funding Limits 

220 a. Travel 

221 (1) Maximum of $250 per student. 

222 b. Annual Cap per Organizations 

223 (1) No organization may receive more than 3.5% of the total budget allocated to the 
224 RSOAC in the annual budget process during a single fiscal year, regardless of the 
225 number of individual requests or categories funded. 

226 (2) For purposes of this section, “total funding” includes all allocations for travel, events, 
227 programming, or any other expenditures recommended by the RSO Allocation 
228 Committee and approved by the Student Senate. 

229 c. Single Allocation Rule 

230 (1) An organization may not receive funding for more than one (1) request within the 
231 same allocation resolution transmitted to the Student Senate. 

232 d. The Committee shall have discretion to recommend that the Student Senate exceed the 
233 funding limit for Travel or Events/Programming with the usage of Senate Projects funding, 
234 said recommendation shall be listed in the scoring rubrics “Evaluator Notes” section. 

235 9. Funding Allocation Schedule 

236 a. In order to comply with University purchasing and travel guidelines, of the funding allocated 
237 to the RSO Allocation Committee in the annual SGA budget: 

238 (1) 5% shall be available for allocation beginning July 1 each year through the end of the 
239 Summer semester; 

240 (2) 47.5% shall be available for allocation in the Fall semester, in addition to any 
241 unexpended funds from earlier in the fiscal year; and 

242 (3) 47.5% shall be available in the Spring semester, in addition to any unexpended funds 
243 from earlier in the fiscal year. 

244 b. All final funding allocations must be approved by the Student Senate at least 30 calendar 
245 days before the event or travel is to take place. 

 Page 9 of 15
246 c. In addition to the requirement above, funding for events or travel scheduled during the 
247 months of May or June must be approved by the Student Senate before the conclusion of 
248 the Spring semester. There shall be no exceptions to this requirement, which is needed in 
249 order to maintain compliance with the University’s fiscal year-end closeout procedures. 

250 10. Post-Award Requirements 

251 a. All events funded by SGA must be publicly advertised on the University-designated student 
252 organization management platform in a manner visible to the general student body. This 
253 shall serve as the baseline standard for public advertisement. Additional promotion through 
254 means such as social media, digital signage, newsletters, or tabling is encouraged but not 
255 required. 

256 b. Any events, programs, travel, or other activities supported by SGA funding must comply with 
257 the FSU Student Organization Conduct Code as well as all federal, state, and local laws. 

258 c. Every organization receiving funding from SGA must submit a post event evaluation form, 
259 along with receipts for any purchases made, to the SGA Accounting Office, within ten (10) 
260 business days following the event. 

261 d. If the requirements above are not followed by an organization, they shall be barred from 
262 requesting any further funding until their post-award violations are rectified with SGA 
263 accounting. 

264 11. Annual Review Requirement 

265 a. No later than the end of the Fall semester each year, the Student Body Treasurer shall 
266 conduct an evaluation of the RSOAC program. This review shall assess the overall 
267 effectiveness of the program and identify any areas for potential improvement. 

268 b. This evaluation shall include: 

269 (1) The number and nature of instances in which standard funding rules or limits were 
270 waived; 

271 (2) An analysis of how such waivers impacted student organizations and the broader 
272 student body; 

273 (3) The adequacy of the current funding level for the program; 

274 (4) Recommendations for enhancing the program’s structure, parameters, and allocation 
275 limits; and 

276 (5) A breakdown of the number and types of organizations that receive funding, 
277 including both organizational status (USSO, ASO, GSO) and programmatic category 
278 (e.g. academic, cultural, special interest, political, community service). 

279 c. Following the evaluation, the Student Body Treasurer shall prepare a report of findings and 
280 recommendations. This report shall be submitted to the Student Senate Budget Committee 
281 during the annual SGA budget planning cycle. 

282 Section 2. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 812, “RSO Allocation 
283 Committee”. 
284 

285 12. Policy Implementation: 

 Page 10 of 15
286 a. The Student Senate shall adopt a policy, pursuant to the requirements of Chapter 416, 
287 Student Body Statutes, to govern the operations of the RSO Allocation Committee, to 
288 establish procedures governing funding requests, and to establish criteria for the committee 
289 to use in evaluating funding requests. At minimum an established policy must create a rubric 
290 that the committee shall use for all allocations. 

291 b. Committee Member Elections 

292 (1) Beginning in the 78th Student Senate Session, five (5) of the student-at-large seats 
293 on the RSO Allocation Committee shall be filled by election during the Fall SGA 
294 elections. 

295 (2) The elected members shall: 

296 (A) Be currently enrolled undergraduate students; 

297 (B) Be in good academic and conduct standing with the University; 

298 (C) Must have completed financial certification at any time during the current 
299 fiscal year, beginning July 1st, and no later than the day before the candidate 
300 declaration filing deadline. 

301 (D) Cannot be the registered President or Treasurer of any Registered Student 
302 Organizations (RSOs). 

303 (3) Candidates for these seats must file for candidacy and comply with all campaign and 
304 election requirements outlined in Title VII of the Student Body Statutes. 

305 (4) Elected committee members shall serve a one-year term beginning at the Fall SGA 
306 Inauguration and ending at the following Fall Inauguration. 

307 (5) In the event of a vacancy in one of the five elected student-at-large seats on the RSO 
308 Allocation Committee, the Student Body President may appoint a replacement 
309 pursuant to the procedures outlined in Chapters 201 and 202 of the Student Body 
310 Statutes, and any other applicable Executive Branch policies governing seat 
311 vacancies. The appointee must meet all eligibility requirements outlined in this 
312 Chapter and shall be referred to the Student Senate Finance Committee for 
313 confirmation prior to being considered by the full Student Senate. 

314 (6) The number of elected seats and eligibility criteria may be reviewed and adjusted 
315 annually by the Student Senate as part of the RSOAC evaluation report submitted 
316 pursuant to Section 11 of this Chapter. 

317 

318 Section 3. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 706, “Fall Elections”. 

319 1. The Fall Election cycle shall include the races for odd-numbered Senate seats, the Campus 
320 Recreation Board, the Congress of Graduate Students, elected members of the RSO Allocation 
321 Committee, and shall include any applicable constitutional amendments, referenda items, and 
322 opinion questions. 

323 2. Campus Recreation Board: 

324 a. There shall be eight (8) elected Campus Recreation Board Seats. Each seat on the Board 
325 shall be elected individually. 

 Page 11 of 15
326 b. The electorate of the Campus Recreation Board shall be limited to students enrolled at the 
327 Tallahassee campus. 

328 c. Beyond the provisions listed here, elections shall proceed pursuant to Section 1006(4). 

329 3. The RSO Allocation Committee 

330 a. There shall be five (5) elected student-at-large seats on the RSO Allocation Committee. All 
331 five seats shall be elected at large by ranked choice voting, if technology permits the use of 
332 that voting method. If ranked choice voting is not feasible, the Supervisor of Elections shall 
333 have the discretion to implement an alternative method consistent with the procedures used 
334 in Student Government Association elections at the time. 

335 b. The electorate for the RSO Allocation Committee shall include all students enrolled at the 
336 Tallahassee campus. 

337 c. Candidates must meet the eligibility criteria established in Chapter 816 of the Student Body 
338 Statutes, including but not limited to: completion of a qualifying financial or SGA funding 
339 exam and not being the registered President or Treasurer of any Registered Student 
340 Organization (RSO). 

341 4. The Congress of Graduate Students: 

342 a. The electorate shall be limited to graduate, post-baccalaureate special and professional 
343 students. 

344 b. Elections shall be held pursuant to Chapter 603 of the Student Body Statutes and COGS 
345 Code Chapter 111. 

346 Section 4. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 100, “Statutory Framework 
347 and Compliance.” 

348 1. Major Offices: 

349 a. Definitions: 

350 (1) Director - The chief executive of an entity. 

351 (2) Assistant Director - The individual who would assume the role of the chief executive

353 (3) Treasurer - The individual in charge of monitoring the finances of an entity. 

354 b. The definitions listed in this statute shall include any positions which fit the criteria of the

Summary of Legislation: 
This legislation would do two main things: first, make it so elected RSOAC members term out, and 
disband elected positions on December 1st; second, make it so the Fall election will not have election 
for elected RSOAC Commissioners. 
 
Background Information: 
This legislation comes together with a larger RSOAC Committee reform underway between the Senate, 
Executive, and Advisors, focusing on transferring general responsibility for initial allocations from the 
Committee to the office of the Treasurer. This section is being proposed first for the fact that the Fall 
Election is considering elected RSOAC Members, and we want to make it clear prior to the elections of 
this change to elected membership. This allows the larger reform bill to continue to be revised and 
workshopped whilst the Senate makes clear what we are working on with RSOAC Membership. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
RSOAC Leadership, Treasury, Finance, Internal Affairs, Judiciary, Elections Office. All legislative 
consultants (besides elections) are additionally on with the larger reform. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation would remove elected members on RSOAC on inauguration, and the legislation would 
have these positions not have to go through the election process this Fall.

Steven; Hearing no Student comments, anyone from the office of government affairs? 

Steven: Hearing none, I’d like to introduce the new dean of graduate students, Gregory Bell. 

Gregory Bell: Thank you for the warm welcome, I am new to FSU. Prior to FSU, I worked 
within various graduate institutions in different universities. I just wanted to tell you about 
myself, my goal is to create a sense of community with graduate students. Community is highly 
correlated to success in your program. There are two things you need to be successful; 1. You 
have someone who has your back, academically and professionally and personally. Second, you 
need to be that person for someone else. That is what community is, and therefore what your 
network is. Building a network is about making connections with anyone and everyone on 
campus and building communities. If you approach an FSU alum, you have an immediate bond, 
so please embrace it. When I was at my previous institution, I served as the COGS advisor; I saw 
that we built it into an organization that provides funding and community. Those small 
interactions are important between students. That's a bit about me; I am happy to answer 
questions or talk more. I view COGS as a way to receive feedback from graduate students. My 
hope is to have an open dialogue and community. 

Steven: Despite Dean Bell only being here a month, he has already gone above and beyond with 
Orientation sessions. Can we take a picture before he leaves? 

Steven: Thank you. Be careful when driving everyone, Tallahassee drivers can be crazy. 

Steven: All of campus was closed for the month of August, but COGS was busy. Thank you to 
all of those who attended orientation sessions. There were 12 sessions with great turn out; we 
have had great interest with petitions after these sessions, so it is a great way to recruit students 

Just a heads up, there is one more tabling opportunity through the GSRC coming up. GSRC hosts 
a lot of great events and has a lot of resources. They offer a lot of similar services, but just have 
some different rules for who can receive funding. This is their leadership team on the 
PowerPoint.

DeSean will be leading the tabling event. If you’d like to join him, please feel free to reach out to

One major success we had that week was being invited to the main Fall 2026 new graduate

the food was gone within 30 minutes. We had a lot of great partners show up, and Strozier was

Then we also presented at the main orientation session. There was probably 750+ people who

Desean: Can we get FSU’s shoe?

Jania: That looks cool!

Steven: Any last questions for Joey? Just a heads up, we have less money allocated this summer.

Steven: Hearing no final questions, Desean.

COGS Meeting Minutes 9-21-2026 
 
Steven: Meeting starting at 6:43pm. We have a few petitioners to kick off tonight’s agenda and 
just one funding request after that. Chairs and vice chairs, please stay after the meeting for a 
quick discussion. 
 
Steven: We’ve got quorum. 
 
Steven: Any questions regarding the minutes? 
 
Dasean: Motion to approve the meeting minutes from August 31st. 
 
Joey: Seconded. 
 
Steven: Seeing none for special introductions. Chase Peterson, the supervisor of elections, said 
he would be here, but he doesn’t seem to be at the moment. If he comes later we’ll give him 
some time for a quick little talk. 
 
Steven: Our four petitioners are here, please come to the front. Each of you will have three 
minutes to give introductions and why you would like to join COGS. 
 
Mahinur: Thank you for the opportunity to introduce myself and be considered for a seat in 
COGS. I understand a lot of challenges we, as graduate students, face regard work-life balance, 
and this is one of my major motives for joining the Congress to better understand the struggles of 
other students and help solve those problems. I am interested in serving on the advocacy 
committee. 
 
Mark: Master’s in strategic communication, worked for FSU for 14.5 years, finally decided to 
take advantage of the tuition waiver and get my master’s degree. I was a news and sports reporter 
for 5 years out of college and then I came to FSU to be the digital media director for the office of 
communications. In undergrad I was a part of SGA, actually on the supreme court as well. I 
decided to apply for COGS to dive into the whole student experience, and I wanted to learn how 
to do as much as I can as a student as well as an employee. 
 
Daniel: MBA, I want to be part of COGS because I was in SGA during undergrad. I would like 
to work in the student advocacy committee because I want to amplify the voices of other students 
within the College of Business. 
 
Olajumoke: From Maryland, long way from home, and I am petitioning to join COGS because 
communication has been at the center of my career. I am passionate about communications and I 
come with experience from student government, residence life/RA, and these experiences have 
taught me how to listen, advocate, and lead effectively. It’s not about telling other’s what to do, 
it’s about listening and making sure voices are heard. I bring relatability and authenticity because 
I have had to seek out resources on campus—and asking for help can be uncomfortable. I look 
forward to encouraging others to take advantage of the resources available to them, especially 
since graduate students have such limited resources. This matters to me because students don’t know about them and thus don’t take advantage of them. It would be an honor to represent the 
school of communication in this seat. 
 
DaSean: Are you all available at this time on Monday’s? 
 
All petitioners: Yes 
 
Sadio: If you had one thing within your respective college you would like to see be changed, 
what would it be? 
 
Mark: More experiences opportunities for students to thrive outside of the classroom. I would 
love to advocate for more part-time positions as well. 
 
Daniel: More funding for college of business, such as for AI in the workforce and research into 
the effectiveness of AI. 
 
Ola: More assistantships, there are very few available and many well-rounded communication 
students who would appreciate the opportunity and relief of tuition costs. 
 
Mahinur: Introduce new ways for students to learn how to use resources and where to find them. 
Students don’t know how to ask for funding or where to find it, and I would like to provide more 
support for students in this aspect. 
 
Joey: Are any of you good in Graphic design or excel? 
 
Mark: Graphic design yes, excel no. 
 
Olajumoke: Canva, graphic design, Adobe Premiere Pro. 
 
Daniel: Excel. 
 
Mahinur: Excel. 
 
Janai: What committee are you guys interested in serving on? 
 
Mark: Internal affairs. 
 
Daniel: Advocacy. 
 
Olajumoke: Advocacy. 
 
Mahinur: Advocacy. 
 
Steven: Any more questions? 
 
Mark: Can we ask a question? 
Steven: Sure, why not. 
 
Mark: What have you learned from being in COGS? How has it benefited you? 
 
DaSean: I’ve learned a lot from the diverse perspectives in COGS. We have great representation 
of international students, and while I’ve had great empathy for them before COGS, talking and 
listening to them has really softened my heart. 
 
Devan: Participation in the decision-making process of what students can do on campus is 
rewarding because of the tangible results and interactions. 
 
Joey: I love being able to help people with questions and handle the budget. 
 
Madison: Getting to know the why behind everything is really interesting, why we make the 
decisions we make, where the money is coming from, and it’s a great reminder that we aren’t the 
only grad organization on campus. It’s awesome to get perspectives from other orgs on campus 
when they come to us for funding. 
 
Steven: We’re very people-oriented, and that’s what makes COGS special, the diversity in 
perspectives is amazing. Thank you all for these great answers, and you as well Mark, for the 
great question. Please step out for about five minutes while we deliberate. 
 
Janai: This is really tough choosing between these two students. 
 
Nichollette: There are student advocate seats that one of them could be selected for instead. 
 
DaSean: All great candidates, I met Olajumoke at one of the events, and she was very passionate 
about coming here and petitioning for one of the seats, I think she would be a great candidate. 
 
Madison: I know Mark from being a videographer for us in my sorority, he was so on top of his 
stuff, excellent communication, he is awesome. 
 
Sadio: Echoing what Madison said, Mark has been very easy to work with, very sweet guy, and 
such a unique perspective since he can speak to the other side of being an employee as well as a 
student 
 
Janai: We could move Olajumoke to the advocacy seat since she is so passionate about 
advocacy, and since Mark has so much experience I think he would fit well for the 
Communication seat. 
 
Rasleen: I would go with Mark based on his experience and connections and I think that he is the 
best pick for this position, 
 
Joey: I also like Mark for his experience, but I also want to vote for Olajumoke since she can use 
Canva. 
Claire: I can use Canva too! 
 
Joey: Well that’s true but then you can have someone to pass some of the work onto. 
 
Claire: Okay that’s true I can’t argue with that. 
 
Nicholette: Could also be good to give voice to Olajumoke since she doesn’t have as much 
experience as Mark. 
 
Madison: I can also do graphic design if you need help Joey. 
 
Joey: Okay I will be reaching out to you, you’ll probably be helping Claire with the budget 
report/ 
 
Claire: Yes please. 
 
Steven: Cons? 
 
Sadio: My hesitation with giving Mark the seat is that maybe it would be better to give a voice to 
someone who doesn’t have as much experience. 
 
Steven: Just for clarification, there is no “Advocate” seat, but there are special kinds of advocate 
seats. Let me read off the seats that are currently vacant. Any questions about those seats? 
 
DaSean: Do we want to have Nicholette go out and talk to the candidates before or after we 
vote? 
 
Steven: Yes, we could. This is a tough decision to make. Are there any objections to going to 
talk to them? Do we want to vote on everyone after the conversation? 
 
Congress: Unanimous support for discussion and then voting after 
 
Steven: Good news, Mark agreed to petition into the Veteran Student Advocate seat. He is very 
passionate about Veterans Affairs and was very excited to hear that this position was open and 
available. His election will be contingent upon his successful completion of the corrected 
petition. 
 
Nicholette: Tentative motion that, upon approval of his submission for the Veteran Student 
Advocate seat petition, he will be given the oath of office during our next meeting. 
 
Sadio: Seconded. 
 
Steven: Any more questions before we get into the vote? Seeing none. 
 
Steven: All those voting yes for Mahinur, please raise your hand now. Vote of 15-0-0 
Steven: All those voting yes for Mark. Vote of 15-0-0 
 
Steven: All those voting yes for Olajumoke. Vote of 15-0-0 
 
Steven: All those voting yes for Daniel. Vote of 14-1-0 
 
Steven: Alright thank you everyone. Nicholette, would you come up to prepare the oath of 
office? 
 
Steven: Congratulations everyone, please come up for the oath of office. Mark, your oath will be 
at the next meeting. 
 
Olajumoke, Daniel, and Mahinur swear their oath of office. 
 
Steven: Congratulations y’all, we will be sending you information on the financial certification 
form you must complete on FSU HQ, and you will not be able to vote until next meeting. 
 
Steven: It looks like Chase is here. Come on up Chase. 
 
Chase: *Read off the seats allocated to each college in COGS.* If any of you guys have 
questions about the justification of seats, please check out the memo on the FSU Unicode. 
 
Daniel: How do you decide the number of seats per college? 
 
Chase: It’s called the method of equal proportions, basically the population of the college and the 
priority values of the colleges determine it. The memo includes the spreadsheets and feel free to 
google it as well. Any other questions? Thank you guys so much. 
 
Steven: Now we can go into the report of the officers. Thank you all for coming out on the 31st 
and meeting the new Dean. He was very impressed with the attendance and discussion, so thank 
you all for that. Going forward, he is interested in attending one COGs meeting and one Exec 
meeting per semester. If you weren’t at that last meeting, we handed out nametags, so please 
come up to me after the meeting to grab yours. We just had another graduate lounge last week, 
and we have another one coming up next month. I encourage all of you to show up next time, 
and thank you for those who came and represented COGS last Friday. 
 
Joey: Things are going well, we have gone through $120k already, we have to start thinking 
about whether or not we want to move from reserves or just accept that not everyone will be 
getting presentation grant funding from us this cycle. 
 
Devan: When does the cycle end? In October? 
 
Joey: Yes it ends at the end of October. It’s not exceptionally early to move money but we can 
wait too. We have about 40 to 60 applications pending right now. It’s probably going to be about 
$24,000 at most; we’ve had a lot of $600 requests. 
DaSean: My only concern is that isn’t November to February the bigger cycle? 
 
Steven: Actually the number of applications and amount of money going out has significantly 
increased this cycle compared to all the others. 
 
DaSean: Could we encourage people to apply for attendance grants instead? 
 
Steven: We could merge them, we’ve done that in the past. 
 
Joey: Yeah that’s something we could do, this is all something to think about. Show of hands 
who thinks it would be a good idea to transfer more money out of reserves? 
 
Nichollette: We could do maybe $5,000 as a trial run this cycle to see if we will have to keep 
doing so for the next cycles? 
 
Joey: Thanks for the input everyone. No bill on the horizon yet, just wanted to put it on 
everyone’s radar. That’s all my updates. 
 
DaSean: The only update I have is that I’m trying to schedule a meeting with someone about 
their college. Advocacy met last week, but Devan will get to that in a bit. 
 
Claire: As you all know, there have been some issues with the Declaration of Candidacy form. 
Feel free to come up after the meeting if you’d like to troubleshoot it. Deadline is until this 
Thursday but pleaseeee do not wait until then just in case you run into any issues. 
 
Nicholette: Very happy to see four new seats filled! 
 
Tanner: Joey and Steven have been working on the new FSUHQ form for grants. This will be 
really nice for students to have it on a centralized platform instead of SurveyMonkey. These new 
forms will be launching on October 1st to begin applications for the next cycle. We will have to 
get the website updated with all of the new links. If you hear any issues from students, it’s 
probably because they’re going to the old form and it no longer works. Declaration of candidacy: 
the form runs three reports on GPA, conduct, and academic honor policy, and medical and law 
students are having an issue because they are on a pass/fail system instead. I was on a phone call 
with ITS for 4 hours on Thursday, very thankful for my ITS friends. Claire has done a great job 
communicating these issues with you guys, so thank you to Claire for that. If you are having an 
issue with declaring candidacy, just stay after and I will give you the link to declare your 
candidacy instead of waiting for Chase to send you the form. You can use FSUHQ if you are 
having issues with the original form, and we will have to manually check everyone who uses the 
FSUHQ form for eligibility and add them to the ballot. If you are unsure if you’re on the ballot, 
just ask me and I can tell you because I have access to it. Any other questions? That’s all from 
me. 
 
Steven: Alright thank you Tanner. Let’s kick off the next item with committee reports, Rasleen. 
 Rasleen: We are working on updating the website and our next meeting is the next Monday on 
zoom at 7pm. 
 
Steven: Alright thank you, Rasleen. Janai. 
 
Janai: We elected a vice chair, Hussaini. We want to try to do Market Wednesdays at least once a 
month. We will have more to report at next meeting. 
 
Steven: Thank you, Janai. Advocacy. 
 
Devan: I was elected Chair, and Sadio was elected Vice Chair. Looking to spark back up town 
hall meetings, but we are also working to brainstorm more ideas. Hoping to fill up the Panama 
City rep spot and some administrative stuff we’re trying to hash out. Next meeting is on 
Mondays at 7:15pm in person in the Union. 
 
Steven: Committees who want to meet in person can also order food for these meetings, so that’s 
an incentive to not do them on Zoom. Chairs and vice chairs, please stay after again for a quick 
discussion. 
 
*Joey now leading the floor since Steven is sponsoring Bill 24* 
 
Joey: You have three minutes 
 
Steven: CHAOS host great events, this was their first event and they put it together really early, 
but it was before our first meeting, so we couldn’t put a formal bill together in time. So we took 
it out of the speaker’s request and now we are reimbursing it so that it is back to what it was. 
 
Joey: Does anyone wish to speak in pro? 
 
Devan: Did they utilize all of the funds? 
 
Steven: Yes, they just sent me the PO actually. 
 
Parker: What’s the logic on the reimbursement? What’s the practical rationale of it? 
 
Steven: I like to keep the speaker’s request as an emergency fund for these kinds of issues. Do I 
need all $10,000? No? Do I need the $600 right away? No. It’s just a formality thing. I’d also 
like the next speaker to have full access to the speaker request fund. 
 
Joey: Motion to call the question? 
 
DaSean: Motion to call the question. 
 
Devan: Seconded. 
 
Vote is 14-0-5, bill passes. 
Janai: Motion to waive round table. 
 
Nicholette: Seconded. 
 
Steven: Any objections? Seeing none. Thank you all for coming out, next meeting is the last one 
in the chambers for a bit and then the next two will be in the student services building since the 
chambers have been reserved by the university. Meeting adjourned at 8:24pm.

71 shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes. During this period only statements in pro or con of the 
72 agenda item being discussed may be made, and Senators who speak in open debate must 
73 specify whether they are speaking in pro or con of the agenda item. Questions relating to the 
74 agenda item must be made in the form of a point of information directed to the presiding officer. 
75 (1) The Senate may motion to add additional time to the period of open debate, as long 
76 as the total time of debate does not exceed thirty (30) minutes. 
77 (2) Any statement in open debate that exceeds the thirty (30) minute maximum, or that 
78 exceeds the allotted time stated by the presiding officer, shall be considered a 
79 filibuster, and the presiding officer may end the debate. This can be overridden by a 
80 simple majority vote of the Senate. 
81 (A) If the Senate votes to override the decision to end debate, the Senator 
82 previously recognized shall be allowed to finish their statement. Once they 
83 have completed their statement, debate shall end. 
84 (3) Once recognized, a Senator shall have three (3) minutes to make a pro or con 
85 statement. This time may be increased by the presiding officer as deemed fit, but shall

 Alexia Holliday

 78th STUDENT SENATE 
 Legislation Cover Sheet 

 Senate Resolution #: 044 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis, Holliday 
Co-sponsor(s): Ramos, Rodriguez, Macalintal, Bigenho, Torres, Rivas, Perantoni, Urrea, Le, 
 Tanner, Aihe 

Short Title: Senate Debate and Rules of Procedure Clarification 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This resolution restructures Rule Nine of Rules of Procedure to move Statements of Dissent 
under New Business, and Rule Ten to update Senate debate procedures. These procedural 
changes will set a maximum time for debate and integrate Robert’s Rules of Order more 
clearly. 
 
Background Information: 
After looking over Robert’s Rules of Order and sitting through recent Senate meetings, it has been 
made clear that the current procedure adopted by Senate does not comply with Robert’s Rules of Order 
Newly Revised, and is also somewhat contradictory of itself when pertaining to statements of dissent. 
When looking over sections of Robert’s Rules and having discussions of what best applies to our 
Senate culture and what should be revised, this resolution was drafted in order to ensure efficiency and 
fairness in how debate works in the Second Reading process, while still maintaining Senate 
leadership’s discretion in running an efficient meeting. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
This legislation was written with particular research done into Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised 
and our own current Rules of Procedure. In addition, outreach was done with the current Senate 
Parliamentarian and the former Senate Parliamentarian to ensure that Robert’s Rules were being 
correctly applied and that the implementation was appropriate for our Senate. In addition, this 
legislation was reviewed by Internal Affairs Committee leadership, Finance Committee leadership, and 
former Senators to receive input and commentary prior to submission. SG&A was contacted and sent a 
copy of the legislation, and any feedback received back will be promptly taken into account. 
 
After receiving Senator input, there was a comment of allowing sponsors the opportunity to respond to 
statements made in debate. After some communication with the Senate Parliamentarian, a fair 
compromise was found to allow sponsors to comment should the recognized Senator yield them the 
time to do so. 

 Page 7 of 8
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
Should this legislation pass through the Senate, Statements of Dissent will fall under ‘New Business’ on 
the Senate meeting agenda, rather than having their own distinct agenda item. In addition, our structure 
of debate will slightly shift; round table will now be called ‘open debate,’ and will almost entirely contain 
pro or con statements towards the given agenda item. Questions are no longer permitted outside of 
general questioning unless they are asked in the form of a point of information once in open debate. 
This resolution would also set a maximum amount of debate time, but allow Senators to specify a given 
amount of time for debate as long as it falls under that minimum. 
 
The definition of filibuster would also be added and addressed in this new debate structure. The 
presiding officer is allowed to end a filibuster, but this may be overridden by a majority vote of the 
Senate if they so choose. Finally, Robert’s Rules of Order would be more clearly cited under this new 
structure of debate: motions to move into open debate, call the question, or table are all nondebatable 
motions under Robert’s Rules, so if objected they will go immediately to a vote won by simple majority. 
Finally, should the need arise (e.g., if several Senators are all wishing to be recognized within a short 
amount of time), the presiding officer is allowed to set an amount of time for each Senator to be 
recognized, but this can’t be less than 3 minutes. In addition, any time not used by the recognized 
Senator can be yielded to the sponsor or candidate to allow them opportunity to comment on the 
previously given statement.

Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can.

recognized September 10th as Suicide Prevention Day. This day of recognition needed more 
awareness, which led to the recognition of the entire month of September as National Suicide 
Prevention Month in 2008.

who need to reach out from doing so. The Student Senate encourages students who are struggling to 
utilize the campus resources and organizations outlined. At Florida State, these conversations have 
been encouraged with multiple resources available to struggling students and campaigns going around 
to help promote all the incredible work that our various departments are doing to combat this issue 
head on. We need to continue this love and encouragement as we navigate the intense timeline of our 
collegiate careers.

Short Title: To Recognize the Civil Rights Legacy of Florida State University and the 
Contributions of the Civil Rights Institute 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation recognizes the 250th Anniversary of American Independence as an 
opportunity to reflect on the nation's ongoing pursuit of civil rights while honoring Florida State 
University's civil rights legacy and the contributions of the Civil Rights Institute. It asserts the 
Student Senate's commitment to promoting civic engagement, historical education, equal 
opportunity, and continued student participation in programs and initiatives that preserve and 
advance civil rights for all members of the FSU community. 
 
Background Information: 
The United States celebrated its 250th Anniversary of Independence this year. As we 
commemorate this historic landmark, it is important that we—as a Student Senate and Student 
Body—reflect not only on the nation’s founding ideals but also on its continual pursuit of equal 
justice, opportunity for all, and civil rights. 
 
According to Merriam-Webster’s dictionary, civil rights are “rights that citizens are guaranteed 
by their government through legislation or other actions to ensure equal opportunities and 
protection under the law, regardless of their race, religion, or sex.” In the Constitution, these 
are personal liberty rights guaranteed to U.S. citizens under the 13th, 14th, and 15th 
Amendments. Additionally, through the Civil Rights Movement, it advanced the cause of 
equality through the efforts of educators, community leaders, advocates, and most importantly, 
students. The works of these groups transformed institutions across the nation, with the 
Supreme Court’s ruling in Brown v. Board of Education in 1954 a culmination of efforts along 
with the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965. 
 
Florida State University has its own unique civil rights history, beginning with the integration of 
the university in 1962 and continuing through the advocacy of students, faculty, alumni, and 
community leaders to expand access, representation, and educational opportunity. The Civil 
Rights Institute was founded in 2018 by alumni Doby Flowers and Fred Flowers, who, 

 Page 17 of 19
approximately 60 years ago, contributed to FSU’s racial integration history with Fred Flowers . 
We also recognize Ted Ellis, the inaugural director of FSU’s Civil Rights Institute. Since 2023, 
Director Ellis has helped expand the institute’s programming, community partnerships, and 
commitment to preserving and promoting civil rights history. Ted Ellis dedicated three years to 
developing the infrastructure and early reputation of the institute. Through its establishment, 
the University further strengthened its commitment to preserving this history through research, 
education, dialogue, and community engagement. 
 
Conversations surrounding the future of the Civil Rights Institute as a university resource for 
students have highlighted the importance of ensuring students remain aware of the Institute’s 
mission. It serves to promote civil rights for all, educate the campus community on the history 
of the civil rights movement and contemporary social issues encourage the intersection of 
academic dialogue and active community engagement, and foster representation for the 
diverse communities that comprise Florida State University, including veterans, students with 
disabilities, multicultural students, LGBTQ+ students, faith practitioners, environmental rights 
advocates, and students across academic disciplines. 
 
This proclamation also reinforces the importance of ensuring that civil rights are not considered 
an isolated reference to a historical period or niche interest, but rather as an ongoing 
responsibility and resource available to every student. Principal Student Ambassador to the 
CRI, Eryn Files, has emphasized strengthening the student-centered nature of the Institute by 
prioritizing inclusive and representative events, the establishment of an affiliated RSO that 
holds positions for members of the aforementioned diverse communities, facilitated 
collaboration with agency leaders who share the needs of their constituents, and the 
continuation of community initiatives such as the Selma and Montgomery Civil Rights 
Experience, the Unity 5K, and Annual Commemorative MLK week events. These efforts would 
further promote civil rights initiatives that serve the diverse communities represented 
throughout Florida State University 
 
As representatives of the student body, the Student Senate has an opportunity to recognize 
the historical significance of civil rights at Florida State University while encouraging continued 
engagement with programs and organizations that promote civic participation, historical 
education, leadership development, equal opportunity, and a more inclusive campus 
community. 
 
This is not a matter that should receive attention only during Black History Month. Civil rights 
should remain a determined commitment of the student body, recognizing the importance of 
preserving, honoring, and advancing a legacy that impacts all students and faculty every day 
of the year.

Florida State University Civil Rights Institute, Associate Dean for Culture and Community 
Engagement Keithen V. Mathis. MSW, CRI Student Ambassador Eryn Files, SGA Executive

STUDENT LIFE COMMITTEE 
 September 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM 
 Location: fla.st/sga-meet-sl 
 MEETING MINUTES 

 Call to Order 
 Chair Rico called the meeting to order at 7:04 PM. 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 
 Chair Rico acknowledges the Land Acknowledgement. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
 Vice Chair Macalintal administered roll call and verified quorum. 
 Quorum is verified. 

 Public Comment 

 • Public Comment #001 
 
 ■ Student Ana Augustine's pre-submitted comment asks Student Government 
 whether FSU plans to follow the lead of the Florida Department of 
 Transportation and Leon County and remove all Flock cameras from 
 campus, while expressing concern regarding technology misuse. 

 Opening Announcements 
 
 • Chair Rico welcomes the committee back to session and announces 
 that the meeting has a busy agenda. 

 Old Business 

New Business 
 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal motions to unlock the calendar 
 • Senator Nturubika seconds the motion to unlock the calendar. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal motions to move proclamation #78-018 to be 
 discussed last. 
 • Senator Nturubika seconds the motion to move proclamation #78-018 
 to be discussed last. 

• Proclamation #78-019 
 
 ■ Sponsor Rodriguez gives an opening statement regarding proclamation 
 #78-019, which is to recognize September as Suicide Awareness and 
 Prevention month and provide information about campus resources for 
 students. 

 • Sponsor yields with 4:28 for their closing. 
 • Chair Rico opens a period of general questioning. 
 • Senator Nturubika motions to move into roundtable discussion. 
 • Senator Engelhard seconds the motion to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Senator Nturubika speaks in pro of the resolution, placing particular 
 emphasis on the importance of resource awareness for college 
 students. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal questions Sponsor Rodriguez about whether 
 there will be a guest speaker appearing in student senate to speak 
 on the topic. 
 • Sponsor Rodriguez states that a presentation is in the process of 
 being made, and she hopes it will be delivered and spoken about at 
 the upcoming student senate meeting on September 23rd. 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell motions to pass the proclamation by 
 unanimous consent. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal seconds the motion to pass the proclamation 
 by unanimous consent. 
 • Sponsor Rodriguez gives her closing statement. 

 The proclamation passes by unanimous consent. 
• Proclamation #78-020 
 
 ■ Sponsor Nturubika gives an opening statement regarding proclamation #78-
 020, which is to recognize the work of Florida State University's Civil Rights 
 Institute during the nation's 250th anniversary. The institute was established 
 in 2018 and prioritizes research, education, dialogue, and community 
 engagement regarding civil rights and social issues. The sponsor expresses 
 hope to bring Institute members to the Senate floor in an upcoming meeting 
 to speak about the proclamation. 

 • Sponsor yields with 2:48 for their closing. • Chair Rico opens a period of general questioning. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal questions Sponsor Nturubika regarding 
 student union outreach, and why some unions are not quoted within 
 the initiative. 
 • Sponsor Nturubika clarifies that he did not reach out to all student 
 unions, but did get in contact with the Black Student Union, the 
 Asian American Student Union, the Pride Student Union, and the 
 Civil Rights Institute. He clarifies that PSU was not included in the 
 proclamation due to a missed deadline. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal asks Sponsor Nturubika if he's able to submit 
 the Pride Student Union's quote as a public comment so that the 
 committee can propose adopting the quote as an amendment. 
 • Sponsor Nturubika says yes, and that he has a fully drafted version 
 with the PSU's quote ready. 
 • Sponsor Nturubika raises a point of inquiry regarding how to submit 
 an amendment. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal clarifies that the process has recently 
 changed. 
 • Chair Rico suggests that the committee make a verbal amendment 
 and handle the structural element at a later date. 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell questions Sponsor Nturubika regarding 
 what the quote from Pride Student Union says. 
 • Sponsor Nturubika reads the quote from Pride Student Union. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal asks Sponsor Nturubika if he would be open 
 to adding quotes from the remaining student unions if she were able 
 to get him in contact with them. 
 • Sponsor Nturubika agrees. 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell motions to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal seconds the motion to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal motions to amend line 86 of the proclamation 
 to include the quote from Pride Student Union. 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell seconds the motion to amend line 86 of 
 the proclamation. 
 • The proclamation is amended. 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell questions Sponsor Nturubika about what 
 the senate floor presentation would look like. 
 • Sponsor Nturubika clarifies that the presenter will read the quote 
 from the proclamation. 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell motions to call the question. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal seconds the motion to call the question. 
 • Chair Rico administers a voice vote. 

The question is called. 
The proclamation passes in a 8-0-2 vote. 

 • Sponsor Nturubika gives his closing statement. 

 • Proclamation #78-018 
 
 ■ Sponsor Aihe gives an opening statement regarding proclamation #78-018, 
 which is to recognize the Inter-Residence Hall Council (IRHC) and the 
 National Residence Hall Honorary (NRHH) for their recent achievements. 

 • Sponsor yields with 4:09 for their closing. 
 • Chair Rico opens a period of general questioning. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal motions to move into roundtable discussion. 
 • Senator Nturubika seconds the motion to move into roundtable 
 discussion. 
 • Senator Nturubika speaks in pro of the proclamation, expressing his 
 knowledge of the importance and impact of the IRHC. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal speaks in pro of the proclamation. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal motions to call the question. 
 • Senator Nturubika seconds the motion to call the question. 
 • Sponsor Aihe gives a closing statement, expressing her thanks for 
 the committee. 

 Chair Rico administers a voice vote. 
 The question is called. 
 The proclamation passes in a 9-0-2 vote. 

 Closing Announcements 
 
 • Chair Rico expresses pride for the committee for handling the 
 proclamation amendment. 
 • Chair Rico encourages the committee to sign up to table at Market 
 Wednesday, as the event is run by Student Life. 
 • Chair Rico encourages senators to speak out at meetings and attend 
 with their cameras on. 
 • Vice Chair Macalintal calls attention to sidewalks failing to be ADA 
 compliant due to overgrown shrubbery. She suggests it as a simple 
 place for senators to start drafting legislation, but states that she will 
 create the draft if nobody is interested in doing so. 
 • Chair Rico clarifies that she will send out the previously discussed 
 legislation suggestion form after the meeting. 

 Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 
 • Final roll call is taken 
 • Senator Saavedra-Howell motions to adjourn. 
 • Senator Nturubika seconds. 

 Meeting adjourned at 7:36 PM.

sections.text:
RSO Allocation Committee Meeting Minutes 9/17/26 

 ● **Call to Order: 6:36 p.m.** 
 ● Land Acknowledgement: Read and acknowledged by Chair Bowen 

Initial Attendance & Quorum Veriﬁcation 

 ● Present: 
 ○ Chair Bowen 
 ○ Vice Chair Rodriguez 
 ○ Chair Perantoni 
 ○ Vice Chair Tizon 
 ○ Senator Aihe 
 ○ Chair Rico 
 ○ Senator Dewey 
 ○ Committee Member Wattkis 
 ○ Committee Member Theodros 
 ○ Committee Member Callahan 
 ● Excused: 
 ○ Senator Ferrer 
 ○ Committee Member Seibert 

Opening Announcements & Public Comment 

 ● Public Comment: None. 
 ● Chair Bowen: Welcomed returning Committee Member Amelia Callahan, noted that this 
 was the third or fourth RSOAC meeting of the semester, and expressed hope for a 
 prompt meeting. 
 ● Vice Chair Rodriguez: No announcements. 

Old Business 

 ● None. 

New Business 

1. Works of Mercy Association 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Submitted via video by President Peyton Lewis and presented in person by Cole 
 Andres. 
 ○ Opening Statement: ■ Requested $1,850 to fund "Mercy Night," a kickoff fellowship and 
 community service recruitment event scheduled for September 25th from 
 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Landis Green. 
 ■ The request included $1,000 for catering and $850 for event supplies, 
 including a canopy tent, tables, retail decor, plates, utensils, tablecloths, 
 and printing. 
 ● Procedural Motion: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to waive the 30-day submission requirement due 
 to administrative scheduling diﬃculties. 
 ○ Vote: Motion passed by roll call vote (Yes: Perantoni, Callahan, Dewey, Theodros, 
 Aihe, Rodriguez). 
 ● Questioning Period: 
 ○ Chair Perantoni: Requested an itemized breakdown of expense quotes. 
 ○ Cole Andres Response: Emailed vendor quote ranges from Publix, Walmart, 
 Sam's Club, Target, Dollar Tree, Michaels, Hobby Lobby, Staples, and Oﬃce Depot. 
 ○ Discussion: Chair Perantoni calculated baseline costs using the lowest provided 
 vendor quotes, totaling $950.02. Andres conﬁrmed no single-use plastic water 
 bottles would be purchased. 
 ● Call to Question & Vote: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to amend the requested consideration total to 
 $950.02]. 
 ○ Second: Senator Dewey seconded. Motion passed. 
 ○ Rubric & Vote: Unlocked and scored with an average score of 98. 
 ○ Allocation Outcome: $931.02 allocated. RSO representatives were instructed to 
 email Chair Perantoni and attend the Senate Finance Committee hearing next 
 Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. in the Student Union. 

2. Students for Dental Dignity (SDD) 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Video submission reviewed; presented live by Ava Gleason. 
 ○ Opening Statement: 
 ■ Requested $2,000 for semester programming across 7 General Body 
 Meetings, comprising $700 for food ($100/meeting), $800 for oral 
 hygiene service kits (toothbrushes, toothpaste, ﬂoss), and $500 for 
 promotional merchandise. 
 ● Questioning Period & Pre-Questioning Analysis: 
 ○ Prior to bringing the presenter in, the committee calculated lowest quote rates: 
 Chick-ﬁl-A catering ($100/meeting), member shirts ($460 for 50), and dental gear 
 ($40.49 for a 300-count kit). 
 ○ Ava Gleason Response: Clariﬁed that a 300-count kit lasts two meetings (~120 
 kits/meeting), requiring 4 bulk orders across 7 general body meetings. ○ Recalculation: Chair Perantoni recalculated dental supplies to $283.43 (4 x 
 $40.49 + adjustment), bringing the total consideration to $1,443.43. 
 ● Call to Question & Vote: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to amend total consideration to $1,443.43. 
 ○ Second: Senator Dewey seconded. Motion passed. 
 ○ Rubric & Vote: Entered and scored with an average score of 99.1. 
 ○ Allocation Outcome: $1,430.54 allocated. Presenter directed to email Chair 
 Perantoni and attend the Senate meeting on Wednesday at 7:30 p.m.. 

3. Undergraduate Mock Trial Club 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Summarized live by Aneesa Sukhwani. 
 ○ Opening Statement: 
 ■ Requested $590 for 50 team-wide member shirts from Custom Ink based 
 on prior year pricing. 
 ● Questioning Period: 
 ○ Chair Bowen & Chair Perantoni: Inquired whether three vendor quotes were 
 provided as required by ﬁnancial statutes. 
 ○ Aneesa Sukhwani Response: Stated only one quote was submitted due to 
 unclear submission instructions and offered to gather additional quotes. 
 ● Motion & Outcome: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to table the request until next week to allow the 
 organization time to obtain three vendor quotes. 
 ○ Second: Vice Chair Rodriguez seconded. 
 ○ Outcome: Request tabled until next week's meeting. 

4. Irresistible Garnettes 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Video presentation reviewed; presented live by Harmony Pierre-Louis. 
 ○ Opening Statement: 
 ■ Requested $2,300 for semester operations, including $2,000 for Leech 
 Recreation Center studio practice space ($40/hour), $280 for 20 folding 
 chairs, and $20 for a portable speaker. 
 ● Questioning & Deliberation Period: 
 ○ Committee Discussion: Expressed surprise and concern over FSU Campus 
 Recreation charging RSOs $40/hour for multi-purpose practice studio space. 
 ○ Chair Perantoni: Noted the policy change took effect August 10, 2026, and 
 pledged to raise the issue in Senate and contact university administration to seek 
 free access for RSOs[74]. ○ Vice Chair Rodriguez: Noted that only single quotes were submitted for the 
 folding chairs and speaker]. 
 ● Motion & Outcome: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to table the request until next week to allow the 
 organization to obtain three vendor quotes for equipment while he investigates 
 the Leech facility fee. 
 ○ Second: Senator Dewey seconded. 
 ○ Outcome: Request tabled until next week's meeting. 

5. Flavor Society 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Video presentation submitted by President Emily Pierce; no representative 
 present live. 
 ○ Opening Statement: 
 ■ Requested $160 for ingredients (syrups, fruit, sodas, heavy cream) and 
 supplies for "Potions and Poisons," an educational mocktail and dirty 
 soda event teaching food science product development and alcohol 
 metabolism. 
 ● Questioning & Deliberation Period: 
 ○ Vice Chair Rodriguez: Suggested zero-funding to redirect the organization to the 
 RSO Development Fund. 
 ○ Advisor Veronica Nelson & Chair Perantoni: Advised against zero-funding 
 without verifying whether the organization had already used their Development 
 Fund allocation. 
 ● Motion & Outcome: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to table the request until next week to allow Chair 
 Bowen to email the organization and clarify their Development Fund status. 
 ○ Second: Vice Chair Rodriguez seconded. 
 ○ Outcome: Request tabled until next week's meeting. 

6. Mexican-American Student Association (MASA) 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Video submission presented by Treasurer Jorge Rodriguez; representative joined 
 live. 
 ○ Opening Statement: 
 ■ Requested $300 from the RSO Development Fund for cultural 
 programming expenses and supplies (aluminum tin engraving and 
 Independence Day event). 
 ● Questioning Period & Guidance: ○ Chair Perantoni: Clariﬁed that the $300 Development Fund is automatically 
 granted to RSOs via FSU HQ under Student Body Treasurer Maddox Goodman 
 and does not require RSOAC committee approval. 
 ● Call to Question & Vote: 
 ○ Motion: Vice Chair Rodriguez moved to zero-fund the RSOAC request so the 
 organization could apply directly through the FSU HQ Development Fund portal. 
 ○ Second: Senator Dewey seconded. 
 ○ Vote: Motion passed; request zero-funded by RSOAC (redirected to FSU HQ 
 Development Fund portal). 

7. DREAM Incorporated (Florida State Chapter) 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Video submission reviewed; presented live by President Wanya Clayton and 
 Aleria Lester. 
 ○ Opening Statement: 
 ■ Requested $1,300 ($1,285.50 calculated) for 143 member shirts 
 ($986.70) and 24 executive board name tags ($298 plus shipping) for 
 community service projects and campus outreach. 
 ● Questioning & Deliberation Period: 
 ○ Vice Chair Rodriguez: Raised statutory concerns regarding funding executive 
 board name tags, referencing proviso limits on Class Council. 
 ○ Advisor Veronica Nelson: Clariﬁed that while executive shirts are prohibited, 
 name tags fall under oﬃce supplies and are not explicitly banned by statute. 
 ○ Wanya Clayton & Aleria Lester Response: Emphasized that name tags provide 
 essential visibility during community service and campus tabling events. 
 ○ Chair Perantoni: Spoke in favor of funding, praising the presentation and ﬁscal 
 responsibility. 
 ● Call to Question & Vote: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Perantoni moved to unlock the rubric at the requested 
 consideration total of $1,285.50. 
 ○ Second: Senator Dewey seconded. 
 ○ Rubric & Vote: Completed with an average score of 99.07. 
 ○ Allocation Outcome: $1,273.53 allocated[143][145]. Representatives directed to 
 email Chair Perantoni and attend the Senate meeting on Wednesday at 7:30 p.m.. 

8. American Marketing Association (AMA FSU) 

 ● Request Presentation: 
 ○ Video submission reviewed; presented live by VP of Corporate Relations Chase 
 Conte and Gregory Feinberg. 
 ○ Opening Statement: ■ Requested $3,000 to support a corporate tour to New York City (October 
 21–24, 2026) for 16 members visiting Spotify, Madison Square Garden, 
 EY Studio Plus, and the New York Times. 
 ● Questioning & Deliberation Period: 
 ○ Chair Perantoni: Noted travel funding is capped at $250 per student ($4,000 
 maximum for 16 students). 
 ○ Chase Conte & Gregory Feinberg Response: Explained that the College of 
 Business will cover hotels but not ﬂights, requesting RSOAC shift allocation to 
 cover ﬂights ($3,200 total for 16 round-trip tickets from Orlando at ~$200/ticket) 
 and Madison Square Garden tour fees ($29/person). 
 ○ Discussion: Committee praised the thorough quote research and preparation. 
 ● Call to Question & Vote: 
 ○ Motion: Vice Chair Rodriguez moved to enter rubric at $4,000.00. 
 ○ Second: Senator Dewey seconded. 
 ○ Rubric & Vote: Completed with a perfect average score of 100. 
 ○ Allocation Outcome: $4,000.00 allocated. Presenters were instructed to email 
 Chair Perantoni and attend the Senate meeting next Wednesday. 

Meeting Allocation Summary 

 ● Initial Total Amount Requested: $7,678.95 
 ● Overall Average Score: 39.61 (reﬂecting zero-funded requests) 
 ● Total Amount Allocated: $7,635.09 

Closing Announcements 

 ● Chair Perantoni: Expressed deep dissatisfaction with Campus Recreation charging RSOs 
 for studio practice space and announced plans to consult with Senator Torres regarding 
 forming a Senate Finance investigative committee. 
 ● Senator Dewey: Thanked the committee for a smooth ﬁrst meeting experience. 
 ● Chair Bowen: Thanked committee members for a successful session. 

Final Attendance & Adjournment 

 ● Final Quorum Veriﬁcation: Conducted by Vice Chair Rodriguez 
 ○ Present: Chair Bowen, Chair Perantoni, Senator Aihe, Chair/Senator Rico, Senator 
 Dewey, Commissioner Wattkis, Commissioner Theodros, Commissioner 
 Callahan, Vice Chair Rodriguez 
 ○ Excused: Commissioner Ferrer, Commissioner Seaver 
 ○ Absent: President Holiday 
 ● Adjournment Motion: 
 ○ Motion: Chair Bowen adjourned the meeting. 
 ● Meeting Adjourned: 9:04 p.m
