Attachment #1- July 20th meeting minutes 
Call to Order: 6:32pm 
II. Pledge of Allegiance 
Steven: Skipped due to zoom 
III. Roll Call 
IV. Reading and approval of the Minutes 
Steven: The June 1st meeting minutes are attached 
Steven: Could I get a motion for approval? 
Joey motions, Claire seconds the motion. 
Steven: Hearing no objection, the meeting have been approved. 
V. Petitions into the Assembly 
None. 
VI. Special Introductions and Student Comments 
Steven: There are several groups here. No need to introduce your bill, but if any of the guest members 
would like to introduce themselves, feel free. 
Ramisa: Hi, I am the president of Bangladeshi Student Association, happy to be here. 
Mallory: Hi, I’m Mallory McCray. I am the president of LSC for 2026-2027, and I am happy to be here. 
Steven: Thank you very much, we appreciate you all being here. 
VII. Messages from Student Government 
None. 
VIII. Report from the Office of Governmental Affairs 
 
IX. Report of Officers 
Report of the Speaker (Steven) 
Steven: This is our last meeting of the semester. I don’t have that many announcements, except for all 
orientations. We would enjoy having COGS representatives there to represent us, and we tell the students 
what COGS can do for them, including a PowerPoint. It will be occurring in the last two weeks of 
August. 17-21, 24-28. I will try to be at all of them, however if you can note August 20, 27, and 28, those 
specific dates I am unavailable. If anyone is able to help, one of those three dates would be especially 
appreciated. I will send out a calendar invite. 
Our first meeting will be in fall on September 7th. 
Report of the Deputy Speaker for Finance (Joey) 
 Not much. A new fiscal has begun, so the Sunshine bill being discussed later tonight has not taken effect. 
 Still figuring out the new platform, and there is an updated financial report attached in the meeting 
agenda. 
Steven: To clarify, our budget is completely reset, but it is mostly the same in grants, but a large slash in 
the reserves. This is a major change for our fiscal year; if you have any questions, reach out to Joey or I. 
Report of the Deputy Speaker for Communications (Claire) 
Not too many updates, I want to just emphasis the importance of the orientation dates and showing off 
COGS. 
Report of the Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs (Nicholette) 
I may be sending out a small survey of what drew you to COGS. 
Report of the Deputy Speaker for Advocacy (DeSean) 
Hi, for those who didn’t see, we did a great donation to the food pantry. We donated a little over $1800 of 
food to the pantry. They were very grateful, and we are hoping to continue this. Should to those who were 
able to join and help out, it was a huge help. You can go to the Instagram if you want to see photos. 
Advisor Announcements (Tanner McKinley) 
I am looking forward to Fall. You all are up to Election coming up in the fall. We are 11 weeks away 
from Election week, and we have a new supervisor of election and should hopefully have them in place 
soon. 
Highlight our leadership Exec board. I am very proud of both them and the representatives. 
For the MSC AND LSC Bills; I saw Section I of the LSC bill it says Fall 2025-2026. In MSC it says 
Spring. We should make a motion to alter those. 
Also, FSU HQ. The long-term plan is to migrate all forms to FSU HQ by the end of the year. We need to 
be careful and diligent about moving over the grant from. It will be easier to have all the forms in one 
central place for students. If you have any questions, send me an email. Thank you for all the hard work 
Steven: We hope to have it mostly done by Fall. 
XI. Committee Introductions and Reports 
Steven: Skipped as we do not meet over the summer. However, new reps, please look around and decide 
what committee you would like to join. If you know already, please reach out to the Exec Board. Besides 
that, we can move forward. 
Steven: We now have four bills for tonight. Two from groups, one is Sunset, and one is for Bangladeshi 
Society. 
XII. Funding Requests 
Bill #20- Sunset Bill 
Steven: 3 minutes for intro 
Joseph: Briefly explains that one grant can be obtained for $600, or $700 for two in total. We passed this 
bill last year with a sunset to discuss the implicates of this bill. We have decided the best course of action 
is to reduce the one time pay to $525. It will go into effect the next cycle as not to blindsight people. 
Additionally, there is another sunset implemented into this bill for next spring. 
Steven: Thank you, any questions? 
Steven: Hearing none, moving to pro 
Desean: I am grateful for Joey’s hard work, and I’m glad we will decide this earlier next year. 
Steven: Thank you, any other comments? 
Steven: I can add that it’s not easy to reduce this kind of funding, but given the current funding situation 
we are facing, as well as an influx of grant submissions, it was a good number for the committee to 
conclude upon, and I enjoy the implementation of a sunset bill. 
Steven: Motion to call to question? 
Desean motions to call to question, Logan Lamb seconds 
Steven: seeing no objections, we will vote. Please use the emoji hand. 
13-0-1 
Joey: Thank you to everyone on sunset committee. I’m happy with the conclusion we came to. 
Bill#21- BSA’s 2026 Eid X Bengali New Year 
Steven: I am sponsoring this bill, so I will hand the floor to Joey. 
Joey: For Bill #21, Deputy Seaker Steve, you have three minutes for opening 
Steven: This bill is for BSA. It is for 2026 Eid and New Years celebration. The funding will include food 
and decorate. The second page has additional information from the organization. The event will be next 
week, with an estimated attendance of 200 people. 
I do want to mention that this organization has already received funds for this event, but this event 
happens irregularly, and it is happening twice this year. Their budget only budgeted for one event this 
year, however it occurs twice this year. Their executive board is here and may be able to better explain. 
Joey: Thank you, we will move into questions. 
Desean: When is the next celebration? 
Ramisa: This is the first celebration, but the next one will occur in April. We have had multiple events 
throughout the year, the budget was used up by other events. We had events we did not budget for the 
current fiscal year and that is where a lot of the money was spent. That is why we are asking for this 
event. 
Desean: That makes sense, thank you. So the next one is in April; are you planning to request money for 
the next one as well? 
Ramisa: No, that is included in our budget. 
 Steven: I can clarify. Since the event is happening twice in the fiscal allocation, they are asking COGS to 
 cover the one that is this week, and then will use their budget for the April event. 
Hussaini: Last time, in April you were in COGS requesting for an Eid. Is this the same event? 
 Steven: Yes. According to meeting minutes, it was denied as there were outstanding questions from the 
 representatives, as the executive members were not there to answer. 
 Ramisa: Yes that answers it. 
 Hussaini: Which EID is being celebrated, please clarify which one 
 Ramisa: Eid al-Fitr and Lunar near year 
 Hussaini: Didn’t those occur a month or two ago? 
 Ramisa: Yes. We typically celebrate those together. It was delayed due to funding issues, our treasurer 
 has had personal issues. 
 Hussaini: Okay, thank you. 
 Joey: any other questions? 
 Desean: In the event that you are unable to fund the other events throughout the year - I have a question; 
 do you all keep track of how much money you are expecting, or are you only relying on the number in 
 FSU HQ? 
 Ramisa: When we asked for the annual budget for next year, and we utilized the budget that we were 
 allocated to estimate our spending allocation. 
 Desean: Thank you. Do you know the number? 
 Ramisa: Around $7000 or $8000. 
 Steven: $7,800 is the total allocation. $2500 is allocated for the combined celebration. 
 Joey: What is your budget for this event in the spring 
 Ramisa: I will have to look. 
 Steven: $2500 
 Joey: Why is this request so much larger? 
 Ramisa: Yes, the number of students involved in the organization increase exponentially. 
 Joey: motion to extend the time? 
 Desean makes the motion to extend the time for 7 minutes, Claire seconds 
 Joey: Do you expect to be back in the spring if the growth is the reason? 
 Ramisa: We plan to re-use decor. The main spending that comes in is the food. We do not expect to come 
 in again, and we expect to make do with the $2500. 
 Steven: First, along with the $2500 allocated to this specific event, and you are allocated $1000 in 
 discretionary funds. So how can we justify over half of your fiscal year budget to be allocated tonight 
 given these circumstances? 
 Ramisa: I am going to pass it over to Shihab Sharar as some of the past funds were spent at his discretion. 
Shihab Sharar: There is already a proposal for the event in April. We have two celebrations 
Steven: Why 4,000 however? 
Shihab: We were unable to accurately estimate our costs. Additionally, our organization has grown. 
Additionally, we added more events that were not initially included in our budget. These events helped 
boost engagement. We also had issues with financial platforms and purchase orders. There were missing 
Amazon packages. If that makes sense. 
Steven: Yeah, I guess. I am done asking questions, thank you. 
 Desean: So first, motion to add 7 minutes. 
 Seconded by parker. 
 Desean: So, your materials didn’t get delivered from Amazon. Wouldn’t you get a refund? 
 Shihab: I believe it went back to COGS. What happens? 
 Steven: It gets swept 
 Hussaini: I know last time the bill was declined since a representative was not there. We were unable to 
 hear where the money was and how it was spent. 
 Shihab: unfortunately, the treasures mother passed away. 
 Hussaini: Okay, but how can the past spending be justified? 
Shihab: Our budget is created by the previous president. Our previous president did not expect so many 
events to occur. Tennis tournament. Pinned all on previous president. The budget was allocated before we 
came into leadership. 
Ramisa is proposing the current budget, but she will be off the board in the Fall after elections. So, the 
next president will not know what was budgeted. That is what occurred to me. I added some events based 
on the current trends that were not included in the current budget, 
Hussaini: So how do you know this will not occur? 
Shihab: We have the data now. I believe we have a strong position that we will not come back, as we will 
project how the community is increasing. 
Steven: motion to extend time for last three questions. 
Joey, Sadio seconds 
Nicholette: Why did you not come earlier in the year around March or April and asked COGS to fund the 
unplanned events opposed to utilizing the other funds that were allocated for the Eid event? 
Shihab: I did ask about that with Jack. He said there was no time. I asked Jack if we could spend the 
money on other events. 
Desean: My concern is that we are allocating your budget for a specific event. It is concerning that the 
budget is not being used for what it was allocated for. I am not understanding why the next president can 
just add events. 
Shihab: It does not occur typically. The previous president left without a budget. This will not occur now. 
Parker: You said 200 people are attending; what are you basing that upon and how are you estimating 
those numbers? 
Shihab: We are basing participation on previous years. The recent trend has changed to graduate students 
bringing their families. We now adjusted this. 
Parker: Is there a form for people to RSVP so that you are better able to budget? 
Shihab: Yes, we have tried but some do not register as they are not students. We ask the Lakefront staff to 
count the attendees. 
Joey: Done with questions, into a round of pro. 
Desean: I want to speak in pro as I am supportive of the event, but I think the amount should be reduced. I 
understand the circumstances, but it may be more responsible for COGS to reduce the funding amount. 
Joey: I support the event, but I am making a motion to adjust the bill $2500 as general expenses and the 
organization can distribute it as they please on this specific event. 
Steven: That motion is for the second round of pro. It has been a pleasure working with the organization 
and they have been diligent about trying to work this issue out. 
Joey: Thank you, anyone else. 
Sadio: Definitely in support, but I agree with Steven and Desean that it should be reduced. It may be a 
good idea to prepare a more clear and concise statement of what this event entails. 
Joey: Anyone else? Seeing none, does anyone have anything to say in con of the bill? 
Joey: hearing none, moving into a second round of question. I move to motion to strike the allocated 
amount to $2500 in the manner described above? 
Joey: Questions about the amendment? 
Steven: Do we want to bring it to account for the $900 they have been allocated for discretionary? I only 
ask because our reserves our low. We would allocate $1600 in total. 
Desean: Maybe meet in the middle and say $2000 in total? 
Joey: I will advocate for $2000. 
Parker: Is there a way to put this on the back burner? We could allow them to spend the money allocated 
to the Eid celebration on this event, and then they could request money in the Spring. 
Steven: It could work, yes. 
Joey: we are still on pros and cons for this amendment. 
Madison: What if we did a meet in the middle of what Parker and Joey has said. Maybe we allocate them 
$1600 now and allow them to transfer. 
 Desean: I changed my mind; I agree with Parker that we should wait. I know they said they wouldn’t add 
 an event, but they may. No shade towards the organization, I am just concerned the money could be used 
 on something else. I would be in con of Joey’s amendment 
Steven: Motion to cancel Joey’s motion. 
Joey: I will withdraw. Onto Parker’s motion, they will be given a transfer of this Spring budgeted line 
item to be utilized on this event and then can return in the Spring and ask for funding for the April Eid 
event. 
Desean: I am in pro; it is a good idea to see how the new changes with the new board will go. 
Joey: I agree. Great motion Parker, as it lets them meet in the middle. 
Joey: Anyone motion to call to question? 
Madison: I motion 
Bella: I second. 
Joey: Round of voting. For the current event being requested, the funding they are allocating being . then 
coming back. We are voting on the amended bill, and redirected to use the Fiscal funding that was 
allocated for this event in April 
Steven: Any questions? To clarify, voting yes will not allocate additional money, it will vote yes on the 
amendment. 
Ramisa: To clarify, to the $2500 for the April event will be disbursed into account now? 
Steven: It already has been disbursed, this amendment will authorize that money’s use on the event 
currently on the floor. 
Joey: Thank you, Steven. Onto voting. 
The motion passes 16-0-1 
Joey: Parker’s motion is passed. 
Tanner in the chat: The $2,500 will not show in FSUHQ due to the migration to the new software. 
However, the funds are there. To access these funds, please email lmckinney@fsu.edu. 
 XIV. New Business 
 Bill #22- LSC Annual Budget 
Steven: Thank you all, but we need to move on to LSC and MSC. 
Steven: Now onto LSC. Joey is up. 
Joey: LSC allocated the budget through their own process. And Mallory and the board was great to work 
with and sit in on the meeting. This occurs every year, I waive my time unless Mallory would like to 
comment. 
Mallory: Thank you, Joey. We did two different deliberation processes and then had an appeal. After all 
of that, we are at $51K for the Fall semester. 
 Steven: Thank you. Any questions? 
 Joey: Are there more events expected in the Spring? 
 Mallory: Yes. That, and barristers utilizes a large amount. We allocated 10,000 addition this time around. 
 Joey: Thank you. For clarification, barrister’s is law school prom. 
 Steven: Thank you. Any other questions? 
 Steven: That’s how you know it’s a good budget if there are no questions. 
 Parker: I appreciated the inclusion of the minutes. I know LSC does good work, so I am in pro. 
 Madison: Yes, I sat in on these calls. The team did a great job at following COGS Code and I’d like to 
 commend them in this process. 
 Mallory: Thank you, Maddie, it was helpful having you there. 
 Desean: I echo previous comments. 
 Joey: Very good job on the bill. 
 Steven: I agree. Great job on this bill, A+ job. 
 Steven: Any cons? 
 Steven: Hearing none, second round of question. I will raise an amendment to correct the typo in the LSC 
 Budget Bill which states “Fall 2025-2026” to “2026-2027”. 
 Steven: hearing no further amendments, motion to call to questions? 
 Desean motions to pass the bill as amended, Madison seconds. 
 Steven: Voting. 
 14-0-1 
 Steven: Great job. 
 Mallory: Is now an alright time for a question? 
Steven: You have a three-minute closing? 
Mallory: What is the timeframe for disbursement? 
Steven: Likely two weeks, you can contact Laurel. 
 Mallory: Thank you so much, feel free to reach out if you ever need anything from LSC. Have a great 
 night. 
 Bill #23- MSC Annual Budget 
 Steven: Great, we are on MSC Bill. 
 Bella: This bill is proposing our budget for the Fall semester. We use the Spring budget to adjust their 
 budget accordingly. The Fall is higher request as there are more medical students on campus. 
 Daniel: Hi everyone, thank you for being here. Generally, we spend the money with a few goals; 
 education and professional development. There are some skills or opportunity that we do not get in our 
 formal education, so that is the goal. One example is the surgery interest group; they get to experience 
 unique experiences. I personally have benefitted from these events. The money also goes towards holistic 
 events, such as pride, women’s health, or black history month. One important part of the professional is 
 being a well-rounded human. The only other thing to mention is we are doing this differently than last 
year. We are proposing a separate Fall and Spring budget. That, and the number we are asking for is very 
similar than last year, except a $400 decrease. 
Steven: Thank you. Are there any questions? 
Steven: No questions? Then onto a period of pro. 
Steven: I can personally say I’m grateful and benefit from the events funded by this allocation. They not 
only fund medical students, but PhD and other students. This team is a great team and put in the extra 
time. Bella and Daniel have been great to work with. 
Steven: Any other pros? Hearing none, onto a period of con. 
Steven: Hearing no cons, onto a second round of questioning. 
Steven: Does anyone motion to correct the text “Spring 2026” in section 1 to “Fall 2026”? 
Desean motioned, Parker seconded. 
Steven: Motion to call to question? 
Terrance motioned to call to question, Madison seconded. 
Steven: The bill passed 14 – 0 – 3. You have time for a closing 
Bella: Thank you! 
Daniel: Thank you everyone and thank you Steven. 
Steven: Thank you everyone. We will not dip into round table, but are there any closing announcements? 
Desean: To clarify, you will send out an email to sign up for the Orientations? 
Steven: Yes, expect the email around the beginning of August. 
Madison: I have a question about travel grants. Can the law school organization EASL request travel 
funds? 
Joey: Yes. They should be fine. 
Steven: Thank you everyone. I will see you all in September for the first meeting of the semester. I 
appreciate everyone for their time tonight. 
XVIII. Next Meeting: September 7th, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. (First Fall 2026 meeting)

sections.heading: 8-31-2026 COGS Meeting Minutes
sections.text:
August 31, 2026 - COGS Meeting Minutes 

Steven: Meeting has begun at 6:40. Welcome back everyone. 

Steven: I have a PowerPoint to update everyone. 

Steven: Please stand for the pledge. 

Steven: Reading and approval of the July 20th meeting, they are attached to the agenda. Does 
anyone have any questions? Hearing none, can I get an appproval. 

Joey approves, DeSean seconds. 

Hearing no objections, meeting minutes are approved. 

Steven; Hearing no Student comments, anyone from the office of government affairs? 

Steven: Hearing none, I’d like to introduce the new dean of graduate students, Gregory Bell. 

Gregory Bell: Thank you for the warm welcome, I am new to FSU. Prior to FSU, I worked 
within various graduate institutions in different universities. I just wanted to tell you about 
myself, my goal is to create a sense of community with graduate students. Community is highly 
correlated to success in your program. There are two things you need to be successful; 1. You 
have someone who has your back, academically and professionally and personally. Second, you 
need to be that person for someone else. That is what community is, and therefore what your 
network is. Building a network is about making connections with anyone and everyone on 
campus and building communities. If you approach an FSU alum, you have an immediate bond, 
so please embrace it. When I was at my previous institution, I served as the COGS advisor; I saw 
that we built it into an organization that provides funding and community. Those small 
interactions are important between students. That's a bit about me; I am happy to answer 
questions or talk more. I view COGS as a way to receive feedback from graduate students. My 
hope is to have an open dialogue and community. 

Steven: Despite Dean Bell only being here a month, he has already gone above and beyond with 
Orientation sessions. Can we take a picture before he leaves? 

Steven: Thank you. Be careful when driving everyone, Tallahassee drivers can be crazy. 

Steven: All of campus was closed for the month of August, but COGS was busy. Thank you to 
all of those who attended orientation sessions. There were 12 sessions with great turn out; we 
have had great interest with petitions after these sessions, so it is a great way to recruit students 

Just a heads up, there is one more tabling opportunity through the GSRC coming up. GSRC hosts 
a lot of great events and has a lot of resources. They offer a lot of similar services, but just have 
some different rules for who can receive funding. This is their leadership team on the 
PowerPoint. DeSean will be leading the tabling event. If you’d like to join him, please feel free to reach out to 
us. 

One major success we had that week was being invited to the main Fall 2026 new graduate 
student orientation. We co-hosted a social for new graduate studnets. The demand was high, and 
the food was gone within 30 minutes. We had a lot of great partners show up, and Strozier was 
rented out for us. DeSean also deserves a shout out, as he organized a music event at the social. 
Thank you, I know that took a lot of work. 

Then we also presented at the main orientation session. There was probably 750+ people who 
attended the main orientation session. Thank you to all those who attended. 

Last update, shoutout for the Graduate Lounge International Coffee Hour at the Globe. The 
undergrads are there two, but the two dates on the PowerPoint you will have seperate lounge for 
graduate students and music will be played. 

My favorite part is the food, but they also have coffee and tea. Its fun to check out and wanted to 
shout out that event. 

As promised, that’s it from me. I want to give a heads up that I will be stepping down from 
speaker. Therefore, there will be at least one paid executive board position open. The election wil 
be on the first Monday of November. I can't speak for other exec board members. Joey, your turn 

Joey: Awesome. Glad to have everyone back. We have presentation grants going well, we are 
looking to shift the system we do grants on to FSU HQ. You can see on the budget this is 
updated, the budget was updated after orientation events. Not much to talk about, but let’s spend 
as much money as we can. Other than that, not much else. 

Steven: Can you describe the report a bit more? 

Joey: Yes. Each line item shows a different expenditure, what is allocated to it, and what is 
currently available. 

Desean: I have a question. We have allocated 85,000 to presentation grants? 

Joey: Yes. There are more to get through as well. The cycle is almost over. 

Desean: did we decide on the graduate assistant position? 

Steven: That is separate. Just so everyone knows, we had this position allocated, however we did 
not see a need for it in the previous year. It is on the main budget that is separate from this list 

Joey: Reserves are different from COGS expenses/food/clothes and awards. Reserves is leftover 
budget that is unused; the other line items are different. The fiscal year ends around June and 
thats when we aim to use a large amount of the COGS reserves 

Desean: Can we get FSU’s shoe? Steven: ??? 

Steven: We managed to get the funding for our current merch from the prior fiscal year. 

Desean: Look at the shoes. 

Jania: That looks cool! 

Steven: anyways if you guys have questions, I am able to utilize my speakers fund at my 
discretion. We used this fund to support an event put on by CHAOS, and we did this right before 
this meeting. Just wanted to make you aware in case Joey wants to transfer the reserves to 
speakers fund later down the line. 

Steven: Any last questions for Joey? Just a heads up, we have less money allocated this summer. 
When we meet with the Florida Board of Trustees we need to say we have wisely utilized our 
budget. 

Steven: Hearing no final questions, Desean. 

Desean: I hope everyone had a great summer. First, I want to mention that we provided $1800 
worth of supplies for the food pantry, and I went in earlier this week, and all of those items are 
no longer there; which is great sense it demonstrates a need. I am also meeting soon with 
someone in applied American policy and politic department. That is pretty much it, except for a 
personal update. It is my first opera at FSU, if you ever have read Mice and Men and I am 
playing Lenny, we are doing and operatic version of it. I may be bringing a bill to do some 
community partnership. I am interested in partnering with other offices to advocate for disabled 
individuals. It is October 30 in Ruby Diamond. It is $10. On Sunday it is at 2:30 or 3:30 in the 
same place, I’ll be in both shows. 

Jania: Please remind us closer to the date. 

Desean: It will not sell out, Ruby is a 1200-person theater. It is a modern opera, and the tickets 
are currently on sale. It's under 2 hours. I think all the lead parts are graduate students. 

Steven: Desean has been voluntold to do the national anthem, and I am always excited to hear it, 
everyone is always shocked. 

Steven: Thanks you. Claire, thank you for coming out on your birthday. 

Claire: It’s great to see everyone in person. Orientation sessions were successful, thank you 
everyone. The transit app is now currently live. It shows you the live location of all buses on a 
route and updates in real time. NightNole was discontinued for Safe FSU; unfortunately there 
was not enough demonstrated need, and it was difficult to demonstrate that it was open to public 
use as stipulated in the grant. The admin believed that students were not using it. Now with Safe 
FSU for a specific boundary you can ride for a flat fee of $6. 

Budget report I am currently editing in Canva, but it is almost done and I will send out soon. Steven: We will also need to do the Oath later tonight for Claire to officially be sworn in. 

Steven: Claire has been helping out all summer, it was just time to officially induct her since we 
are in person. 

Steven: Report from our advisor who also won an award this year. 

Tanner: Thank you everyone, I did not expect the award. I was the very last award in the very 
back of the room, not expecting a thing, and Andy, my boss, says I need to sit up. I was so 
confused, and I didnt even hear what the award was, and I just heard my name. It was really 
cool, I am thankful. 

Tanner: note to everyone. We are meeting today because next Monday is Labor Day. The next 
COGS meeting will be on September 21. I want to shoutout Joey, as he’s been handling FSU 
HQ. He’s been handling moving over our grant applications and centralizing all of COGS forms 
onto one website. Joey has fully built it out and we have a meeting next week, and I’m hoping to 
have an hour after COGS after September 21 and break the application, because the form has to 
launch October 1st. I do not want to launch an important form that doesn't work. If you have to 
leave you are fine, but we’d love to test it out. Shoutout Joey and Steven for their work in this. 

You all will be on the Fall ballot. There are also opinion questions on the fall ballot. The campus 
pulse commission is Thursday, September 3rd?. This commission is involved in placing opinion 
questions on the fall ballot. If you do decide to come, be mindful of your questions. Think about 
bebing specific; for example, what does “underserved” mean? Make sure you are being 
deliberate about your word choices, and the question is measurable. 

The SGA newsletter used to be monthly, but this year we found it chaotic. We are now doing 
twice a semester; the first one can be an introduction of E-board and other things, and at the end 
of the semester can be a review of what your organization has done. These will be sent to you all 
likely in late September. Please check it out; it’s interesting to see what SGA is funding, anyone 
who is a line item in their budget can submit. 

Elections are oct 12 and 13. Even though you all have petitioned in, you must fill out a 
declaration of candidacy. Most COGS people run opposed, and you must place your name on the 
ballot. I will keep you all updated. SGA’s version of redistricting, reappointment, etc; it is 
moving seats. The supervisor of elections will join us for a meeting as well. 

Then, the Fall inauguration is Tuesday, December 1st at 5pm; you all will have a spot. Please 
attend, it is at the ballroom and there is free food. The event is open to everyone. 

Steven: The dinner is great. 

Tanner: It is a really great event, and you all deserve to celebrate. 

Steven: I will also be giving my outgoing speech. Tanner: There are also awards. I would also like everyone to consider running for Speaker. It can 
be intimidating but there is a great foundation for transition, I really encourage everyone to ask 
questions or reach out. That's all from me, thank you. 

Steven: If there are any questions about where COGS sits in SGA, the website explains it clearly. 
You all have full access to the office that is housed near SGA individuals. We have the 
undergrad executive team and the graduate senate, which is similar to an undergraduate 
counterpart of COGS. We therefore still need to be on the ballot, and if you do not put your 
name down on this ballot, you will not be on COGS. I don't have the authority to make an 
exception. It’s happened once, please let that be a good warning. Be on the lookout for those 
emails. That will start the 35th Graduate student. The new Speaker will also give an introduction 
speech. Any other questions I am available. 

Steven: That is it for introductions. There are some QR codes on this PowerPoint. We have the 
COGS Committee information. We have a list assigning everyone to a committee tonight. 

Steven: If you would like, please separate your committees. 

Steven: Thank you everyone. Congrats to Jania, the chair of Outreach. Outreach will select a vice 
chair next meeting. Advocacy will be meeting on the 14th at 7pm and getting food together. 
Elections will occur then. Internal Affairs, Rasleen is the chair, and Parker is the vice chair. 
Congrats everyone. If everyone newly brought in can stick around after the meeting. 

Steven: Anyone want to waive? 

Jania: No please! 

Steven: We will do short updates. 

Round table occurred 

Logan: I will sadly be stepping down from COGS. I enjoyed my experience here deeply and will 
still be attending COGS events. 

Steven: Thank you Logan, we are sad to see you go. Thank you everyone for doing roundtable. 

Steven: Thank you everyone for coming out tonight. The meeting is adjourned at 8:14, but 
please stay for cake.

sections.text:
STUDENT LIFE COMMITTEE 
 August 29, 2026 at 12:30 PM 
 Location: (Location or Zoom Link) 
 MEETING MINUTES 

 Call to Order 
 Acting Chair Macalintal called the meeting to order at 12:32 PM. 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 
 Acting Chair Macalintal acknowledged the Land Acknowledgement. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
 Acting Chair Macalintal verified quorum had been met. 
 
 Present: Macalintal, Rico, Noel, Saavedra Howell, Vivian, Urrea-Perez, 
 Dawkins, Finman, Ambroggio, Nturubika, Owens, Amirzadeh, Ramos 
 
 Absent: Maxwell (U), Santos (U), Engelhard (U), Re (U), Soto (U) 

 Public Comment 
 N/A 

 Opening Announcements 
 Acting Chair Macalintal thanks the committee for blocking out time for this 
 special session and announces that the new chair of the Student Life 
 Committee will be responsible for organizing a final committee meeting time 
 for Fall. 

 Old Business 
 N/A 

 New Business 

• Chair Election 
 
 ■ Acting Chair Macalintal entertains a motion to open the floor for the Student 
 Life Chair nominations. 
 Senator Rico moves to entertain the motion. 
 Senator Noel seconds. 
 
 Acting Chair Macalintal questions if there are any nominations for Chair at 
 this time. 
 Senator Nturubika motions to nominate himself for Chair. 
 Acting Chair Macalintal announces self-nominations are not permitted, and 
 a member of the committee must nominate him, followed by a second. 
 Acting Chair Macalintal asks if any member of the committee would like to 
 nominate Senator Nturubika? 
 Senator Vivian nominates Senator Nturubika. 
 Senator Owens seconds. 
 Senator Nturubika accepts his nomination 
 Acting Chair Macalintal asks if there are any more nominations on the floor. 
 Senator Noel nominates Senator Rico. 
 Senator Vivian seconds. 
 Senator Rico accepts her nomination. 
 Acting Chair Macalintal asks if there are any more nominations on the floor. 
 Seeing none, Acting Chair Macalintal entertains a motion to close the 
 Student Life Committee Chair nominations. 
 Senator Noel motions to close the floor. 
 Senator Vivian seconds. 
 
 Acting Chair Macalintal runs through the procedure for Chair elections with 
 the committee. 
 
 Senator Nturubika gives an opening statement stating that under his Chair-
 ship, he will encourage the committee to become more proactive and 
 interactive with the Student Body instead of waiting for issues to hit the 
 floor. His three main priorities are to strengthen Affiliated Project 
 relationships, encourage proper stakeholder outreach, and become more 
 active as a committee. He states he is not running for Chair to command, 
 but to listen to fellow senators as part of the committee and find solutions. 
 The senator says their past leadership experience has made them feel 
 equipped to assume the role of Student Life Chair. Senator Nturubika 
 thanks the committee for their consideration. 
 Senator Nturubika reserves 1:09 seconds for their closing 
 
 The committee enters a period of questioning. 
 Acting Chair Macalintal asks the committee if there are any questions at this 
 time? 
 
 Senator Saavedra Howell questions how the senator would plan to address 
 Market Wednesday tabling? 
 Senator Nturubika responds, stating they would continue with a sign-up 
 sheet system to hold senators accountable for their sign-up times. 
 Senator Owens questions if the Senator has any specific course of action 
planned for the committee to become more involved with the Student Body? 
Senator Nturubika says he would like to create student and senator meeting 
spaces for students to interact with senators in a more comfortable setting. 
 
The committee moves into a period of Pro Debate. 
 
Senator Noel speaks in pro, saying the candidate has a lot of experience in 
leadership and exemplifies excellent qualities of communication. 
Senator Owens speaks in pro, stating the candidate seemed very 
passionate during their opening statement, which would only benefit the 
committee. 
 
Senator Nturubika says regardless of the vote count, he will continue to 
work towards the betterment of the Student Life Committee and thanks the 
committee. 
 
Senator Rico gives her opening statement and says she has been involved 
in the Student Life Committee for her entire term as a Senator. She states 
she wants to continue building the confidence of new senators to continue 
positive interactions during the meeting. She also wants to visit each 
affiliated project under review to expose the committee to the affiliated 
project's structure. She believes it is very important to emphasize why 
Affiliated Project Review is done when it comes time for the Budget 
Committee to meet. 
 Senator Rico yields with 0:00 seconds for her closing. 
 
The committee enters a period of general questioning. 
Senator Noel asks for any breakdown in leadership positions that has led 
Senator Rico to feel prepared to take on this role? 
Senator Rico responds by saying she was Student Body President in high 
school; however, it was helpful to understand how to increase 
engagement. 
Senator Ambroggio asks for more explanation on Affiliated Project Review? 
Senator Rico explains she wants to implement a quiet senator operation for 
senators to inspect SGA-funded Affiliated Projects, where those people can 
then share their perspective. 
 
The committee moves into a period of Pro Debate. 
 
Senator Noel speaks in favor of Senator Rico, stating she has done so 
much in the Senate and loves her planned initiatives. 
Senator Ambroggio speaks in favor of the candidate, saying she supports 
Senator Rico's approach to focus on more engagement. 
 
Acting Chair Macalintal calls the vote for the next Student Life Chair. 
 
Senator Rico has been elected the new Chair of the Student Life 
Committee. 
 
Chair Rico appreciates the committee for selecting her as the New Chair 
and coordinates a permanent meeting time. 
 Closing Announcements 
 Vice Chair Macalintal appreciates the committee for meeting and appreciates 
 the candidates who have chosen to run today. 
 Senator Noel reminds the committee that FSU Ambassador applications are 
 open now. 
 Chair Rico thanks the committee 

 Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 Chair Rico entertains a motion to adjourn. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal accepts the proposed motion. 
 Senator Noel seconds. 
 
 Present: Macalintal, Rico, Noel, Saavedra Howell, Vivian, Urrea-Perez, 
 Dawkins, Finman, Ambroggio, Nturubika, Owens, Amirzadeh, Ramos 
 
 Absent: Maxwell (U), Santos (U), Engelhard (U), Re (U), Soto (U) 
 
 The meeting is adjourned at 1:12 PM. 

[MIN_FOOT]

#78-034 This resolution would encourage this SGA to begin exploring, and

 damaging waste around overfilled trash cans. This resolution would

 change aligns the Rules of Procedure with the new monthly financial 
 reporting requirements established under the companion bill 
 amending Chapter 409, Student Body Statutes. (Assigned to Rules, 
 Finance, 07.15.2026) (Passed Rules, 07.16.2026) (Tabled in 
 Finance, 07.21.2026) 

 Legislation on Second Reading 
Proclamation Sponsored by Carlos Rivas, Iris Rodriguez 
#78-015 This proclamation expresses the Florida State University Student 
 Senate’s solidarity with the people of Venezuela following the 
 devastating earthquakes that struck the country on June 24, 2026. It 
 recognizes the humanitarian impact of the disaster and supports the 
 relief efforts organized by the Venezuelan Student Association and 
 the Hispanic/Latine Student Union through a campus-wide donation 
 drive. The proclamation also encourages Student Senators and the 
 broader FSU community to raise awareness and contribute to 
 humanitarian assistance efforts for those affected. (Assigned to 
 Student Life, 07.15.2026) (Passed Student Life, 07.20.2026) 
Proclamation Sponsored by Sophia Ambroggio 
#78-016 This proclamation recognizes July 2026 as Disability Awareness 
 Month, which honors and contributes to the advocacy of the 
 experiences of the disability community within FSU and beyond, 
 around the globe. The efforts of the FSU Office of Accessibility 
 Services and the FSU Student Senate towards fostering accessibility 
 and disability accommodations are highlighted in the 
 document. (Assigned to Student Life, 07.15.2026) (Passed 
 Student Life, 07.20.2026) 

Bill #78-033 Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis 
 This bill is a follow-up to the previous #78-022. It clarifies 
 expenditures outside of the election period, and sets procedure for 
 how expense submission works for these non-election periods. All 
 expenses will now be submitted in the Final Expense Statement due 
 at the end of each Fall and Spring’s election period; the method of 
 submission is left to the Election Office’s discretion. In addition, a 
 limit is set for expenses outside of the election period to ensure that 
 there is framework for campaigning outside of the election period. 
 (Assigned to Judiciary, Finance, 07.15.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 
 07.20.2026) (Passed Finance, 07.21.2026) 

Bill #78-032 Sponsored by Alexia Holliday 
 This comprehensive 65-page bill updates our Student Body Statutes 
 to remove all reserved chapters from Municode, moving all 67 
 unused sections to a renamed “Archive Book”, simultaneously 
 relocating all “Historical Senate Documents” to their own tabs under 
 “Enrolled Legislation”. It renumbers chapters, titles, and the citations 
 within them accordingly so that our governing document is up to date 
 with itself in all sections. The accompanying resolution explains all 
 chapters and titles being removed and updated, while detailing how 
 future updates to the Archive Book shall take place by working 
 alongside the Office of Student Governance & Advocacy. (Assigned 
 to Judiciary, 07.15.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 07.20.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Alexia Holliday 
#78-035 This comprehensive 65-page bill updates our Student Body Statutes 
 to remove all reserved chapters from Municode, moving all 67 
 unused sections to a renamed “Archive Book”, simultaneously 
 relocating all “Historical Senate Documents” to their own tabs under 
 “Enrolled Legislation”. It renumbers chapters, titles, and the citations 
 within them accordingly so that our governing document is up to date 
 with itself in all sections. The accompanying resolution explains all 
 chapters and titles being removed and updated, while detailing how 
 future updates to the Archive Book shall take place by working 
 alongside the Office of Student Governance & Advocacy. (Assigned 
 to Judiciary, 07.15.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 07.20.2026) 
Bill #78-036 Sponsored by Dylan Gaynor 
 In partnership with the Department of Governmental Affairs in the 
 Executive Branch, and the Civic Engagement Board in the College of 
 Social Sciences and Public Policy, SGA will be hosting a Voter 
 Registration drive for the 2026 Midterm Elections to encourage civic 
 participation and community. This event will take place on October 
 1st, 2026, on Landis Green and will feature food from 4 Rivers 
 Smokehouse and a raffle. (Assigned to Internal Affairs, Finance, 
 Student Life, 07.15.2026) (Passed Internal Affairs, Student Life, 
 07.20.2026) (Passed Finance, 07.21.2026) 

Bill #78-038 Sponsored by Sara Mendez Arango 
 This Transfer Bill would allocate $70,000 from the Campus 
 Advancement and Development fund for the purchase and 
 installation of a brand new HVAC unit for the Flying High Circus. The 
 funds would be set aside, and an accompanying resolution would 
 ensure there is a Grant Agreement between the Student Body 
 President and the Director of the Flying High Circus. (Assigned to 
 Student Life, Finance, 07.15.2026) (Passed Student Life, 
 07.20.2026) (Passed Finance, 07.21.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Sara Mendez Arango 
#78-040 This Resolution would allocate $70,000 from the Campus 
 Advancement and Development fund for the purchase and 
 installation of a brand new HVAC unit for the Flying High Circus. The 
 funds would be set aside, and it would ensure there is a Grant 
 Agreement between the Student Body President and the Director of 
 the Flying High Circus for reimbursement procedures. (Assigned to 
 Student Life, 07.15.2026) (Passed Student Life, 07.20.2026) 

Bill #78-035 Sponsored by Dylan Gaynor, Tanner Bigenho 
 This bill would allow the Student Body President, through the annual 
 policy on the organization of the executive branch, to create a list of 
 Suggested Qualifications for all Executive appointed positions, not 
 including vacant Senate seats. It also designates power to allow 
 unqualified applicants to be disqualified with appropriate Senate 
 checks. (Assigned to Internal Affairs, Judiciary, 07.15.2026) 
 (Passed Internal Affairs, Judiciary, 07.20.2026) 

Bill #78-037 Sponsored by Vanessa Aihe, Tanner Bigenho 
 This bill amends Chapter 303 upon the request of institute leaders. It 
 updates the Freshman Leadership Institute (FLI) section to mandate 
 participatory leadership experience be a crucial factor in Director 
 selection, transition pursuant to Chapter 207, and codifies an 
 attendance requirement for graduation. It also requires Senate 
 confirmation for Assistant Directors, and allows each institute to 
 adopt internal policy pursuant to Chapter 421. (Assigned to Internal 
 Affairs, Judiciary, 07.15.2026) (Passed Internal Affairs, 
 Judiciary, 07.20.2026) 
Resolution Sponsored by Dillon Costello, Riley Perantoni 
#78-036 This resolution respectfully requests that Florida State University 
 review whether balances in the Campus Advancement and 
 Development (CAD) Fund may lawfully be held in university-
 approved, principal-protected, interest-bearing accounts or cash-
 management vehicles. It also respectfully requests written guidance 
 on whether CAD Fund balances currently earn interest through any 
 University cash-management structure and, if legally and 
 administratively permissible, whether interest attributable to CAD 
 Fund balances may be credited back to the CAD Fund. This 
 resolution does not authorize any transfer, expenditure, 
 appropriation, or investment of funds by the Student Senate or by 
 any individual officer. (Assigned to Finance, 07.15.2026) (Passed 
 Finance, 07.21.2026)

sections.text:
FINANCE COMMITTEE 
 July 21, 2026 at 7:30 PM 
 Location: (Location or Zoom Link) 
 MEETING MINUTES 

 Call to Order 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 
 Chair Perantoni acknowledges the land acknowledgment. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
 Vice Chair Tizon administers the roll and verifies the quorum. 
 
 First Roll: 
 Present: Perantoni, Tizon, Costello, Gentile, Hidalgo, Bollinger, Oria, Dewey. 
 Excused: Janet Rodriguez-Garcia, Dana Scarpone, Katie White, Sachate 
 Kaul. 

 Public Comment 
 None 

 Opening Announcements 
 Chair Perantoni welcomes everybody to the final summer Finance Committee 
 Meeting. Vice Chair Tizon wishes everyone a good remainder of summer. 

 Old Business 
 None. 

 New Business 
 
• Bill #78-038 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes Sponsor Mendez Arango. 
 
 Sponsor Mendez Arango discusses Bill #78-038. This bill aims to solve an 
 air conditioning issue in the "hut" for FSU's circus, which has no current 
 installation. The bill solves this by purchasing a HVAC unit for $70,000, 
 drawing money from the CAD. Sponsor Mendez Arango discusses how this 
 will enable the FSU circus to be more accessible to students during 
 showtimes and practices. Sponsor discusses how the current heat in the 
 "hut" is the main reason for this bill, to help the student body as a whole. 
 Sponsor yields with 2:35 seconds for closing. 
 
 Sen. Hidalgo asks why SGA is being asked to fund the HVAC unit rather 
 than the circus itself. 
 Sponsor Mendez Arango discusses how she wanted to fund it as a passion 
 project, and how SGA's mission is to better FSU, backing this bill. The 
 sponsor also discusses long-term benefits for SGA. 
 
 Sen. Bollinger asks if this HVAC replacement would save money in the long 
 term and if the air conditioning would be actually felt. 
 Sponsor says the air conditioning would be felt. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks if there was consulting with the office of the treasurer. 
 Sponsor elaborates on the grant agreement and where the funding comes 
 from. 
 
 Sen. Dewey asks how much the current HVAC rental system costs. 
 Sponsor is unaware of the current cost but states she can obtain that 
 information. 
 
 Sen. Dewey asks how long the unit would last. 
 Sponsor states ideally decades. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon asks if the sponsor consulted the office of the treasurer. 
 Sponsor states she did. 
 
 Sen. Dewey asks how many different quotes the sponsor obtained for the 
 HVAC unit. 
 The sponsor states she had gotten the quote previously from Chad 
 Matthews, and now the best value unit she has found was roughly sixty-six 
 thousand. 
 
 Sen. Bollinger asks if the quote includes shipping, installation, etc., 
 regarding the vendor for the HVAC unit. 
 Sponsor states the original quote factors in extra funding allocated towards 
 installation. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks if this is a one-time payment or if money will be pulled out of 
 CAD long term. 
 The sponsor states this is a one-time payment, all future maintenance will 
 come from the FSU circus. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks if the circus is able to fully fund this if we could not allocate 
 this money. 
 Sponsor states the circus cannot currently fund this without pulling from the 
 CAD fund. 
 
 Sen. Hidalgo asks if the sponsor has any ideas or plans for SGA 
 recognition for the funding of the HVAC unit. 
 Sponsor states she would like the circus to include a speech during one of 
 the circus shows. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon motions to move into roundtable and asks for a follow-up. 
 Sen. Dewey seconds. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon asks if the circus would be able to cover extra shipping 
 and installation costs that may arise. 
 Sponsor states that will be worked on in the future. 
 
 VC Tizon speaks in pro. 
 
 Sen. Gentille speaks in pro. 
 
 Sen. Dewey speaks in pro. 
 
 Sen. Bollinger speaks in pro and asks to elaborate on the HVAC unit. 
 Sponsor replies. 
 
 Sen. Costello speaks in pro and asks to see the cost per person in the 
 future. 
 Sponsor states she has the cost per person. 
 
 Sen. Hidalgo motions to call the question. 
 Sen. Oria seconds. 
 
 The sponsor closes and thanks the committee and states she will get any 
 information requested and elaborates on the impact this bill will have. 
 
 VC Tizon calls the vote. 8Y, 0N, 1A, bill passes. 
• Bill #78-033 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes Sponsor Gurtis. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis discusses that this is follow-up legislation for campaign 
 expenditures & how it clarifies when the campaign period starts, with a 
 $2,000 cap for expenditures during non-election periods. Sponsor yields 
 with 2:36 seconds. 
 
 Chair Perantoni asks a question. 
 Sponsor replies. 
 
 VC Tizon asks about the $2,000 cap for non-campaign periods. 
 Sponsor replies. 
 
 VC Tizon asks another question regarding campaign contributions. 
 Sponsor states they will stay the same with additional contributions for 
 summer semesters. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks a question to the sponsor regarding expenses. 
 Sponsor Gurtis replies that this bill focuses on expenses outside of 
 campaign periods. 
 
 VC Tizon motions to call the question by unanimous consent; the bill 
 passes. 

• Resolution #78-036 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes Sponsor Costello. 
 
 Sponsor Costello discusses the bill that goes over interest review for CAD 
 and SGA. 
 
 Sen. Hidalgo asks if the interest gained is worth going through the legal 
 action required. 
 Sponsor replies. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks if the interest gained will be used for scholarships. 
 Sponsor states that the current goal is for the interest gained to be placed 
 back in the CAD fund, and allocating scholarships would be a future goal. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks for clarification of the bill. 
 Sponsor replies that the interest would not be able to be invested by 
 students, but rather trustees into the lowest risk investments. Sponsor 
 elaborates that this is putting interest already being gained back into the 
 Senate's hands. 
 
 Sen. Bollinger motions to move into roundtable. 
 Sen. Oria seconds. 
 
 Sen. Bollinger speaks in pro. 
 
 Sen. Gentile speaks in pro. 
 
 Sen. Hidalgo speaks in pro. 
 
 VC Tizon speaks in pro and motions to call the question. 
 Sen. Bollinger seconds. 
 
 Sponsor elaborates the resolution during his closing. 
 
 VC Tizon calls the vote, 6Y, 0N, 2A, resolution passes. 

• Bill #78-034 
 
 ■ Tabled until fall. 
 • Resolution #78-038 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni states this was tabled to fall. 
 
 • Bill #78-036 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes sponsor Gaynor. 
 
 Sponsor Gaynor discusses the bill which allocates money towards catering 
 for a voter registration drive held by SGA and the Department of 
 Governmental Affairs in the Executive Branch, and the Civic Engagement 
 Board in the College of Social Sciences and Public Policy. The sponsor 
 elaborates on what else will be funded by the partners of this event. 
 
 VC Tizon asks if there is a cost per person. 
 Sponsor states they estimate 200-300 attending and eating. 
 
 Chair Perantoni asks a question regarding the voting registration. 
 Sponsor replies to the question, stating everybody can come and eat 
 regardless of voting status. 
 
 Sen. Oria asks if there will be guest speakers. 
 Sponsor states they are hoping to have special guests, at minimum, the 
 Leon County supervisor of elections. 
 
 VC Tizon motions to calls the question by unanimous consent. 
 
 Bill passes by unanimous consent. 
 
 Sponsor thanks the committee. 

 Closing Announcements 
 Chair Perantoni thanks the committee for all of their work this summer. 
 
 VC Tizon motions to adjorn. 
 Seconds by Sen. Oria. 

 Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 Final Roll: 
 Present: Perantoni, Tizon, Costello, Gentile, Hidalgo, Bollinger, Oria, Dewey. 
 Excused: Janet Rodriguez-Garcia, Dana Scarpone, Katie White, Sachate 
 Kaul. 

[MIN_FOOT]

sections.text:
STUDENT LIFE COMMITTEE 
 July 20, 2026 at 8:00 PM 
 Location: (Location or Zoom Link) 
 MEETING MINUTES 

 Call to Order 
 Chair Mendez Arango called the meeting to order at 8:05PM. 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 
 Chair Mendez Arango acknowledged the Land Acknowledgment. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
 Vice Chair Macalintal verified the quorum. 
 
 Present: Mendez-Arango, Macalintal, Rico, Owens, Nturubika, Maxwell, Noel, 
 Urrea-Perez, Vivian, Santos-Ramirez, Ambroggio, Dawkins 
 
 Absent: Ramos (U) 

 Public Comment 
 N/A 

 Opening Announcements 
 Chair Mendez Arango welcomed the committee and sponsors of the planned 
 legislation. 

 Old Business 
 N 

 New Business 
 
• Proclamation #78-015 
 
 ■ The sponsor gives an opening statement calling attention to the two 
 powerful earthquakes measuring magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5 experienced in 
 Venezuela. These earthquakes resulted in significant damage to homes, 
 infrastructure, and public 
 services, leaving thousands of families displaced and in urgent need of 
 humanitarian assistance. In response to this tragedy, the Venezuelan 
 Student Association and the Hispanic/Latine Student Union at Florida State 
 University have organized a campus-wide donation drive to support relief 
 efforts. This proclamation was additionally written with the intention of 
 comforting students who have family or know someone involved in this 
 natural disaster. 
 Sponsor yields with 3:21 seconds for their closing. 
 
 The floor enters a period of general questioning. 
 
 Vice Chair Macalintal asks the chair to reserve a follow-up 
 Chair Mendez Arango agrees. 
 
 Vice Chair Macalintal motions to place the committee into a roundtable 
 discussion. 
 Senator Rico seconds. 
 
 For their follow-up, Vice Chair Macalintal spoke in pro of the proclamation, 
 claiming this is exactly how Agency Liaisons should proceed with their 
 position and commended Senator Rivas on their work. 
 Senator Rico speaks in pro stating the sponsor did a phenosal job on their 
 research. 
 Chair Mendez Arango speaks in pro and says the senator has done a great 
 job. 
 
 Senator Rico motions to approve by unanimous consent. 
 
 Senator Rivas appreciated the committee for their support. 
 
 Passes Proclamation #78-015 unanimously. 

• Resolution #78-034 
 
 ■ The sponsor gives an opening statement claiming how fun and exciting 
 Student Life is compared to their Internal Affairs meetings. They elaborate 
 on a trash can project they have been working on since they started SGA. 
 These trash cans self-compact thrown-away materials to limit overflow in 
 high-traffic trash areas to further preserve campus beauty and support 
 sustainable initiatives. 
 The sponsor thanks the people who have helped him on this project, 
 including Aramark, OBS, Facilities, Kyle Clark, and Vice Chair Macalintal, 
 known as the trash can queen. 
 The sponsor yields with 2:37 seconds for their closing. 
 
 The floor enters a period of general questioning. 
 
 Senator Rico asks what the intent is with this resolution. 
 The sponsor responds, saying it is to establish it if passed, a project SGA 
 as a whole wants to pursue. 
 
 Vice Chair Macalintal requests a follow-up. 
 Chair Mendez Arango agrees. 
 
 They ask the sponsor if the SGA symbol will be displayed on the trash can. 
 The sponsor says yes; it will need approval. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal says she no longer needs her follow-up. 
 Senator Nturubika questions Vice Chair Gaynor about how he had identified 
 hot spots on campus. 
 Vice Chair Gaynor explains that food service areas are the priority then it is 
 based on student input. 
 
 Senator Vivian requests a follow-up. 
 Chair Mendez Arango agrees. 
 
 Senator Vivian makes a motion to move the committee into roundtable 
 Senator Nturubika seconds. 
 
 Senator Vivian speaks in pro. 
 Senator Rico speaks in pro, saying self-compacting trashcans are 
 amazing. 
 
 Vice Chair Macalintal requests a follow-up. 
 Chair Mendez Arango agrees. 
 
 Vice Chair Macalintal speaks in pro. 
 
 Vice Chair Macalintal motions to call to question by unanimous consent. 
 
 The sponsor thanks the committee for their time. 
 
 Resolution #78-034 passes with unanimous consent. 
• Proclamation #78-016 
 
 ■ The sponsor gives an opening statement recognizing this month as 
 Disability Awareness Month to promote awareness. The Florida State 
 University Student Government Association remains committed to fostering 
 an inclusive and accessible campus environment where all students, 
 regardless of ability, have the opportunity to learn and succeed. 
 Sponsor yields with 3:35 seconds for their closing. 
 
 Senator Noel requests a follow-up. 
 Chair Mendez Arango agrees. 
 
 Senator Noel motions to move the committee into a roundtable. 
 Senator Santos-Ramirez seconds. 
 
 Senator Noel speaks in favor and applauds the sponsor. 
 VC Macalintal questions what the proposed cover letter and amendment 
 mean on the agenda posting. 
 Senator Ambroggio responds that it is just an updated version of the 
 proclamation after doing outreach with the Office of Accessibility Services 
 (OAS). 
 
 VC Macalintal motions to adopt the amendment as seen in the agenda. 
 Senator Santos Ramirez seconds. 
 The sponsor finds it friendly. 
 
 VC Macalintal motions to call to question. 
 Senator Rico seconds. 
 
 The sponsor says this is their first legislation and recognizes Resolution 
 #78-029 for the good work it has done for this cause. 
 
 Proclamtion #78-016 passes (10Y, 0N, 1A) 
 
• Bill #78-036 
 
 ■ Sponsor gives an opening statement about transferring $2,260.12 to 
 Executive Projects for the SGA x CEB Civic 
 Engagement Fair. The entire cost of the event is $4,520.24, which is being 
 split between Executive and Senate Projects. All students are welcome, 
 and the event will feature tabling from student organizations, agencies, and 
 the Leon County Supervisor of Elections, who will be assisting with the 
 Voter Registration effort. 
 Sponsors yield with 3:30 seconds for their closing. 
 
 The floor enters a period of general questioning. 
 
 Senator Santos-Ramirez motions to enter a period of roundtable 
 discussion. 
 Senator Nturubika seconds. 
 
 VC Macalintal speaks in pro claiming this as one of VC Gaynor's best 
 initiatives he has done, which is surprising considering his previous work. 
 
 VC Macalintal motions to call to question. 
 Senator Santos-Ramirez seconds. 
 
 The sponsor appreciates the committee and states that the Civic 
 Engagement Board will be covering all immediate small costs. 
 
 The Bill #78-036 passes. (11Y, 0N, 0A). 
• Bill #78-038 
 
 ■ Chair Mendez Arango entertains a motion to hear Bill #78-038 and 
 Resolution #78-040 in block. 
 Senator Noel accepts the considered motion. 
 VC Macalintal seconds. 
 
 Chair Mendez Arango relinquishes the Chair to VC Macalintal during the 
 presentation of their bill. 
 VC Macalintal accepts and is now acting Chair. 
 
 The sponsor gives an opening statement stating this legislation would 
 allocate $70,000 from the Campus Advancement and Development fund for 
 the purchase and installation of a brand new HVAC unit for the Flying High 
 Circus. The Director of the FSU Flying High Circus, Chad Mathews, will 
 enter into a Grant Agreement memorandum, which will detail the process of 
 reimbursement for the purchase of the HVAC Unit. This project will provide 
 a cooling environment to the performers, students, and families who attend 
 the Circus performances and support personal safety by limiting the chance 
 of heat exhaustion. 
 The sponsor yields with 2: 44 seconds for their closing. 
 
 The floor enters a period of general questioning. 
 
 Senator Santos Ramirez requests a follow-up. 
 Chair Macalintal agrees. 
 
 Senator Santos Ramirez motions to enter a period of roundtable 
 discussion. 
 Senator Owens seconds. 
 
 Senator Santos-Ramirez speaks in pro. 
 Senator Rico speaks in pro, stating she understands how much Senator 
 Mendez Arango has done for the success of this project. 
 Senator Noel speaks in pro, stating this makes the tent a safer environment 
 for the summer camps that use the tent. 
 Senator Maxwell questions the sponsor about why she has chosen to go 
 with the installation of an HVAC rather than other solutions. 
 Senator Mendez Arango responds, saying the infrastructure of the tent 
 already houses a place for the HVAC to be installed, making it an easier 
 solution. 
 
 Senator Santos-Ramirez motions to call to question. 
 
 The sponsor appreciated the committee, saying this was her main goal for 
 her last remaining time as a senator. 
 
 Bill #78-038 and Resolution #78-040 pass in block. (10Y, 0N, 2A). 

• Resolution #78-040

 34th Congress of Graduate Students Legislation 
 Cover Sheet 
 COGS Bill #22 

 Sponsor(s): Speaker Serrone 

Short Title: A bill allocating LSC Funds for the Fall 2025 Semester. 

Summary of Legislation: 
The bill allocates $51,235.85 from the Law School Council to the Council and to College of 
Law Student Organizations. 
 
Background Information: 
Every year, in the annual budget, the Congress allocates funds to the Law School Council 
(LSC) for LSC to distribute to the student organizations at the College of Law. In fall 2023, the 
Law School Governance Reform Act was passed, which mandated that LSC allocate its 
annual funds in a semesterly budget. 
 As part of its budget process, LSC holds an initial informational session with student 
organizations walking through the budget process for the semester and answering any 
questions from the organizations. Organizations then have a period of time to submit budget 
requests to LSC. These requests are initially reviewed at a meeting of the LSC and Round 
One cuts are made. These cuts are made off of the submissions and are meant to bring down 
the volume of the initial request. Once the Round One cuts are provided to the organizations, 
each organization has a period of time to appeal the cuts and provide additional arguments for 
why that organization should receive more funding than initially proposed. LSC hears these 
arguments and incorporates them into a final allocation. 
 The final allocations are then transmitted to the COGS Speaker, who works with the 
representatives from the College of Law to draft a bill based off of the allocations made by 
LSC. Typically, a representative from the College of Law sponsors the budget bill. 
 The Congress, subject to veto by the university president or their designee, has final authority 
over the allocations made by LSC and may amend or reject the allocations as it sees fit. 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
Passage of the bill allocates $51,235.85 from the Law School Council to the Council and to 
College of Law Student Organizations.

 CONSOLIDATED MINUTES OF FALL 2026 BUDGET DELIBERATIONS AND APPEALS 
 
 Florida State University College of Law 
 
 Special Meetings Held Remotely via Zoom on July 6, July 7, and July 13, 2026 
 
 These consolidated minutes document the Law School Council’s review of Fall 2026 budget 
requests submitted by the College of Law’s registered student organizations, the Council’s initial 
 allocation decisions, and the subsequent appeals process. 

 SECTION I - JULY 6, 2026: INITIAL DELIBERATIONS 
Call to Order: Chair Mallory McCray called the special meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
Attendance: Mallory McCray, Carter Schatt, Christian Christakos, Bailey Hicks; Nathan Grodsky 
joined at 6:24 p.m.; Devyn Wishon joined at 7:05 p.m. Also participating were SBA 
Representative Maddie Riscigno and COGS Representative Madison Shostack. 
Procedure: The Council considered organizations in alphabetical order. For each organization, 
the assigned board member presented a staff analysis, representatives were allowed to provide 
public comment, members debated proposed changes, and the Council voted on the 
recommended allocation and any amendments.

Staff presentation: Carter Schatt | Second: Bailey Hicks 
The Council discussed vendor availability for culturally appropriate food. APALSA’s 
representative, Meghana Raj, requested assistance locating an approved vendor.

 Christian: Yes; Bailey: Yes. Motion passed 5-0.

 Christian: Yes; Bailey: Yes; Nathan: Yes. Motion passed 6-0. 
 Approved allocation at this meeting: $1,259.41
