 CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS 
 
 SECTION III - JULY 13, 2026: APPEAL DELIBERATIONS 
Call to Order: Chair Mallory McCray called the special meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
Attendance: Mallory McCray, Carter Schatt, Christian Christakos, Devyn Wishon, and Nathan 
Grodsky. Also participating were SBA Representative Maddie Riscigno and COGS 
Representative Madison Shostack. 
Meeting purpose and procedure: The Council convened to consider timely appeals from the 
initial Fall 2026 allocations. Approximately $2,400 had been set aside for possible appeal 
adjustments. Appeals were reviewed with public comment, staff analysis, and line-item debate. 
The Council considered clerical corrections, additional documentation, and substantive requests 
for reconsideration. 
Record note: Our available written materials do not preserve individual roll-call votes for every 
appeal motion. Accordingly, this section reports the verified motion outcomes and final 
allocation adjustments without attributing individual votes where the record is incomplete. 
 
Association for Criminal Justice (ACJ) 
Appeal based on clerical error that was a miscalculation on RSO spreadsheet. 
 Outcome: No appeal adjustment is reflected in the final allocation inventory. ACJ’s allocation 
 remained $1,259.41. 
 
Black Law Students Association (BLSA) 
Carisse Joseph addressed three appealed items: additional food for the induction ceremony, 
crewneck pricing, and the Ben Crump event. Joseph explained that the induction ceremony was 
an evening program requiring an additional platter and that the crewneck price depended on 
order quantity. The Zoom chat reflects a quoted price of $26.40 per crewneck and discussion of 
the COGS merchandise limit. 
 Staff analysis and debate: Christian initially recommended a $414 adjustment and later 
 proposed an amended amount of $450. That proposal was withdrawn after further 
 discussion. Members considered lower-cost crewneck options, the number of items to be 
 funded, consistency with merchandise decisions for other organizations, and the need for an 
 additional induction-ceremony platter. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a net appeal increase of $300.00. The final 
 allocation increased from $1,914.73 to $2,214.73. The approved adjustment supported the 
 induction-ceremony need and a limited crewneck purchase. 
 
Consumer Advocates Society (CAS) 
CAS appealed a small food item connected to a bankruptcy-court tour. 
 Staff analysis and debate: The Council considered whether granola bars were a 
 reasonable and directly related support item for participating students during the tour. 

 Florida State University, New Student Union Room 3251, Tallahassee, FL, 32304 
 Telephone 850-644-1811 | Fax 850-644-0814 | http://sga.fsu.edu/ 

 FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY 
 CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS 
 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved an additional $15.00, increasing CAS’s 
 allocation from $482.58 to $497.58. 
 
Entertainment, Arts, and Sports Law Society (EASL) 
Elijah Cochran and Alannah Rowe clarified the organization’s appealed requests, including T-
shirt pricing for a pickleball event, the distinction between two entertainment-law panels, and 
revised event costs. The appeal included $103.00 in additional requests, including $87.00 for 
pizza at a painting social and $16.00 for networking-event refreshments. 
 Staff analysis and debate: The Council reviewed whether the painting social had sufficient 
 substance, whether refreshments at the networking event were necessary, and whether the 
 revised merchandise and panel documentation resolved the concerns identified during initial 
 deliberations. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council restored $87.00 for the painting social and declined the 
 additional $16.00 refreshment request. EASL’s final allocation increased from $2,111.03 to 
 $2,198.03. 
 
Environmental Law Society (ELS) 
Sarah Chair provided additional information regarding ELS’s nature walks, scheduling 
decisions, and the use of hydration supplies for outdoor programming. 
 Staff analysis and debate: The Council reconsidered the previously removed Gatorade 
 expense in light of the outdoor nature-walk format and the practical need to provide 
 hydration. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council restored $24.00 for Gatorade or comparable hydration 
 supplies. ELS’s allocation increased from $1,299.00 to $1,323.00. 
 
Federal Bar Association at FSU (FBA) 
Jennifer Pennypacker presented a revised and prioritized appeal. FBA removed most 
merchandise requests other than Constitution Day T-shirts and sought additional funding for 
substantive events, including a quiz bowl, a naturalization-ceremony reception, and a federal 
criminal-defense panel. 
 Staff analysis and debate: The Council examined updated and more cost-conscious 
 estimates, the proposed $140.24 quiz-bowl request, food costs for the naturalization 
 ceremony and criminal-defense panel, and uncertainty regarding expected attendance. 
 Members expressed concern about approximately $400 in pizza costs and a prior $500 shirt 
 request while recognizing the substantive nature of the programs. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a net appeal increase of $180.24. FBA’s 
 allocation increased from $1,349.16 to $1,529.40. 
 
Jewish Law Students Association (JLSA) 

 Florida State University, New Student Union Room 3251, Tallahassee, FL, 32304 
 Telephone 850-644-1811 | Fax 850-644-0814 | http://sga.fsu.edu/ 

 FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY 
 CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS 
 
Sophia Stines requested an opportunity to clarify JLSA’s appeal after joining the meeting. The 
appeal addressed food pricing and the additional expense associated with kosher options. 
 Staff analysis and debate: Nathan presented a recommendation that accounted for kosher 
 food costing up to $15.00 per person while reducing projected attendance from 25 to 20 
 students. Members discussed consistency with the approximately $12.50 per-person 
 approach used in initial deliberations and the need to recognize legitimate dietary-cost 
 differences. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a $100.00 appeal adjustment. JLSA’s 
 allocation increased from $1,065.00 to $1,165.00. 
 
Middle Eastern Law Association (MELA) 
Jenny Said supplied additional explanations concerning attendance, bowling costs, baklava, 
and culturally significant food selections. The appeal also addressed a joint event and requested 
sweatshirts. 
 Staff analysis and debate: The Council reviewed documentation for the collaborative 
 program and bowling activity, considered the cultural purpose of specific food items, and 
 evaluated merchandise consistency. Members declined to add sweatshirt funding because 
 the organization already had support for T-shirts. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a net appeal increase of $217.00 for selected 
 program items. MELA’s allocation increased from $1,381.26 to $1,598.26. 
 
National Lawyers Guild (NLG) 
Avery Bell provided additional information concerning NLG’s book club and related 
programming. The Council revisited the cost of literature materials and the division of support 
among collaborating organizations. 
 Staff analysis and debate: Mallory proposed a possible future model in which students 
 would contribute a nominal amount toward a book and receive the book through the 
 program. The Council determined that a new participation-fee model should not be 
 imposed during the current cycle and could instead be considered for a later semester. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a $150.00 appeal increase. NLG’s 
 allocation increased from $1,141.91 to $1,291.91. 
 
OUTLaw 
OUTLaw sought reconsideration of funding associated with a social event and provided 
additional context that had not been available during the initial review. 
 Staff analysis and debate: Carter’s initial appeal analysis recommended no restoration 
 because of insufficient documentation. After further debate, the Council considered the 
 event’s purpose, revised justification, and consistency with social-event funding provided to 
 other organizations.

 Telephone 850-644-1811 | Fax 850-644-0814 | http://sga.fsu.edu/ 

 FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY 
 CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS 
 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a $200.00 appeal adjustment. OUTLaw’s 
 allocation increased from $904.53 to $1,104.53. 
 
Public Interest Law Students Association (PILSA) 
PILSA appealed funding for a First Amendment event and explained the intended collaboration 
with the First Amendment Clinic. Lainey Fox also clarified that PILC and Career Services did not 
have food budgets available to absorb the event expense. 
 Staff analysis and debate: Nathan initially recommended no restoration because the appeal 
 did not sufficiently justify the request. The Council later reconsidered the substantive value of 
 the First Amendment program and the practical limits on support available from other law-
 school offices. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a $50.00 appeal adjustment for the First 
 Amendment event. PILSA’s allocation increased from $1,299.51 to $1,349.51. 
 
Trial Team 
Trial Team sought reconsideration of several event costs, including a mandatory jury-selection 
workshop, an IM social event, and an October social. The initial discussion was paused so 
members could review the request in greater detail before continuing. 
 Staff analysis and debate: Devyn clarified that the jury-selection workshop was mandatory 
 for Trial Team members and moved to restore $43.00. The Council also considered 
 additional appealed programming costs and debated increasing the October social allocation 
 from $600.00 to $800.00 but retained the existing $600.00 allocation. 
 Motion and outcome: The Council approved a net appeal increase of $93.00, including 
 $43.00 for the jury-selection workshop. Trial Team’s allocation increased from $2,610.52 to 
 $2,703.52. 
Adjournment: Carter Schatt moved to adjourn; Devyn Wishon seconded. The meeting 
adjourned at 9:24 p.m.

Short Title: A Resolution Amending Rule 8.3 of the Senate Rules of Procedure to Rename the 
“Report of the SGA Accounting Office” as the “Report of Remaining Fund Balances.” 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This resolution amends Rule 8.3 of the Senate Rules of Procedure by renaming the recurring meeting 
agenda item “Report of the SGA Accounting Office” to “Report of Remaining Fund Balances.” This 
change aligns the Rules of Procedure with the new monthly financial reporting requirements 
established under the companion bill amending Chapter 409, Student Body Statutes. 
 
Background Information: 
This resolution is a companion to a bill codifying monthly financial reporting requirements in Chapter 
409 (“Senate In The Sunshine”) of the Student Body Statutes. Because Rule 8.3 currently refers to this 
recurring Consent Calendar item as the “Report of the SGA Accounting Office,” a title that does not 
reflect the substance of the report or the new statutory language, this resolution updates the Rules of 
Procedure to use consistent terminology. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Andy Johnson, Program Director for Student Governance & Advocacy. His office was consulted on the 
feasibility of monthly reporting and recommended this rule change alongside the companion Chapter 
409 bill. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If adopted, Rule 8.3 of the Senate Rules of Procedure will refer to this recurring agenda item as the 
“Report of Remaining Fund Balances,” consistent with the terminology used in the companion bill 
amending Chapter 409.

Short Title: Amending Rule One, Senate Rules of Procedure, Updating Organizational Session 
Presiding Officer 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This resolution amends Rule One of the Senate Rules of Procedure to match current organizational 
session statutes. It clarifies the chain of presiding officers for the session in the event an Outgoing 
Senate leader seeks reelection. 
 
Background Information: 
Following amendments to Chapter 400, language in the Senate Rules of Procedure lacks consideration 
for a scenario in which an outgoing Senate leader seeks reelection. Current language, adopted when 
the organizational session was codified last fall, only refers to outgoing Senate President and Pro 
Tempore as leaders for the session, operating under the assumption neither runs for reelection. 
Already existing in Senate Rules of Procedure is a chain of command for committee leadership, or in 
the event none are available, the most senior senator, to takeover Senate President and Pro Tempore 
responsibilities should either be incapable to perform their duties. This resolution utilizes that list and 
language for the organizational session. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Existing Senate leadership, and committee leadership was contacted in efforts to craft this legislation. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This resolution would fix a procedural error in organizational session facilitation. It would allow 
organizational sessions in which outgoing leadership seeks to run for reelection to operate with a clear 
plan and chain of presiding officers. It also makes the Senate Rules of Procedure clearer and more 
flexible should outgoing leadership be unable to preside over the session, making Senate 
administration more effective.

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can.

Short Title: Amending various sections of the Student Body Constitution for the Removal of 
Obsolete and Revised Language. 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
The constitutional amendment would update Articles II, III, and V to eliminate references to institutions 
and practices that no longer exist in Student Government operations. The amendment deletes 
references to executive Beuraus, which no longer exist, and elected positions in Agency and Affiliated 
Project leadership, which now use what is considered an appointment process. The constitutional 
amendment also clarifies language within the Constitution relating to the naming of the Student Body 
Treasurer, consistently referring to the office as “Treasurer” to mirror references made to “President” 
and “Vice President.” 
 
Background Information: 
Every three years, pursuant to the Student Body Constitution Article VI Section 6, the Constitutional 
Review Commission is formed to update the Student Body Constitution. The body proposes 
amendments to put the document in line with current SGA practices, and to streamline overall SGA 
structure and operation. However, with fast and important structural changes in SGA happening in the 
in between years, constitutional updates sometimes are necessary sooner. Sometimes also several 
commissions can miss small but important provisions in our constitution in need of change. 
 
Since 2013 Student Body Statutes have not dictated the election of Agency leaders, instead stipulating 
appointment pursuant to Section 304 and Agency Rules of Procedure. However, even after the Uniform 
Agency Act of 2023 confirmed no Agency leader is to be popularly elected by the Student Body, 
references to popular election in the Student Body Constitution remain. Similarly, while records are 
harder to trace, Affiliated Projects were overhauled in 2013 to presumably eliminate the election of their 
leadership, yet constitutional reality has yet to change. Finally, after the passage of the CORE, or 
Executive Departments Act, of 2025, Executive branch Bureaus were retired for executive departments. 
The Student Body Constitution, SGA’s most important governing document, lacking practical daily 
operations such as mechanism of Director institution and the existence of part of the executive branch, 
must be updated in light of these changes. 

 Page 7 of 25
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Senate and Executive Branch leaders were consulted in the drafting of this constitutional amendment. 
Sponsors give a special thanks to the Student Body Treasurer, Deputy Student Body Treasurer, and 
the Student Senate President for extra attention given in drafting. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
The constitutional amendment would change no operation, enforcement, or structure within SGA. 
Agency and Affiliated Project Leadership would continue to be selected as Student Body Statutes and 
their respective rules of procedure provide. Obsolete constitutional language referring to election would 
be brought up to date with statutes. Removal of reference to nonexistent Bureaus would allow further 
constitutional accuracy, and consistent reference to “Treasurer” would enable consistency in the 
document. Overall, the adoption of the amendment would provide SGA’s bedrock document with more 
authority and utility as it properly depicts current operations.

Short Title: A transfer of $3,050 to Think Twice Inc. 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill will facilitate a transfer of $3,050 to Think Twice Inc. for the purchase of Drink Test 
Strips to determine if a drink has been tampered with. These strips will be distributed to the 
Student Body after the efficacy is confirmed by members of SGA. 
 
Background Information: 
The idea for this legislation was derived from the previous legislation that purchased ‘Night Caps’ for 
drinks to be distributed to students; it was found at other universities that when these testing strips were 
provided to students, they felt safer and they felt protected. 
 
Several different manufacturers were contacted regarding how their strips worked, what they tested for, 
whether students found them to be successful, and prices were also taken into consideration when 
looking for the right manufacturer to use. Think Twice Inc. was the manufacturer that was eventually 
determined because of their success with other universities such as the University of Florida, and they 
offered a deal to give a discounted price and also post the SGA logo on the packaging for each kit so 
that when the strips are distributed to students they know who purchased them, and that SGA is 
representing them and their needs to the best of their ability. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
This legislation was derived from a group that formed specifically to facilitate a project that could make 
students feel safer. This went through several talks with Senate leadership, as well as varying entities 
on campus, such as the FSU PD, CHAW, FSL, and Administration. Before even looking into 
manufacturers, there was discussion on what the best methods for a project of this focus to look like, 
and the best ways to move forward; FSUPD was a great resource that gave insight and advice into 
different reports on campus, steps to move forward, and ideas that were and weren’t going to work. 
 
In addition, several manufacturers were contacted so that the best fit for SGA’s needs could be found. 
Price was one of the considerations, but also how many different substances the strips tested for, since 
there wasn’t solid evidence that one substance was used more than others in reports on campus. Once 
Think Twice was decided on, Senate leadership was consulted further to ensure that this was a project 
that would work to benefit students. 

 Page 12 of 25
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If this legislation were to pass, the funds would be transferred from Senate Projects to Think Twice Inc. 
for the purchase of the testing strips. These strips would first be distributed to members of SGA to test 
the efficacy is varying locations, before further consultation with stakeholders to then distribute the 
strips to members of the Student Body. This will primarily be done through CHAW and FSL, with FSL 
focusing on Panhellenic chapters to start.

 Legislation Cover Sheet 

 Senate Bill #: 031 

 Primary Sponsor(s): Rodriguez 
 Co-sponsor(s): Holliday 

Short Title: Amending Chapter 202, Student Body Statutes, to Hold Candidates Up for 
Confirmation Accountable 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill amends Chapter 202 of Student Body Statutes to include procedures on how to handle 
candidates that are up for confirmation by the Student Senate that are unresponsive and absent from 
their confirmation hearings in their applicable Committee meeting or on the Student Senate floor. This 
bill further codifies that it is the responsibility of the applicable Committee Chair(s) to inform the 
Candidate of the date and times for their committee hearing, and to work with the candidate on finding 
an applicable schedule. 
 
Background Information: 
In the Spring semester of 2026, there were multiple cases of candidates forwarded from the Executive 
Branch and up for confirmation that never appeared before their applicable Committee Meeting nor the 
Senate floor for their confirmation hearings. Because of this, the candidates continued to be tabled 
week after week with no notice or follow up from the candidates. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Outgoing Student Senate Parliamentarian, Student Senate President 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This bill will formally outline a procedure for the Student Senate on how to handle cases of candidates 
up for confirmation who do not communicate with Student Senate leadership about their confirmation 
hearing attendance, as well as establishing the applicable Committee Chair(s) as the main point of 
contact for the candidate as well as the one responsible for notifying the Student Senate if and when 
the candidate fails to appear before their applicable Committee.

 July 9, 2026 at 7:00 PM

 Call to Order 
 Chair Mendez Arango called the meeting to order at 7:34 PM. 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is

Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the

extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of

connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to

in all the ways that we can. 
 Chair Mendez Arango acknowledged the Land Acknowledgment.

 Old Business 

 New Business 

 • Constitutional Amendment #78-003 
 
 ■ The sponsor gave an opening statement about the Constitutional 
 Amendment. He clarified that this CA was very straightforward and cleaned 
 up old or repetitive language to match previously passed legislation. It was 
 stated that the constitutional amendment would change no operation, 
 enforcement, or structure within SGA. 
 Sponsor yields with 3:17 seconds for their closing. 
 
 The floor enters a period of general questioning. 
 
 Senator Rico makes a motion to move into a roundtable discussion. 
 Senator Noel seconds. 
 
 Senator Rico speaks in favor of the bill. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal spoke in favor and congratulated the sponsor, as this 
 is a rare form of legislation. 
 
 Senator Noel motions to call to question. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal seconds. 
 
 The sponsor gives a closing statement, appreciating the committee for their 
 support, and urges members to reach out to him if there are any 
 confusions. 
 
 - Passed CA #78-003 (6Y, 0N, 1A) 
 
• Resolution #78-031 
 
 ■ The sponsor gives an opening statement about how this resolution was 
 written with the intent for senators to have their own SGA email that will be 
 shared among anyone who fills that particular seat. This is in the hope that 
 it will help senators organize SGA business and personal emails received 
 by the university, while also establishing credibility for senators. 
 Sponsor yields with 3:52 seconds for their closing. 
 
 The floor enters a period of general questioning. 
 
 Chair Mendez Arango asks if Ben Young has been consulted on this 
 legislation. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal replies with no, but they have been in talks with Ethan 
 Bischof, the Senate Tech Officer. 
 Senator Rico questions if these new emails will be visible to the members of 
 the College for outreach purposes. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal says that is something that can be done. 
 Senator Noel asks whether the main intent of this legislation was to 
 establish credibility or to streamline communication between members of 
 that college and its elected senators. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal says the main intent was to establish credibility. 
 Senator Rico asks if delegation leadership will get their own email. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal says that can also be done. 
 Senator Rico asks if only delegation leadership can be available to the 
 public to limit confusion. 
 Vice Chair Macalintal says that is a good idea and supports it. 
 
 Senator Noel motions to move into roundtable. 
 Senator Vivian seconds. 
 
 Chair Mendez Arango asks that the sponsor contact Ben Young before this 
 legislation is on second reading to learn if this is achievable. 
 Senator Rico says she agrees with this resolution's intent; however second 
 guesses the logistics of this project. 
 
 Senator Noel motions to call to question. 
 Senator Rico seconds. 
 
 The sponsor thanks the committee for their questions and says she and 
 Chair Perantoni will work on those suggestions before second reading. 
 
 The resolution passes with (5Y, 0N, 2A) 
• Bill #78-028 
 
 ■ Senator Rico motions to hear Resolution #78-033 and Bill #78-028 in 
 block. 
 Senator Noel seconds. 
 
 The legislation Bill #78-028 and Resolution #78-033 passes (7Y, 0N, 2A) 
• Resolution #78-033 
 
 ■ Senator Rico motions to hear Resolution #78-033 and Bill #78-028 in 
 block. 
 Senator Noel seconds. 
 
 The sponsor gives an opening statement about how the drink test kit strips 
 are being provided by ThinkTwice Inc, a known supplier to many schools in 
 California, the University of Florida, and the military. The sponsor wishes to 
 purchase 1200 drink test kit strip packages and pull $3,050.00 from the 
 Senate Projects fund. These packages will contain 2 strips for people to use

Short Title: 
Amending Chapters 301.4, 816.10, and 1116.12, Student Body Statutes, and resolving 
RSOAC Section 4 of rules and procedures, replacing all instances of “NoleCentral” with “the 
University-designated student organization management platform”. 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapters 301.4, 816.10, and 1116.12, Student Body Statutes, following the 
university-wide platform change from NoleCentral to FSU HQ on June 30th, 2026. The bill replaces two 
mentions of “NoleCentral” with “the University-designated student organization management platform”, 
eliminating the need for future statute updates regarding platform changes. This resolution would 
resolve Section 4, Criteria for Evaluation of Funding Requests, Table #1: RSO Allocation Committee 
Full Evaluation Rubric, Column 4, Row 1A, with the same changes, updating one instance of 
“NoleCentral”. If the platform were to change from “FSU HQ” in the future, no additional statute 
changes would be required due to this bill & resolution. 
 
Background Information: tgh 
Beginning June 30, 2026, FSU HQ will replace NoleCentral. FSU HQ will become the new home 
platform for student involvement opportunities, student events, registered student organizations and 
pathways and badging for students enrolled at Tallahassee and Panama City campuses. With the new 
platform, all instances of “NoleCentral” in student body statutes must be updated to reflect current 
changes.

Program Director, Academic & Student Services. Raeshawn Coonce, Student Program Coordinator, 
Department of Student Engagement.

This bill keeps the Student Body Statutes up to date regardless of platform change, highlighting the 
example of the current change of “NoleCentral” to “FSU HQ” and taking into account any future 
platform changes.

Short Title: Amending Chapter 202, Student Body Statutes, to Hold Candidates Up for 
Confirmation Accountable 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill amends Chapter 202 of Student Body Statutes to include procedures on how to handle 
candidates that are up for confirmation by the Student Senate that are unresponsive and absent from 
their confirmation hearings in their applicable Committee meeting or on the Student Senate floor. This 
bill further codifies that it is the responsibility of the applicable Committee Chair(s) to inform the 
Candidate of the date and times for their committee hearing, and to work with the candidate on finding 
an applicable schedule. 
 
Background Information: 
In the Spring semester of 2026, there were multiple cases of candidates forwarded from the Executive 
Branch and up for confirmation that never appeared before their applicable Committee Meeting nor the 
Senate floor for their confirmation hearings. Because of this, the candidates continued to be tabled 
week after week with no notice or follow up from the candidates.

Outgoing Student Senate Parliamentarian, Student Senate President

up for confirmation who do not communicate with Student Senate leadership about their confirmation 
hearing attendance, as well as establishing the applicable Committee Chair(s) as the main point of 
contact for the candidate as well as the one responsible for notifying the Student Senate if and when 
the candidate fails to appear before their applicable Committee.

Opening Announcements 
 Chair Gurtis: 

 The Chair opened the meeting by stating that the agenda was relatively 
 straightforward despite appearing lengthy. The Chair reminded members to 
 reference the previously provided slides in Flare for additional explanations 
 and breakdowns of the legislation items if clarification was needed. 

 The Chair also informed members that Memo 4 had been posted, which 
 would require a special Senate meeting on July 22 during the committee’s 
 normal meeting time. Due to the scheduling conflict, the Chair announced that 
 a new Judiciary Committee meeting time would need to be established and 
 stated that a “when to meet” scheduling poll would be sent out following the 
 meeting. 

Old Business 

New Business 

• Constitutional Amendment #78-003 
 
 ■ Opening Statement: 

 The sponsor explained that the constitutional amendment primarily removes 
 obsolete language and makes technical clarifications rather than creating 
 substantive policy changes. The bill updates the Constitution to reflect that 
 agency directors and affiliated project officers are appointed by the Student 
 Body President, rather than elected, and removes references to bureaus, 
 which no longer exist. It also corrects grammatical errors and standardizes 
 references to the Student Body Treasurer for consistency with other 
 executive officers. 

 Additionally, the amendment clarifies that the organizational session must 
 occur between election certification and inauguration rather than by a fixed 
 deadline of eight days before inauguration, providing greater scheduling 
 flexibility. Finally, it removes language prohibiting Senate meetings during 
 the final week of classes, clarifying that meetings may continue through the 
 last week of classes but not during finals week, consistent with the intent of 
 the Constitutional Review Convention. The sponsor stated these changes 
 are technical and housekeeping in nature and yielded for questions. 
 
 General Questioning: 
 Senator Rodriguez: Asked whether there were any remaining concerns 
 about attendance, quorum, or balancing academic responsibilities if a 
 Senate meeting were to occur during finals week, referencing the 
 discussion about adjusting the timing of the final Senate meeting. 
 -The sponsor clarified that the amendment does not permit Senate 
 meetings during finals week. Instead, it allows meetings through the final 
 week of classes while continuing to prohibit meetings during finals. The 
 sponsor explained that the current constitutional language previously 
 prevented an additional regular Senate meeting, requiring a special session 
 for committee elections. The amendment is intended to provide greater 
 scheduling flexibility and correct that issue. The sponsor added that they 
 are not concerned about meeting quorum, noting that Senate typically 
 maintains strong attendance and that the final meeting generally has a 
 lighter agenda. The sponsor confirmed these changes are intended to 
 address prior drafting errors and provide clarity. 
 
 Round Table: 
 Senator Cineas: pro 
 Senator Rodriguez: pro 
 
 Closing: 
 Thank you! 
 
 Vote: 
 YAY: 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Ian Rodriguez 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 
 The Amendment passes unanimously. 

• Bill #78-026 
 
 ■ Opening Statement: 
 The Sponsor introduced legislation developed by the RSOC Working Group 
 (or Task Force) that represents the first phase of a broader effort to improve 
 the RSOC Allocation Committee. They explained that while additional 
 reforms are planned for the beginning of or during the fall semester, this bill 
 focuses primarily on housekeeping changes and clarifying existing 
 procedures. The legislation corrects typographical errors, updates the 
 committee's attendance policy by reducing the removal threshold for 
 appointed members from four unexcused absences to three, and requires 
 those members to be reappointed if removed. It also clarifies the distinction 
 between appointed and designated members of the committee, specifying 
 that if a designated representative is removed because of excessive 
 absences, the individual or organization responsible for that designation is 
 not obligated to appoint a replacement. The presenter concluded by noting 
 their role as Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee and invited 
 questions from the Senate regarding the legislation. 
 General Questioning: 
 Senator Fordham: The senator raised a technical concern about the bill's 
 requirement that organizations submit a seven-minute video as part of the 
 application process. They questioned whether the Qualtrics submission 
 form or other application portal currently supports video uploads of that 
 length, noting that similar platforms have strict file size limits that could 
 prevent applicants from successfully submitting their videos. They asked 
 whether this potential issue had been reviewed to ensure the requirement 
 would not create unintended technical barriers for applicants. 
 - we can fix this to accomodate. 
 Senator Iarossi: The committee member asked for clarification on the 
 rationale behind lowering the suspension threshold from four absences to 
 three absences and requested further explanation regarding the reasoning 
 behind the change. 
 - The sponsor explained that the rationale for lowering the suspension 
 threshold from four absences to three was based on attendance concerns 
 experienced during the previous semester. The sponsor noted that RSOAC 
 had experienced several meetings where maintaining quorum was a 
 challenge.The sponsor stated that lowering the threshold would create 
 consistency by holding appointed members to the same attendance 
 standard as designated members. Additionally, the sponsor explained that 
 the change would allow RSOAC to better address repeated absences, 
 ensure members are able to consistently participate, and reduce future 
 quorum concerns. 
 
 Closing: 

 The sponsor thanked committee members for their engagement and 
 questions regarding the legislation. The sponsor expressed excitement 
 about submitting one of their first pieces of legislation and shared their 
 appreciation for and its current impact. The sponsor stated that they value 
 the program and enjoyed discussing its importance with the committee 
 before yielding their time. 

 Vote: 
 YAY: 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 
 Unanimous approval 
 
• Bill #78-027 
 
 ■ Opening Statement: 
 The presenter explained that the legislation is a simple statutory cleanup bill 
 intended to keep SGA statutes accurate and consistent. They noted that 
 current statutes still reference the position of “Senate Program Assistant,” 
 which no longer exists within SGNA and has been outdated for several 
 years. The bill updates these references by replacing them with the 
 appropriate current positions, such as referring to SGA generally or 
 specifically to the SGNA Program Director depending on the context. 
 Additionally, the legislation corrects formatting inconsistencies within 
 statutes, particularly where sections containing lists or additional 
 information following a colon were not properly organized as subdivisions. 
 These changes are intended to improve readability, maintain consistency, 
 and ensure that the statutes accurately reflect current SGA structure and 
 procedures. 
 
 Round Table: 
 Senator Kaighin: pro 
 Senator Rodriguez: pro 

 Closing: 
 Thank you all! 
 
 Vote : 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 Ian Rodriguez 
 
 Bill passed by unanimous approval. 

• Bill #78-029 
 
 ■ Opening Statement: 

 The sponsor presented their first piece of legislation, explaining that it 
 updates references to “Nole Central” throughout three chapters of the 
 Student Body Statutes. The legislation replaces those references with 
 “university-designated student organization management platform” to reflect 
 the transition from Nole Central to FSU HQ. The sponsor explained that this 
 broader language was recommended by Andy Johnson and other 
 stakeholders, including Co-Sponsor Holiday, to prevent the need for future 
 amendments if the platform changes again. The sponsor stated that the 
 legislation is a straightforward technical update and yielded their time. 

 Round Table: 
 Senator Rodriguez: Love the municode beautification. Love this. 
 
 Senator Cineas: Pro 
 
 Closing: 
 Thank you all for such an easy process. Judiciary is the best committee. 
 
 Vote: 
 YAY: 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 Ian Rodriguez 
 
 Bill passes. 
• Bill #78-030 
 
 ■ Opening Statement: 
 The presenter introduced legislation amending the Office of the Supervisor 
 of Elections by establishing clearer guidelines for the term limits and terms 
 of office for the Deputy Supervisors of Elections. Previously, Deputy 
 Supervisors did not have a defined term and could remain in their positions 
 until they were removed, resigned, or graduated. This legislation aligns the 
 Deputy Supervisor’s term with the Supervisor of Elections who appointed 
 them, ensuring that both positions operate on the same timeline. The bill 
 also establishes a formal process for the Supervisor of Elections to dismiss 
 their deputies and codifies the right of dismissed deputies to appeal their 
 removal through the same process available to other appointed positions. 
 The presenter noted that after submitting the legislation, they received 
 feedback from the current Deputy Supervisor of Elections, who raised a 
 potential concern regarding the lack of a current Supervisor of Elections 
 and how that situation may impact the implementation of the bill. 
 
 General Questioning: 
 Vice chair Iarossi: Does this give the deputy any new powers or just clarify 
 them? 
 - Clarifies 
 Senator Fordham: Does the student body president hire this position or the 
 supervisor of elections? 
 - The SoE 
 
 Roundtable: 
 Senator Cineas: pro 
 
 Closing: 
 Thank you all again! 
 
 Vote: 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 
 Passed my unanimous approval. 

• Bill #78-031 
 
 ■ Opening Statements: 
 This bill is about decency essientially. After the Student Senate president 
 confirms the committee for the candidate, it is up to the candidate for 
 responsibility for communication about confirmation hearings would no 
 longer fall solely on the committee chair. Candidates would also be required 
 to communicate any scheduling conflicts, availability issues, or 
 circumstances preventing them from attending their confirmation hearing. If 
 a candidate fails to communicate or does not appear for their scheduled 
 hearing, the Senate President or committee chair must notify them that they 
 have one remaining absence before their candidacy is considered null and 
 void. If the candidacy is ultimately deemed null and void, the position would 
 be returned to the appointing authority, most commonly the Student Body 
 President, who would then be responsible for selecting a new candidate. 
 The legislation is intended to create accountability and ensure a more 
 efficient confirmation process. 
 
 Round Table Disscussion: 
 Vice Chair Iarossi: I would like to speak in pro. This is the parenting bill 
 essentially. 
 Senator Cineas: Pro 
 Senator Fordham: I would love to speak in pro I want to add timeline for 
 when they fail to communicate and how long. I want to make an 
 amendment. Ex: Failing to reply for a specific timeframe on line 12. 
 
 Amendment passed. 
 
 Senator Rodriguez: Amendment to make more inclusive language 
 scratching out SBP as full 
 
 Closing: 

 The sponsor commended the Judiciary Committee for successfully handling 
 multiple amendments during the current term, noting that this process was 
 a significant accomplishment for the committee. The sponsor also 
 recognized Senate President Holliday and former Parliamentarian Simon 
 for their assistance in developing the legislation during the previous 
 semester. The sponsor stated that the legislation had been worked on 
 previously but was not submitted before the end of the semester, and was 
 later revisited and brought forward during the summer. 

 Vote: 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 Ian Rodriguez 
 
 Bill passes by unanimous approval. 

Closing Announcements 
 Chair Gurtis: Love you guys and so proud of the questions you all have been 
 asking. The Chair also provided closing remarks and praised the committee 
 for their work, highlighting the successful consideration of three amendments 
 and the high level of engagement throughout the meeting. The Chair 
 commended members for asking thoughtful, well-informed questions and 
 encouraged them to continue their strong participation. 

 The Chair reminded members, including those who joined late, that a “when to 
 meet” scheduling poll would need to be completed and stated that the 
 information would be sent out accordingly. 

 Vice Chair Iarossi: expressed appreciation for the committee and thanked 
 members for creating a welcoming and collaborative environment. The 
 member shared their enjoyment of working with the committee and 
 recognized Chair Gerdas for helping foster a positive committee culture. The 
 member praised the growth and development of the committee, expressed 
 pride in the members, and stated their excitement to continue working with 
 everyone in the future. 

Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 Present 
 Isabel Tanner 
 Colby Kaighin 
 Eddie Fordham 
 Melyne Cineas 
 Anne Bristol 
 Ian Rodriguez 

 Meeting was adjured at 8:19 pm.

FINANCE COMMITTEE 
 July 8, 2026 at 5:45 PM 
 Location: (Location or Zoom Link) 
 MEETING MINUTES 

 Call to Order 
 Chair Perantoni calls the meeting to order at 5:49pm EST. 

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty 
in all the ways that we can. 
 Chair Perantoni acknowledges the Land Acknowledgment. 

 Roll Call and Verification of Quorum 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the roll and verifies quorum. 
 
 Present: Perantoni, Tizon, Oria, Costello, Bollinger, Rodriguez, Hidalgo, 
 Dewey 
 
 Excused: White, Scarpone, Kaul 
 
 On Leave: Gentile 

 Public Comment 

 Opening Announcements 
 Chair Perantoni comments on the upcoming special session. Vice Chair Tizon 
 welcomes the committee to the meeting. 

 Old Business 
 Chair Perantoni acknowledges Anthony Naranjo-Abraham for the 
 Hispanic/Latin Student Union Treasurer. 
• Anthony Naranjo-Abraham - Hispanic/Latin Student Union, 
 Treasurer (Assigned to Finance, 06.17.2026) (Tabled in Finance, 
 06.24.2026) 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes Anthony Naranjo-Abraham to speak. 
 
 Candidate Anthony Naranjo-Abraham speaks on his past experiences and 
 how they relate to his application for the Hispanic/Latin Student Union. 
 Candidate yields with 3:30 seconds for his closing. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon asks if the candidate has any ideas whilst in the treasurer 
 position. 
 
 Candidate Anthony Naranjo-Abraham states his first idea is to take current 
 inventory for future events. Speaker mentions how supplies have been 
 overlooked and have been unneccesarrily purchased instead of using pre-
 existing inventory. The inventory would be made on excel spreadsheets. 
 
 Chair Perantoni asks how the candidate plans to learn and apply rules of 
 budget proviso into the HLSU. 
 
 Candidate Anthony Naranjo-Abraham states he would consult previous 
 treasurers for insight as well as administrative side to understand how new 
 system changes may be put into place. 
 
 Chair Perantoni asks about how the candidate will work with the office of 
 the treasurer. 
 
 Candidate Anthony Naranjo-Abraham states he will communicate with the 
 office of the treasurer and create relationships to help avoid mistakes for 
 the end-of-year budget presentation. 
 
 Senator Dewey asks if the candidate has any disagreements with how the 
 previous treasurer conducted business within their position. 
 
 Candidate Anthony Naranjo-Abraham speaks highly of the previous 
 treasurer and their excel sheet organization within the HLSU, and states he 
 wants to continue improving on their current processes. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon motions to call the question. 
 
 Senator Dewey seconds. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon conducts the vote, with 7 Y, 0 N, 1 A, candidate passes. 

New Business 
 Chair Perantoni welcomes Candidate Phoebe Nguyen for Asian American 
 Student Union, Treasurer. 

• Phoebe Nguyen - Asian American Student Union, Treasurer (Assigned to 
 Finance, 07.01.2026) 
 
 ■ Candidate Phoebe Nguyen thanks the committee for the opportunity to be 
 considered for this position. Candidate Nguyen speaks about how the 
 position holds financial responsibilities and expands on her involvement 
 within the AASU. Candidate Nguyen discusses her experience shadowing 
 executive board meetings. 
 
 Candidate yields with 3:36 seconds. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon asks what ideas the candidate has for the position. 
 
 Candidate Nguyen states her goal is to match AASU funds with integrity, 
 alongside encouraging collaboration with business organizations. 
 Candidate has further elaboration. 
 
 Chair Perantoni asks the candidate about following budget proviso. 
 
 Candidate Nguyen replies regarding the previous question. 
 
 Chair Perantoni asks a follow up question. 
 
 Candidate Nguyen replies. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon motions to call the question. 
 
 Senator Bollinger seconds 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the question 
 
 Candidate Nguyen closes speaking about AASU's mission and thanks the 
 committee for their time. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the question, 6 Y, 0 N, 1 A, candidate passes. 
• Thomas Bruce - Pride Student Union, Treasurer (Assigned to Finance, 
 07.01.2026) 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes candidate Thomas Bruce for the Pride Student 
 Union, Treasurer. 
 
 Candidate Thomas Bruce opens and explains that this vote will be for a 
 reappointment. He is a rising senior in physics and philosophy. Candidate 
 Bruce states his past experience in improving quality of life, training, and 
 the creation of systems and documents that treasurers across other 
 agencies have used. Candidate discusses how he has worked closely with 
 the finance committee and the previous finance committee chair. The 
 candidate closes with 3:13 seconds. 
 
 Senator Bollinger asks the candidate to elaborate on an event managed 
 with their PSU's budget. 
 
 Candidate Thomas Bruce discusses how the budget affects their keystone 
 events, towards the end of the year. The candidate mentions the "prom-
 like" experience they hosted, which was successful this previous year, 
 alongside a lavender graduation ceremony with keynote speakers. The 
 candidate also mentions success in bringing in support and performers for 
 events, alongside partnering with the center for health and wellness. 
 Candidate Bruce discusses a successful sexual health pantry that provides 
 resources to students. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon asks what ideas the candidate has for the upcoming year 
 in this position. 
 
 Candidate Thomas Bruce explains how he has experienced hardships this 
 past year in his position, and how the systems and documents he has 
 created for managing the PSU budget have become self-sufficient. 
 Candidate states a main issue he faced was lack of communication with 
 past treasurers, and states he would like to make the systems easily 
 accessible for future treasurers. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon motions to call the question. 
 
 Senator Oria seconds. 
 
 Candidate Thomas Bruce thanks the committee in his closing, and states if 
 appointed he will continue to work closely with this committee and help 
 students approach financial systems within SGA. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the vote, the candidate passes with 7 Y, 0 N, 1 A. 
• Constitutional Amendment #78-003 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes sponsor Gurtis. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis explains the constitutional amendment, which removes 
 grammatical errors in the constitution, updates "elected positions" into non-
 elected categories, alongside other changes. Sponsor Gurtis further 
 discusses this amendment. Sponsor yields with 3:09 seconds for closing. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon motions to call the question. 
 
 Senator Costello seconds. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis yields the time for closing. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the vote, amendment passes with 7 Y, 0 N, 1 A. 
• Bill #78-028 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni welcomes Sponsor Gurtis for Bill #78-028. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis discusses a transfer bill of $3,050 to ThinkTwice Inc, for 
 production of drink testing strips for students. Sponsor Gurtis states they 
 have given a discount and provide the SGA logo without any additional 
 charge. Sponsor yields. 
 
 Senator Costello asks what the plan for distribution of the testing strips is. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis states we will not see the strips on campus until roughly 
 September, but when they are received they will be tested within SGA first, 
 and then focus on different locations around Tallahassee. Sponsor Gurtis 
 states this test run will take 2–3 weeks to hear feedback. Sponsor Gurtis 
 states the strips will prioritize the Greek community, with an initial order of 
 1100 testing strips. 
 
 Senator Bollinger asks if there will be distribution to night-life businesses 
 like bars. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis states their main priority is to give them to students, keeping 
 distribution on campus first. Sponsor Gurtis elaborates on the post-roofie 
 resources FSU provides as well. 
 
 Senator Oria asks if this is only a test-run or will be a long-term 
 implementation. 
 
 Sponsor Gurtis states the test strips will hopefully last until the end of the 
 semester, and if it is successful, then it will be kept as a budget line item. 
 Sponsor Gurtis emphasizes the student feedback of the test strips. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon motions to call the question. 
 
 Senator Costello seconds. 
 
 Sponsor thanks the committee and yields with 3:35 seconds. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the question, the bill passes with 7 Y, 0 N, 1 A. 
• Bill #78-029 
 
 ■ Sponsor Tizon discusses the bill and yields with 4:16 seconds. 
 
 Senator Bollinger motions to call the question 
 
 Senator Dewey Seconds. 
 
 Sponsor Tizon yields his time. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the question, the bill passes with 7 Y, 0 N, 1 A. 
• Bill #78-026 
 
 ■ Chair Perantoni speaks down to speak as sponsor of this bill, Vice Chair 
 Tizon becomes acting chair. 
 
 Acting chair Tizon welcomes sponsor Perantoni and grants him a 5-minute 
 opening. 
 
 Sponsor Perantoni discusses this bill that removes the cap on expenses of 
 travel for RSOAC. Sponsor discusses the next change regarding how 
 submissions will be presented to the RSOAC committee. Sponsor 
 Perantoni discusses further updates to RSOAC within this bill. Speaker 
 yields with 2:24 seconds for closing statements. 
 
 Senator Bollinger asks about the travel expense cap update, asking if 
 Sponsor Perantoni anticipates any issues with this update. 
 
 Sponsor Perantoni states he does not anticipate any issues, and elaborates 
 on how the updated funding cap works. 
 
 Senator Bollinger follows up regarding the expense cap for travel in bigger 
 organizations. 
 
 Sponsor Perantoni elaborates on his rebuttal regarding the expense cap. 
 
 Senator Rodriguez asks how the bill will ensure RSOAC will watch the new 
 pre-submitted videos. 
 
 Sponsor Perantoni discusses how time will be allocated in the meetings to 
 review the videos. 
 
 Senator Oria asks the sponsor for clarification if there is a budget cut from 
 5,000 to 3,000 per RSO. 
 
 Sponsor Perantoni further discusses the new budget cap. 
 
 Senator Oria motions to call the question. 
 
 Senator Dewey Seconds. 
 
 Sponsor Perantoni thanks the committee, and elaborates how there has 
 been a lot of work behind this bill to improve RSOAC's operations. Speaker 
 yields with 2:11 seconds. 
 
 Acting Chair Tizon calls the question, with 7 Y, 0 N, 1 A, the bill passes. 
 
 Acting Chair Tizon steps down as chair, Chair Perantoni resumes his 
 position. 

Closing Announcements 
 Chair Perantoni discusses a when-to-meet he will be sending out, as well as 
 offering guidance for any legislation that senators are writing. 

Final Roll Call and Adjournment 
 Senator Oria motions to adjorn. 
 
 Senator Costello seconds. 
 
 Vice Chair Tizon calls the final roll. 
 
 Present: Perantoni, Tizon, Oria, Costello, Bollinger, Rodriguez, Hidalgo, 
 Dewey 
 
 Excused: White, Scarpone, Kaul 
 
 On Leave: Gentile 

 Meeting is adjourned at 5:52PM.

 to Rules, 07.01.2026) 

Resolution Sponsored by Ellie Macalintal, Morgan Gurtis 
#78-033 This resolution expresses support for the purchase and distribution of 
 drink test kit strips as a preventative measure for students to use 
 when participating in social activities. Drink tampering remains an 
 ongoing concern for Florida State Students and directly impedes 
 students' feeling safe. Through increased discussion about high-risk 
 environments pertaining to drink spiking, students may feel more 
 prepared to make safer decisions. The purpose of the internal 
 distribution program is to evaluate implementation procedures and 
 discuss operations to ensure the program can be distributed as 
 effectively as possible to the student body. (Assigned to Student 
 Life, 07.01.2026) 

Bill #78-030 Sponsored by Ian Rodriguez 
 This bill clarifies various previously undefined parts of the Deputy 
 Supervisor of Elections role. It ensures that their terms run 
 concurrently with the Supervisor who appointed them, affirms that it 
 is the Supervisor of Elections who appoints them, and ensures that 
 they have the right to appeal if they are dismissed, as is standard for 
 appointed positions in impeachment procedure. (Assigned to 
 Judiciary, 07.01.2026) 

Bill #78-031 Sponsored by Ian Rodriguez 
 This bill amends Chapter 202 of Student Body Statutes to include 
 procedures on how to handle candidates that are up for confirmation 
 by the Student Senate that are unresponsive and absent from their 
 confirmation hearings in their applicable Committee meeting or on 
 the Student Senate floor. This bill further codifies that it is the 
 responsibility of the applicable Committee Chair(s) to inform the 
 Candidate of the date and times for their committee hearing, and to 
 work with the candidate on finding an applicable 
 schedule. (Assigned to Rules, Internal Affairs, Judiciary, 
 07.01.2026) 

 Legislation on Second Reading 
Allocation Sponsored by Riley Perantoni, James Tizon 
Resolution This resolution proposes the allocation of $1,932.47 to two RSOs 
#78-009 who requested funding from the RSOAC. (Placed on Second 
 Reading by Senate President pursuant to SBS § 816.5(d), 
 07.01.2026) 

Allocation Sponsored by Riley Perantoni 
Resolution This resolution proposes the allocation of $118.556.00 to various 
#78-008 Sports Clubs who request funds from the Sports Club Distribution 
 Council. (Assigned to Finance, 06.17.2026) (Passed Finance, 
 06.24.2026) 

Bill #78-024 Sponsored by Morgan Gurtis, Isabel Tanner 
 This bill amends Chapter 401.7 of the Student Body Statutes by 
 removing the requirement that the Student Senate President Pro 
 Tempore sign enrolled copies of legislation in a ministerial capacity. 
 Under this legislation, enrolled copies would instead require only the 
 signature of the Student Senate President before proceeding to the 
 enrollment process. (Assigned to Judiciary, 06.17.2026) (Passed 
 Judiciary, 06.24.2026) 

Bill #78-025 Sponsored by Tanner Bigenho, Morgan Gurtis 
 The legislation preserves vital institutional memory and wisdom 
 through the allowance of a second term in Senate leadership. It 
 allows the Student Senate to continue its leadership for an additional 
 year, giving choice and stability to the body. It also eliminates the 
 strict eight days prior to fall inauguration timeline for the holding of an 
 organizational session to elect Senate leadership. (Assigned to 
 Judiciary, 06.17.2026) (Passed Judiciary, 06.24.2026) 

Proclamation Sponsored by Mathias De Macedo 
#78-013 This proclamation recognizes America’s 250th anniversary on July 4, 
 2026. In honor of this historic milestone, it further recognizes 
 individuals who played a significant role in securing America’s 
 independence. Lastly, it recognizes the Institute for Governance and 
 Civics at Florida State University on their contributions to the 
 principles that honor America’s 250th anniversary. (Assigned to 
 Student Life, 06.17.2026) (Passed Student Life, 06.25.2026)

Short Title: Commemorating the 250th Anniversary of American Independence and Recognizing the 
Institute for Governance and Civics at Florida State University. 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation recognizes America’s 250th anniversary on July 4, 2026. In honor of this historic 
milestone, it further recognizes individuals who played a significant role in securing America’s 
independence. Lastly, it recognizes the Institute for Governance and Civics at Florida State University 
on their contributions to the principles that honor America’s 250th anniversary. 
 
Background Information: 
On July 4th, 2026, the United States of America will celebrate its 250th anniversary since it gained 
independence on July 4th, 1776. There were certain key figures that helped America thrive in the chase 
for independence. The figures are George Washington, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin 
Franklin, and numerous others. Also, the Institute for Governance and Civics at Florida State University 
has contributed greatly to the principles that honor America 250th anniversary. The Institute for 
Governance and Civics at Florida State University has taken significant steps to honor our nation’s 
founding principles and should therefore be recognized for its efforts. These include the establishment 
of a new degree program, the awarding of scholarships, hosting speaker events, and support for the 
First Amendment Clinic at the FSU College of Law, as well as the Founding Voices Initiative. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Director of the Institute for Governance and Civics Dr. Ryan Owens, Assistant Director of the Institute 
for Governance and Civics Lila Seagle, and the Constitutional Liberty Branch Head at the Institute for 
Governance and Civics James Strickland. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This legislation, if passed, would recognize America’s 250th anniversary. It would also recognize 
George Washington, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Franklin, and numerous others that 
were key to America gaining independence. Lastly, it would recognize the Institute for Governance and 
Civics at Florida State University for the various initiatives they have taken to honor the founding 
principles crucial to the anniversary.

Short Title: Legislative Enrollment Act 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
This bill amends Chapter 401.7 of the Student Body Statutes by removing the requirement that the 
Student Senate President Pro Tempore sign enrolled copies of legislation in a ministerial capacity. 
Under this legislation, enrolled copies would instead require only the signature of the Student Senate 
President before proceeding to the enrollment process. 
 
Background Information: 
The current language of Chapter 401.7 requires both the Senate President and Senate President Pro 
Tempore to sign enrolled legislation following Senate approval. Since both officers serve largely 
ministerial rolls in this process, requiring two Senate officer signatures can create unnecessary 
procedural redundancy within the legislative enrollment process. 
 
The amendment is intended to streamline internal Senate procedures while preserving the Senate 
President’s authority to certify legislation passed by the Student Senate. The proposed changes aim to 
improve efficiency in the enrollment process without altering the substantive review and approval 
structure for legislation. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
The Student Senate President was consulted regarding the proposed amendment and its effect. SG&A 
was consulted regarding the proposed amendment and in favor of the change. The Student Senate 
President Pro Tempore was also notified of the proposed changes. Discussion centered on the 
administrative nature of the enrollment process and whether the existing dual-signature requirement 
remains necessary to ensure proper certification of Senate-approved legislation. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
The proposed legislation would simplify the enrollment process for Student Senate legislation by 
removing redundant signature requirements for the Student Senate President Pro Tempore. This 
change is expected to improve efficiency and reduce administrative obstacles while maintaining proper 
oversight of Senate-approved legislation.

Short Title: Amending Chapter 400, Student Body Statutes, the Trusted Executive Reelection 
Measure (TERM) Act 
 
Summary of Legislation: 
The legislation preserves vital institutional memory and wisdom through the allowance of a second term 
in Senate leadership. It allows the Student Senate to continue its leadership for an additional year, 
giving choice and stability to the body. It also eliminates the strict eight days prior to fall inauguration 
timeline for the holding of an organizational session to elect Senate leadership. 
 
Background Information: 
The Florida State University Student Senate possesses one of the deepest traditions of student self-
governance in the United States, managing a multi-million dollar Activity and Service Fee budget and 
serving as the foundational voice of the student body. Within this complex legislative ecosystem, the 
roles of Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore are paramount, acting as chief fiscal 
stewards, constitutional interpreters, and institutional anchors for the Student Government Association. 
 
An analysis of FSU Senate history reveals that effective legislative leadership has frequently relied on 
multi-term service to achieve stability, navigate institutional crises, and execute long-term policy goals. 
Rather than encouraging stagnation, multi-term tenures have historically served as periods of peak 
legislative production, providing the necessary institutional memory to pass complex fiscal and 
structural reforms. 
 
During the mid-1990s, Rich Templin and Mike Van Dyke provided rare, back-to-back leadership across 
the 47th and 48th Senates. This extended tenure allowed the legislative branch to successfully defend 
student media and protect independent campus journalism during an era of intense university 
administrative restructuring and legal challenges surrounding the Florida Flambeau. 
 
Similarly, the well-traveled pipeline of serving a full term as Pro Tempore before ascending to the 
Presidency has consistently yielded tangible policy outcomes. Caroline Chance utilized her consecutive 
terms of legislative leadership across the 62nd and 63rd Senates to aggressively tackle local student 
rights issues, forming the first major student-led coalitions with the City of Tallahassee to reform 
predatory student towing practices and campus-adjacent transit safety. 

 Page 14 of 16
Multi-term leadership has proved equally vital during periods of unexpected mid-term vacancies. 
Brandon Eisaman stepped in to stabilize the 64th Senate following an abrupt resignation, and because 
he was re-elected to lead the 65th Senate, he was able to pass sweeping fiscal modernization bills that 
overhauled how the Programming Allocations Committee (PAC) and Resource Travel Allocations 
Committee (RTAC) distributed funding to hundreds of Registered Student Organizations. 
 
In recent years, this necessity for continuous, seasoned oversight was demonstrated by Joseph Cofer, 
who helped steer the legislative branch across consecutive semesters in the 75th and 76th Senates. 
This prolonged leadership stability allowed the Senate to successfully navigate massive post-pandemic 
A&S fee fluctuations, safely restoring millions of dollars in continuous operational funding to vital 
student identity agencies, bureaus, and leadership institutes without structural disruption. 
 
While history demonstrates that the Senate frequently benefits from retaining experienced leadership to 
execute these complex initiatives, unlimited terms risk consolidating institutional memory within too few 
individuals, potentially stifling democratic renewal. Currently, the Student Body Statutes do not explicitly 
define a clear ceiling for senate leadership tenure. This bill codifies FSU SGA tradition by setting a strict 
two-term limit for the offices of Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore. By capping 
leadership at two terms, this statutory reform strikes the perfect historical balance: it legitimizes the 
time-tested practice of multi-term service and proven legislative execution, while ensuring that the 
pipeline to the highest levels of the Legislative Branch remains open, dynamic, and accessible to future 
generations of Florida State University leaders. 
 
It is important finally to consider the history of constitutional and statutory definition of the office of 
Senate President and Pro Tempore has been one always of extending the ability to serve, not 
hampering it. The oldest versions of the Student Body Constitution on record document Senate 
leadership as having a yearlong term, protected from disruption as the seats of Senators serving in 
these roles would not come up for election. In 2004 an amendment would not seek to decrease the 
role, but to extend it, specifying initially elected Spring Senators needed not seek reelection as Senate 
President and Pro Tempore, for the continuity of the body. Since 1990 has Chapter 400 housed the 
organization of the Senate. In the thirty-six years the chapter has existed, and across thirty-three bills 
amending Senate organization, in only the most recent adoption of the organization session last 
October were term limits for Senate officers ever imposed. From the available constitutional and 
statutory precedent and history, there is no basis for a limit on leadership. 
 
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: 
Existing Senate leadership, and the leadership of every Standing Committee and Ad Hoc was a part of 
efforts to craft this legislation. Proponents reached out to almost every two-term Senate leader for input 
on the legislation, including Louis Dilbert (56th and 57th Senate President), Kourtney Hahn (58th and 59th 
Senate President), Brandon Eiasaman (64th and 65th Senate President), and Mike Van Dyke (47th and 
48th Senate President). The Executive Branch, including the Student Body President, were also a part 
of efforts to craft legislation. 
 
Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted, this legislation would return the Senate to the historical choice for a continuity in leadership. 
As has been the practice among some of the most impactful and successful Senates in FSU SGA’s 
history, the 79th Student Senate and forward would have the option to extend to their leadership 
another term in office based on the best qualifications a candidate could have, prior experience in the 
role. Increased flexibility in the scheduling of the organizational session would also be permitted by 

 Page 15 of 16
eliminating the eight days prior to inauguration rule, allowing for logistical planning without the threat of 
stator noncompliance due to uncontrollable circumstances in meeting planning.
