Short Title: A Resolution Allocating $1,006.42 from Senate Projects to Students for Sensible 
Drug Policy for the Distribution of Fentanyl Testing Strips

Summary of Legislation: 
This resolution allocates $1,006.42 from the Senate Projects fund to Students for Sensible 
Drug Policy (SSDP) at Florida State University. The funds will be used to purchase and 
distribute 2,000 fentanyl testing strips at Greek Life chapters and nightclubs in an effort to 
reduce the risk of accidental overdoses within the student body and the broader community.

Background Information: 
The opioid crisis has led to a significant rise in accidental overdoses due to the presence of 
fentanyl in recreational drugs. Fentanyl, a potent synthetic opioid, is often mixed into 
substances without the knowledge of the user, leading to severe health risks and fatalities. 
FSU’s SSDP is dedicated to harm reduction initiatives that educate students and provide 
resources to mitigate these dangers. By distributing fentanyl testing strips, SSDP aims to 
empower individuals to make informed choices regarding substance safety. Senate Projects 
funding will allow the organization to expand its efforts and directly contribute to student well-
being.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This Resolution would transfer $1,006.42 from Senate Projects to SSDP at FSU to purchase 
2000 fentanyl testing strips to distribute to students.

Request 1 - Fentanyl Test Strips

Why?
We distribute free fentanyl test strips to students in Tallahassee. Fentanyl test strips are a vital 
harm reduction resource on college campuses as they can identify the presence of fentanyl in 
recreational substances before a student consumes them. If having Narcan is the air bag, using 
fentanyl test strips is safe driving. Test strips are important in preventing accidental overdoses in 
the first place so that there is not a need to save someone's life with Narcan.

Short Title: Amending statutes to further clarify forms of legislation and updating requirements 
for legislative approval

Summary of Legislation: 
This bill aims to clarify the forms of legislation seen in Chapter 401, specifically resolutions, 
proclamations, and bills by streamlining language. The amended language pertains to funding 
allocations or transfers within resolutions or clarifying budget language under bills. The 
amendments to 401.5 “Enrolled Copies” edit the signatures per form of legislation, including 
proclamations, resolutions, and bills. The amendments to Chapter 402 also update the 
language regarding enrolling copies of bills and revising the veto and veto reconsideration 
process. The amendment in Chapter 803 also clarifies language regarding transfer 
requirements.

Background Information: 
With the introduction of new forms of legislation and legislative processes, a need for 
clarification of language within Chapters 401, 402, and 803 has arisen. For Chapter 401, there 
is outdated language for resolutions and bills that do not reflect how the FSU Student Senate 
currently functions. Regarding Chapter 401.5, a detailed explanation of who signs enrolled 
copies of each type of legislation is also necessary to uphold cohesiveness. The changes also 
ensure that proclamations are direct opinions of the Student Senate by having only the Senate 
President and Senate President Pro-Tempore sign them (in a ministerial capacity, which 
means that they affirm the vote of the Senate). With this, the signatures required for 
resolutions (Senate President, Senate President Pro-Tempore, and the Program Director of 
Student Governance and Advocacy) also ensure that efficiency is maintained since policy-
specific resolutions directly involve the legislative branch and/or executive branch and transfer 
resolutions directly execute a budget that is approved by the Vice President of Student Affairs. 
The amendment in Chapter 402, has been updated to state that legislation is sent and 
approved via DocuSign rather than the previous system used before SGA procedures were 
digitized. It also gives the Senate President one day before the Student Body President 
provides oral justification for a veto to send the Senate the Student Body President’s written 
reasoning for their veto. The amendment in Chapter 803 simply designates resolutions as a 
form of legislation in that SGA entities and RSOs are allocated Activity and Service Fee 
money.

The changes in section 1 clarify language that explains resolutions, proclamations, and bills. 
The changes in Section 2 solidify who signs each type of legislation. The proclamation is to be 
signed by the Senate President and Senate President Pro-Tempore. Resolutions are to be 
signed by the Senate President, Senate Pro-Tempore, and the Program Director of Student 
Governance and Advocacy. Bills are to be signed by the Senate President, Senate Pro-
Tempore, Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy, Student Body President, 
and the Vice President for Student Affairs. The changes in section 3 update the submission of 
bill language as well as veto process language. It also gives the Senate President twenty-four 
(24) hours to distribute the Student Body President’s justification for their veto before their oral 
justification on the Senate floor.

Short Title: A Resolution Advocating for Student Representation in Florida State University’s 
Post-Incident Review Process

Summary of Legislation: 
This proposed resolution urges Florida State University to include formal student 
representation—through the Executive Branch, Student Senate, and Congress of Graduate 
Students—in the University’s forthcoming post-incident review of the April 17, 2025, tragedy. It 
outlines the Student Government Association’s position that meaningful student involvement is 
critical to developing thoughtful, effective campus safety reforms.

Background Information: 
On April 17, 2025, an active shooter opened fire inside the FSU Student Union, killing two 
members of the university community and injuring six others. In the days that followed, over 
30,000 individuals signed a public petition calling for improved safety infrastructure, particularly 
locks on classroom doors. Students, faculty, and staff across campus have since expressed a 
strong desire to be heard and included in the recovery and prevention process.

This proposed resolution responds to that moment by formally requesting that student voices 
be integrated into the University's after-action review. It further affirms the Student Government 
Association’s readiness to coordinate student feedback and support a comprehensive, 
prevention-focused approach to future safety planning.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If adopted, this resolution would establish the official position of the Student Government 
Association that students must be active participants in the University’s institutional review and 
future safety initiatives. It would authorize the Student Body President to formally transmit this 
position to university leadership on behalf of the SGA.

Short Title: A Proclamation Honoring the Victims and Community Response to the April 17, 
2025, Tragedy at Florida State University

Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation, issued by the Student Senate President and the Student Senate President 
Pro Tempore on behalf of the 77th Student Senate and the Student Government Association, 
commemorates the lives lost and the individuals injured during the April 17, 2025, active 
shooter incident at Florida State University. It recognizes the profound grief and trauma 
experienced by the campus community, honors the extraordinary efforts of first responders 
and university personnel, and establishes April 17th as the "FSU Day of Reflection and 
Resilience" in remembrance and unity.

Background Information: 
On April 17, 2025, a shooting took place inside the FSU Student Union, resulting in the deaths 
of two beloved community members: Robert Morales and Tiru Chabba, and injuries to six 
others. Countless students, staff, and faculty were forced to shelter in place, unsure if they 
would be safe. The incident deeply affected thousands of members of the university family and 
has left a lasting impact on the emotional, academic, and professional lives of many.

The FSU community responded with overwhelming courage, compassion, and unity. Vigils 
were held. Class policies were adapted. Support centers were opened. And students, faculty, 
and staff alike found ways to hold one another through a time of profound difficulty.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If proclaimed, this resolution becomes the official statement of the Student Government 
Association and serves as a lasting tribute to those lost, a formal acknowledgment of those 
injured and traumatized, and a commitment to remembering April 17th each year as a day of 
resilience and shared reflection.

 2 shooter opened fire inside the Student Union, killing two members of our community and injuring six 
 3 others; and

Land Acknowledgement 
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is 
located on land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee 
Nation, the Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the 
Seminole Tribe of Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and 
extend that respect to their descendants and to all Indigenous people. We 
recognize this land remains scarred by the histories and ongoing legacies of 
settler colonial violence, dispossession, and removal. In spite of all this, and with 
tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations have remained deeply 
connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities, and to their 
cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that these 
Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and 
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to 
learn about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous 
Nations whose land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty

Short Title: Amending Chapter 207 to Require Narcan Certification for Elected Student 
Government Officials

Summary of Legislation:

This bill amends Chapter 207 of the Student Body Statutes, titled “The Student Government 
Training Act,” to mandate Narcan Certification for all elected student government officials 
within twenty (20) school days of their inauguration. It establishes oversight responsibilities for 
the Chair of the Campus Recreation Board, outlines an appeal process for extenuating 
circumstances, and details consequences for non-compliance in order to establish 
enforcement towards Narcan Certification.

Background Information:

As a response to growing concerns surrounding overdoses related incidents on college 
campuses, this legislation seeks to ensure that all elected student government officials are 
equipped with lifesaving Narcan training. Florida State University has historically held an active 
voice in addressing student health and safety, and these amendments strengthen that 
commitment by requiring Student Government leaders to be prepared for emergency situations 
involving opioid overdoses. The Center for Health Advocacy and Wellness (CHAW) currently 
offers free Narcan Certification, Narcan product, and resources in order to ensure general 
education surrounding conservations around overdoses and how to respond in a crisis 
situation. CHAW hosts weekly meetings every Wednesday and Thursday at 1PM that typically 
last 20-30 minutes long enabling students to become Narcan Certified.

Effect of Proposed Legislation:

If enacted, this bill will require all elected student government officials to complete a Narcan 
Certification Course through CHAW within twenty (20) school days of their inauguration. The 
Chair of the Campus Recreation Board will oversee compliance, maintain certification records, 
and issue reminders. Failure to comply may result in suspension from Student Government 
roles, with enforcement determined by the respective leadership of each governing body.

Short Title: Proclamation on TPS Designation for Venezuelans

Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation gives context as to the situation that Venezuelans are facing, including 
students, who are under TPS (Temporary Protected Status) currently. The removal of this 
status is explained, specifically the detrimental effects that this will have on students who are 
trying to complete their education at higher institutions like Florida State University.

Background Information: 
This is important to bring up to Senate, as a significant percentage of the Hispanic population 
on campus is Venezuelan and some are under TPS and may be unable to finish their studies 
after the status expires. This protected status has been in effect since 2021 and currently there 
are no other pathways for Venezuelans to stay in the United States legally, therefore they 
would be at risk for deportation if they wished to stay and complete their studies or work that 
they have already started.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This is just a way of making the percentage of the student body that this is referring to know 
that we are here to support them in this tumultuous time, especially as a lot of issues with 
immigration are uncertain and on pause.

Short Title: A Proclamation Condemning Hazing and Honoring the Life of Caleb Wilson

Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation condemns the practice of hazing, specifically highlighting the tragic death of 
Caleb Wilson, a student at Southern University, who died due to hazing. The proclamation 
calls for stronger preventative measures, urges the University Administration to take action, 
and emphasizes the responsibility of student organizations to prevent harm in the name of 
tradition.

Background Information: 

Caleb Wilson, a 20-year-old student at Southern University, tragically lost his life due to 
fraternity hazing. Hazing continues to be a dangerous and unlawful practice that has led to the 
loss of many students’ lives across the nation. The proclamation aims to condemn hazing, 
honor Caleb Wilson’s life, and encourage stronger actions to prevent further tragedies. This 
issue has a significant impact on the broader university community and student organizations, 
including fraternities and sororities, who must address these harmful practices.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 

If enacted, this proclamation will officially condemn the actions that led to Caleb Wilson’s death 
and encourage the University Administration to strengthen anti-hazing policies and educational 
efforts. It will also promote a culture of accountability within student organizations to ensure 
safety, transparency, and respect among students, preventing further hazing incidents.

Short Title: A Proclamation Supporting the Expansion of Brightline to North Florida and 
Advocating for a Financial Agreement to Benefit Students. 

Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation expresses support for the expansion of Brightline to North Florida, including 
Tallahassee, Tampa, Jacksonville, and Gainesville, to improve transportation access for 
students at Florida State University (FSU) and other institutions in the region. It highlights the 
financial burdens many students face due to limited transit options and urges university 
leadership and state officials to advocate for a student financial assistance program for 
Brightline travel. The expansion and implementation of affordable student rates would enhance 
accessibility, sustainability, and academic and professional opportunities for students.

Background Information: 
Affordable and reliable transportation is a critical issue for students, particularly those from 
minority and lower-income backgrounds. North Florida lacks strong public transit connections 
to major metropolitan areas such as Orlando, Tampa, and Miami, making travel costly and 
inefficient for students without personal vehicles. Expanding Brightline and establishing a 
financial assistance program would significantly improve mobility, increase access to job and 
internship opportunities, and foster collaboration between Florida's universities.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This proclamation calls for formal advocacy efforts from FSU leadership and state officials to 
ensure students benefit from expanded Brightline services. It also requests semesterly 
updates from relevant stakeholders, including Brightline leadership, the Florida Department of 
Transportation, and FSU Administration. Additionally, copies of this proclamation will be sent to 
university presidents, student government leaders, and key local and state officials to garner 
widespread support.

Short Title: Supporting Full Coverage of LSAT, GRE, MCAT, and Bar Exam Fees for Pell 
Grant and Need-Based Aid Students at Florida State University. 

Summary of Legislation: This legislation advocates for Florida State University to fully cover 
the costs of the LSAT, GRE, MCAT, and Bar Exam for students receiving Pell Grants or other 
need-based aid. These exams serve as critical gateways to graduate and professional 
education but often present significant financial barriers for low-income students. By 
eliminating these costs, FSU can promote equitable access to higher education, ensure 
students are not deterred from pursuing advanced degrees due to financial constraints, and 
reinforce its commitment to student success and upward mobility.

Background Information: Students receiving Pell Grants or other need-based aid often face 
financial challenges that extend beyond tuition, including costs associated with graduate and 
professional school entrance exams. While some fee waivers exist, they do not cover all 
associated expenses, such as study materials and multiple test attempts. By ensuring full 
coverage of these exam fees, FSU can support equitable access to postgraduate opportunities 
for all students, regardless of financial background. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: This proclamation calls for FSU to fully cover the costs of the 
LSAT, GRE, MCAT, and Bar Exam for students receiving Pell Grants or other need-based aid. 
It urges the university administration to establish a funding mechanism for this initiative and 
requests updates from relevant offices, including the Office of Financial Aid and the Student 
Government Association. Additionally, copies of this proclamation will be sent to FSU 
leadership, the Florida Board of Governors, and other relevant stakeholders to advocate for 
broader institutional and state-level support.

Summary of Legislation: This resolution urges the Student Government Association (SGA) to 
collaborate with the administration in researching the feasibility of renovating Moore Auditorium 
to support student-led events. It emphasizes the need for upgrades to ensure the space meets 
the diverse needs of the student body and enhances the overall experience for performances, 
discussions, and cultural expressions.

Background Information: Moore Auditorium serves as a central venue for student-led events, 
including cultural showcases, performances, and political or spiritual gatherings, contributing to 
a dynamic campus life. Over time, the auditorium has experienced aging infrastructure, limiting 
its ability to fully support high-caliber events. Many student organizations, from cultural groups 
to performing arts organizations, depend on Moore Auditorium to host events that foster 
inclusivity and dialogue. The university has long valued artistic and cultural engagement, 
making it important to invest in the renovation of Moore Auditorium to maintain its role as a key 
space for student expression. 

Effect of Proposed Legislation: If enacted, this legislation would prompt SGA to collaborate 
with the administration on researching the renovation of Moore Auditorium. The goal is to 
ensure that the necessary upgrades—such as improved accessibility, seating, lighting, and 
technology—are made, and that the needs of student organizations are addressed. This will 
enhance the auditorium’s capacity to host diverse events and support the university’s mission 
of fostering student involvement and cultural engagement.

Short Title: Proclamation honoring the late State Senator Geraldine Thompson

Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation recognizes the impactful contributions of State Senator Geraldine 
Thompson to Florida’s political and social landscape. Her dedication to public service, 
education, and civil rights left an enduring legacy. Her tireless advocacy for marginalized 
communities and commitment to justice and equality have shaped the lives of many Floridians 
and specifies the voting thresholds required for passage of each type of legislation.

Background Information: 
State Senator Geraldine Thompson dedicated her career to advancing civil rights, improving 
educational opportunities, and championing social justice. A trailblazer in Florida politics, she 
was the first African American woman elected to represent District 12 in the Florida House of 
Representatives. Senator Thompson was instrumental in preserving African American history 
through her efforts with the Wells’ Built Museum of African American History and Culture. Her 
passion for equity and education reform made her a respected leader across party lines. Her 
passing marks the loss of a true champion for justice, equity, and the betterment of her 
community.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
If enacted by the Student Senate, this proclamation would honor the values of leadership, 
integrity, and dedication exemplified by Senator Thompson. It would acknowledge her 
contributions to the state of Florida and serve as an inspiration for future leaders to continue 
her legacy of service and advocacy.

Short Title: This proclamation condemns the measures of Florida SB 2-C, which overlook 
students in the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program who reside in Florida 
by unfairly revoking them of in-state tuition.

Summary of Legislation: 
This proclamation addresses the recent passage of SB 2-C into Florida law and its mandatory 
measures that demand undocumented students pay out-of-state tuition in Florida post-
secondary education institutions. This action blankets over students under the Deferred Action 
for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program, otherwise known as “Dreamers,” in Florida, despite 
them being brought to this country under circumstances beyond their control when they were 
very young, along with growing up in Florida and having attended secondary school and high 
school in Florida. Furthermore, this proclamation shows our Senate’s disapproval of our 
legislature’s actions and urges that our university acknowledges this unfounded discriminatory 
anti-immigration bill and provides resources to Dreamers that reside in our university to ease 
the monetary and stigmatizing burden SB 2-C will evoke come July 1, 2025.

Background Information: 
On February 13, 2025, SB 2-C and other anti-immigration bills were signed into law by 
Governor Ron Desantis after being passed through Florida’s legislature. This bill includes 
measures that revoke in-state tuition from undocumented students who reside in Florida. 
However, under these terms, students within the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals 
(DACA) program are included due to them being considered as “undocumented immigrants.” 
This bill includes them despite most having grown up in the states, having completed their 
secondary education in Florida, and being required to complete their high school education to 
even be eligible for DACA. 

In June of 2012, the DACA program was established by the Obama Administration to ensure 
the protection of children who were brought to the U.S when they were young from removal 
processes and enabling them work authorization. DACA was brought in order to protect youths 
who were brought into this country under circumstances beyond their control and support them 
accordingly.

 Page 61 of 111In 2014, HB 851 was signed into law by former Governor Rick Scott that allowed Dreamers to 
pay in-state tuition rates in post-secondary education institutions within Florida if they met 
certain criterion under F.S 1009.26. This is now dismissed under SB 2-C, denying Dreamers of 
in-state tuition and forcing them along with other “undocumented” students to pay out-of-state 
tuition starting July 1, 2025. 

This bill pressures Dreamers with an outstanding economic burden, along with further 
stigmatizing them and their legal status despite previous protections being installed within the 
U.S and Florida state government that show empathy and discretion to their situation. Due to 
the lack of permanency of DACA, as it was temporary solution to resolve struggles of 
Dreamers, it is seen nationally how state legislatures are choosing to strip Dreamers of their 
liberties and resources to pursue their aspirations that they rightfully deserve and have earned. 
Florida is following suit, as this bill dehumanizes Dreamers, overlooking the countless 
distributions to their country they provide through economic means, as Dreamers and eligible 
DACA individuals have provided roughly $304 million in federal and state taxes in 2021 
according to the American Immigration Council.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
The university and student senate will acknowledge how SB 2-C targets it’s students under 
DACA and the university will take onto itself the action of seeking and providing Dreamers with 
resources to help them continue their post-secondary education in Florida State University.

Short Title: Amending Chapter 400 to replace committee Chair and Vice Chair elections with 
Senate President appointments as the default in the case of a vacancy.

Summary of Legislation: 
This bill would amend Chapter 400, Student Body Statutes, to allow the Senate President to 
appoint standing committee Chairs and Vice Chairs after committee allocations. It establishes 
a chain of command that ensures elections are still an alternative in some scenarios. This bill 
also changes a couple standards for what constitutes a sufficient majority for various voting 
situations.

Background Information: 
This bill is being proposed to help alleviate the duties of the Senate President and President 
Pro Tempore by increasing the likelihood of having the most qualified Senators fill Chair and 
Vice Chair positions. There has been some concern that the elections of these positions have 
led to the most popular Senator fulfilling the Chair position rather than the most qualified 
Senator. Considering this, it also highlights the Senate President as a trusted individual who is 
capable of leaving their personal bias out of appointing committee leadership and choosing 
who they genuinely believe is the best fit for the role. If a Senate President violates this trust, 
any Senator has the option to make a motion of no-confidence according to Senate Rules of 
Procedure Rule 1.8. Finally, to put a check on this proposed change, the removal of a Chair or 
Vice Chair would now require a lesser majority.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This bill would effectively remove elections as the default when determining the Chair and Vice 
Chair of standing committees, leaving appointments up to the Senate President if they choose 
to do so.

Short Title: Consent Resolution for the allocation $2779.80 to be allocated amongst various
RSOs.

Summary of Legislation: 
This consent resolution proposes the allocation of $2779.80 to be distributed among various
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) on campus to support their programming needs for
this semester. This funding will be essential in enhancing the student experience by providing
financial support for events, activities, and initiatives organized by the RSOs. With these funds,
the organizations will be able to host a variety of programs, including cultural, educational,
social, and community-building events, all of which contribute to a lively and engaging campus
environment. This allocation ensures that RSOs have the resources necessary to engage
students, foster a sense of community, and enrich campus life. By supporting these
organizations, we are investing in student leadership, creativity, and the creation of diverse,
inclusive programming that benefits the entire student body.

Background Information: 
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming that aligns with the values of inclusivity and community-
building at FSU.

Effect of Proposed Legislation: 
This resolution will provide vital financial support to the RSOs, empowering them to carry out
transformative activities that drive cultural engagement and professional growth. These funding
requests are not just investments in individual organizations, but in the future of the FSU
community, advancing inclusivity, fostering leadership, and creating invaluable career
opportunities for students.
